import {buildNotificationFaviconSvg, buildStatusFaviconSvg, resetActionFavicon, syncActionRunFavicon, syncNotificationFaviconDot} from './favicon-status.ts';

test('buildStatusFaviconSvg uses action status icons', () => {
  const success = buildStatusFaviconSvg('success');
  expect(success).toContain('viewBox="0 0 640 640"');
  expect(success).toContain('fill:#609926');
  expect(success).toContain('data-actions-status-name="success"');

  const running = buildStatusFaviconSvg('running');
  expect(running).toContain('data-actions-status-name="running"');

  const failure = buildStatusFaviconSvg('failure');
  expect(failure).toContain('data-actions-status-name="failure"');
});

test('syncActionRunFavicon updates favicon links', () => {
  document.head.innerHTML = `
    <link rel="icon" href="/assets/img/favicon.svg" type="image/svg+xml">
    <link rel="alternate icon" href="/assets/img/favicon.png" type="image/png">
  `;
  const links = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll<HTMLLinkElement>('link[rel~="icon"]'));
  syncActionRunFavicon('running');
  for (const link of links) {
    expect(link.href).toMatch(/^data:image\/svg\+xml,/);
    expect(decodeURIComponent(link.href)).toContain('data-actions-status-name="running"');
  }
  resetActionFavicon();
  expect(links[0].href).toContain('favicon.svg');
});

// the module remembers the page's links once, as on a real page, so keep the links an earlier test created
function setupFaviconLinks() {
  if (!document.querySelector('link[rel~="icon"]')) {
    document.head.innerHTML = `
      <link rel="icon" href="/assets/img/favicon.svg" type="image/svg+xml">
      <link rel="alternate icon" href="/assets/img/favicon.png" type="image/png">
    `;
  }
  return Array.from(document.querySelectorAll<HTMLLinkElement>('link[rel~="icon"]'));
}

const showsDot = (link: HTMLLinkElement) => decodeURIComponent(link.href).includes('data-notification-dot');
const showsRunStatus = (link: HTMLLinkElement) => decodeURIComponent(link.href).includes('data-actions-status-name=');

describe('notification dot on the tab icon', {concurrent: false}, () => {
  afterEach(() => {
    resetActionFavicon();
    syncNotificationFaviconDot(false);
  });

  test('the dot uses the primary color, like the navbar unread count', () => {
    document.documentElement.style.setProperty('--color-primary', '#123456');
    expect(buildNotificationFaviconSvg()).toContain('fill="#123456"');
    document.documentElement.style.removeProperty('--color-primary');
  });

  test('AC1 unread notifications add a dot and reading them all restores the default icon', () => {
    const links = setupFaviconLinks();
    syncNotificationFaviconDot(true);
    for (const link of links) expect(showsDot(link)).toBe(true);
    syncNotificationFaviconDot(false);
    expect(links[0].href).toContain('favicon.svg');
    expect(links[1].href).toContain('favicon.png');
  });

  test('AC2 an Actions run status wins over the dot, and the dot returns when the run page is left', () => {
    const links = setupFaviconLinks();
    syncNotificationFaviconDot(true);
    syncActionRunFavicon('running');
    expect(showsRunStatus(links[0])).toBe(true);
    expect(showsDot(links[0])).toBe(false);
    syncNotificationFaviconDot(true); // a count update while on the run page must not take the icon back
    expect(showsRunStatus(links[0])).toBe(true);
    resetActionFavicon();
    expect(showsDot(links[0])).toBe(true);
  });

  test('AC2 leaving a run page with nothing unread restores the default icon', () => {
    const links = setupFaviconLinks();
    syncActionRunFavicon('success');
    resetActionFavicon();
    expect(links[0].href).toContain('favicon.svg');
  });
});

import {getActionStatusIcon} from './action-status-icon.ts';
import type {ActionsStatus} from './gitea-actions.ts';
import {svgParseOuterInner} from '../svg.ts';
import {html, htmlRaw} from '../utils/html.ts';

const {svgOuter, svgInnerHtml: giteaFaviconInner} = svgParseOuterInner('gitea-favicon');
const faviconViewBox = svgOuter.getAttribute('viewBox')!;
const [, , faviconViewBoxWidth, faviconViewBoxHeight] = faviconViewBox.split(/\s+/).map(Number);

// the status badge is rendered in the bottom-right corner, following GitHub Actions favicon proportions
const badgeIconSize = 16;
const badgeSizeRatio = 340 / 640;
const badgeMargin = 6;
const badgeDrawSize = faviconViewBoxWidth * badgeSizeRatio;
const badgeX = faviconViewBoxWidth - badgeDrawSize - badgeMargin;
const badgeY = faviconViewBoxHeight - badgeDrawSize - badgeMargin;
const badgeScale = badgeDrawSize / badgeIconSize;
// white ring behind the badge so it stands out from the logo, like GitHub's favicon
const badgeCenter = badgeDrawSize / 2;
const badgeRingRadius = badgeCenter + badgeDrawSize * 0.08;

// two badges compete for the icon: an Actions run's status wins over the unread notification dot
let actionStatus: ActionsStatus | null = null;
let notificationDot = false;
let notificationDotDataUrl: string | null = null;
const defaultFaviconHrefs = new Map<HTMLLinkElement, string>();
const faviconDataUrlCache = new Map<ActionsStatus, string>();
let colorProbe: HTMLElement | null = null;

function rememberDefaultFaviconHrefs() {
  if (defaultFaviconHrefs.size > 0) return;
  for (const link of document.querySelectorAll<HTMLLinkElement>('link[rel~="icon"]')) {
    defaultFaviconHrefs.set(link, link.href);
  }
}

function resolveTailwindTextColor(colorClass: string): string {
  if (!colorProbe) {
    colorProbe = document.createElement('span');
    colorProbe.style.display = 'none';
    document.body.append(colorProbe);
  }
  colorProbe.className = colorClass;
  return getComputedStyle(colorProbe).color || '#000000';
}

function buildStatusIconMarkup(status: ActionsStatus): string {
  const {name, colorClass} = getActionStatusIcon(status, 'circle-fill');
  const color = resolveTailwindTextColor(colorClass);
  const {svgInnerHtml} = svgParseOuterInner(name);
  const coloredInner = svgInnerHtml.replaceAll('currentColor', color);
  const ring = html`<circle cx="${badgeX + badgeCenter}" cy="${badgeY + badgeCenter}" r="${badgeRingRadius}" fill="#ffffff"/>`;
  const badge = html`<g data-actions-status-name="${status}" transform="translate(${badgeX}, ${badgeY}) scale(${badgeScale})" fill="${color}" color="${color}">${htmlRaw(coloredInner)}</g>`;
  return html`${htmlRaw(ring)}${htmlRaw(badge)}`;
}

export function buildStatusFaviconSvg(status: ActionsStatus): string {
  return html`<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="${faviconViewBox}">${htmlRaw(giteaFaviconInner)}${htmlRaw(buildStatusIconMarkup(status))}</svg>`;
}

function buildStatusFaviconDataUrl(status: ActionsStatus): string {
  const cached = faviconDataUrlCache.get(status);
  if (cached) return cached;
  const dataUrl = `data:image/svg+xml,${encodeURIComponent(buildStatusFaviconSvg(status))}`;
  faviconDataUrlCache.set(status, dataUrl);
  return dataUrl;
}

function setFaviconHref(href: string) {
  rememberDefaultFaviconHrefs();
  for (const link of defaultFaviconHrefs.keys()) {
    if (link.isConnected) link.href = href;
  }
}

export function buildNotificationFaviconSvg(): string {
  // same color as the navbar's unread count bubble
  const color = getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue('--color-primary').trim() || '#4183c4';
  const cx = badgeX + badgeCenter;
  const cy = badgeY + badgeCenter;
  const ring = html`<circle cx="${cx}" cy="${cy}" r="${badgeRingRadius}" fill="#ffffff"/>`;
  const dot = html`<circle data-notification-dot="" cx="${cx}" cy="${cy}" r="${badgeCenter}" fill="${color}"/>`;
  return html`<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="${faviconViewBox}">${htmlRaw(giteaFaviconInner)}${htmlRaw(ring)}${htmlRaw(dot)}</svg>`;
}

function buildNotificationFaviconDataUrl(): string {
  notificationDotDataUrl ??= `data:image/svg+xml,${encodeURIComponent(buildNotificationFaviconSvg())}`;
  return notificationDotDataUrl;
}

function restoreDefaultFavicon() {
  rememberDefaultFaviconHrefs();
  for (const [link, href] of defaultFaviconHrefs) {
    if (link.isConnected) link.href = href;
  }
}

function renderFavicon() {
  if (actionStatus) {
    setFaviconHref(buildStatusFaviconDataUrl(actionStatus));
  } else if (notificationDot) {
    setFaviconHref(buildNotificationFaviconDataUrl());
  } else {
    restoreDefaultFavicon();
  }
}

export function syncActionRunFavicon(status: ActionsStatus | ''): void {
  if (status === '') {
    resetActionFavicon();
    return;
  }
  if (status === actionStatus) return;
  actionStatus = status;
  renderFavicon();
}

export function resetActionFavicon(): void {
  if (actionStatus === null) return;
  actionStatus = null;
  renderFavicon();
}

export function syncNotificationFaviconDot(show: boolean): void {
  if (show === notificationDot) return;
  notificationDot = show;
  renderFavicon();
}

function select(start: Node, startOffset: number, end: Node, endOffset: number) {
  const range = document.createRange();
  range.setStart(start, startOffset);
  range.setEnd(end, endOffset);
  const selection = window.getSelection()!;
  selection.removeAllRanges();
  selection.addRange(range);
  return selection;
}

function text(root: HTMLElement, selector: string) {
  return root.querySelector(selector)!.firstChild!;
}

test('selectedCommentMarkup', () => {
  const root = createElementFromHTML<HTMLElement>(timeline);
  document.body.append(root);
  const first = root.querySelector('#first .markup');

  expect(selectedCommentMarkup(select(text(root, '#first p'), 0, text(root, '#first p'), 5))).toBe(first);
  expect(selectedCommentMarkup(select(text(root, '#first p'), 0, text(root, '#first p:last-child'), 6))).toBe(first); // across paragraphs
  expect(selectedCommentMarkup(select(text(root, '#first p'), 2, text(root, '#first p'), 2))).toBeNull(); // collapsed
  expect(selectedCommentMarkup(select(text(root, '#first p'), 0, text(root, '#second p'), 5))).toBeNull(); // two comments
  expect(selectedCommentMarkup(select(text(root, '#outside'), 0, text(root, '#outside'), 7))).toBeNull();
  expect(selectedCommentMarkup(select(text(root, '#dismissed p'), 0, text(root, '#dismissed p'), 9))).toBeNull(); // no raw content to quote
  window.getSelection()!.removeAllRanges();
  expect(selectedCommentMarkup(window.getSelection())).toBeNull();
  root.remove();
});

function elemFromKbd(kbd: HTMLElement): HTMLInputElement | HTMLTextAreaElement | null {
  return shortcutWrapper(kbd)?.querySelector<HTMLInputElement>('input, textarea') || null;
}

function kbdFromElem(input: HTMLElement): HTMLElement | null {
  return shortcutWrapper(input)?.querySelector<HTMLElement>('kbd') || null;
}

export function initGlobalShortcut() {
  registerGlobalInitFunc('onGlobalShortcut', initShortcutKbd);
  registerGlobalInitFunc('onShortcutLink', initShortcutLink);
  registerGlobalInitFunc('onShortcutHelp', initShortcutHelp);
  document.addEventListener('keydown', (e: KeyboardEvent) => globalRegistry.handleKeyDown(e));

  // A <kbd> element next to an <input> declares a keyboard shortcut for that input.
  // initShortcutKbd registers it, so pressing the matching key focuses the sibling input.
  // When Escape is pressed inside such an input, the input is cleared and blurred.
  // The <kbd> element is shown/hidden automatically based on input focus and value.
  document.addEventListener('keydown', (e: KeyboardEvent) => {
    // Ctrl/Alt/Cmd+Escape is left alone
    if (e.ctrlKey || e.metaKey || e.altKey) return;

    const target = e.target as HTMLElement;

    // Handle Escape: clear and blur inputs that have an associated keyboard shortcut
    if (e.key === 'Escape') {
      const kbd = kbdFromElem(target);
      if (kbd) {
        (target as HTMLInputElement).value = '';
        (target as HTMLInputElement).blur();
      }

import {initNotificationCount} from './notification.ts';
import {GET} from '../modules/fetch.ts';
import {localUserSettings} from '../modules/user-settings.ts';

vi.mock('../modules/fetch.ts', () => ({
  GET: vi.fn(),
}));

class FakeNotification {
  static permission: NotificationPermission = 'granted';
  static shown: string[] = [];
  constructor(_title: string, options: NotificationOptions) {
    FakeNotification.shown.push(options.body!);
  }
  addEventListener() {}
}

const pollEvery = 1000;

// /notifications/new answers with these unread counts, one per poll
function serveCounts(...counts: number[]) {
  for (const count of counts) {
    vi.mocked(GET).mockResolvedValueOnce({ok: true, json: () => Promise.resolve({new: count})} as Response);
  }
}

function setVisibility(state: DocumentVisibilityState) {
  vi.spyOn(document, 'visibilityState', 'get').mockReturnValue(state);
}

const countText = () => document.querySelector('.notification_count')!.textContent;

// the polling fallback, used when the shared worker or the event stream is unavailable
describe('notification count poller', {concurrent: false}, () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    vi.useFakeTimers();
    document.documentElement.lang = 'en-US'; // trN resolves plural rules from the document language
    document.body.innerHTML = `
      <span class="notification_count" data-desktop-alert-title="Gitea" data-desktop-alert-1="You have %d new notification" data-desktop-alert-n="You have %d new notifications">0</span>`;
    vi.stubGlobal('localStorage', new Storage()); // Node's own localStorage global hides happy-dom's
    FakeNotification.shown = [];
    vi.stubGlobal('Notification', FakeNotification);
    localUserSettings.setBoolean('notification-desktop-alerts', true);
    // EventSourceUpdateTime stays 0, so initNotificationCount takes the poller path
    Object.assign(window.config.notificationSettings, {MinTimeout: pollEvery, TimeoutStep: pollEvery, MaxTimeout: pollEvery});
  });
  afterEach(() => {
    vi.clearAllTimers();
    vi.useRealTimers();
    vi.restoreAllMocks();
    vi.mocked(GET).mockReset();
    vi.unstubAllGlobals();
    Object.assign(window.config.notificationSettings, {MinTimeout: 0, TimeoutStep: 0, MaxTimeout: 0});
    document.body.replaceChildren();
  });

  test('AC5 a hidden tab alerts with the number of new notifications since its last poll', async () => {
    setVisibility('hidden');
    serveCounts(2, 3);
    initNotificationCount();
    await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(pollEvery);
    expect(countText()).toBe('2');
    await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(pollEvery);
    expect(countText()).toBe('3');
    expect(FakeNotification.shown).toEqual(['You have 2 new notifications', 'You have 1 new notification']);
  });

  test('AC7 a visible tab does not alert, and a lower count does not alert', async () => {
    setVisibility('visible');
    serveCounts(2);
    initNotificationCount();
    await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(pollEvery);
    expect(countText()).toBe('2');
    setVisibility('hidden');
    serveCounts(1);
    await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(pollEvery);
    expect(countText()).toBe('1');
    expect(FakeNotification.shown).toEqual([]);
  });

  test('polling keeps going when the browser refuses to show the alert', async () => {
    // Android Chrome exposes Notification but its constructor throws "Illegal constructor"
    vi.stubGlobal('Notification', class {
      static permission = 'granted';
      constructor() {
        throw new TypeError('Illegal constructor');
      }
    });
    vi.spyOn(console, 'error').mockImplementation(() => {});
    setVisibility('hidden');
    serveCounts(1, 2);
    initNotificationCount();
    await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(pollEvery);
    expect(countText()).toBe('1');
    await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(pollEvery);
    expect(countText()).toBe('2');
    expect(GET).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);
  });
});

---
name: gitea-wsync-test-workflow
description: Edit code in this Windows Gitea folder; run tests/lint/build in WSL Debian ~/gitea via `wsync <cmd>` from Git Bash
metadata:
  type: project
---

Carson's setup (2026-09-14): **all code edits happen in this Windows `Gitea` folder** (logged
SpecStory sessions launch here). WSL Debian `~/gitea` is a **test runner only** — never edit there.
Native Windows test runs produce Windows-only failures, and lint is ~20x slower, so don't trust them.

**Run tests/lint/build with `wsync` from the Bash tool (Git Bash):**
```bash
wsync pnpm exec vitest run web_src/js/features/common-page.test.ts
wsync go test -run '^TestName$' ./routers/web/misc/
wsync make lint-js
wsync make build
wsync            # sync only
```
`C:\Users\carso\bin\wsync` reads the branch checked out here, warns if tracked files are
uncommitted (only COMMITTED work reaches WSL — commit first, ask Carson before committing), then
runs WSL `~/bin/wsync-wsl <branch> [cmd]`: fetches remote `win` (this folder over /mnt/c;
push disabled), force-switches `~/gitea` to that branch, runs the command with Go 1.26.4/Node PATH.

Gotchas: don't run `git status` on `/mnt/c` from WSL (hangs); WSL can't run `.exe`s; use
`wsl -d Debian --exec bash -c '...' name args` (plain `wsl -- bash -c` drops args).
To try the app: `~/gitea/custom/conf/app.ini` serves Gitea on http://localhost:3001 (SQLite) —
run `wsl -d Debian --exec bash -c 'cd ~/gitea && ./gitea web'` in the background after `wsync make build`.
Baseline rule: some backend tests fail on `main` too — compare branch vs `main`, not vs zero.

## Why PR #161 can't merge

**What actually blocks the merge button is the missing review, not CI.** The `main` ruleset only requires **1 approving review** and **all review threads resolved**. It has no required status checks. The one review thread (gitar-bot's Android Chrome bug) is resolved, but nobody has approved yet (`REVIEW_REQUIRED`). The course rule still says a PR merges only once "CI passes", though, so CI has to go green before anyone should approve.

**The CI failures all have one cause.** `vitest.config.ts` sets `isolate: false`, so test files that run in the same worker share modules and the same `document`. Which files end up together changes from run to run, so failures look random:

1. **`frontend` job: `favicon-status.test.ts:28` (caused by this PR).** `notification.test.ts` ends with an unread count above 0, which leaves `notificationDot = true` inside `favicon-status.ts`. Its cleanup never resets that. When the favicon test runs next, `resetActionFavicon()` puts the dot back instead of the default icon.
2. **`sonarqube` job: `repo-issue-edit.test.ts` (already broken on `main`, not caused by this PR).** That file and `shortcut.test.ts` both call `initGlobalShortcut()`. Each call adds another keydown listener to the shared `document`, so every key press runs twice. I reproduced it with just those two files, and it fails in either order. Those tests came from #95 and #60. This PR only adds new test files, which changed how files get grouped into workers.
3. **SonarCloud gate: a side effect of #2.** The quality gate failed on `new_coverage 0.0 < 80`. Because vitest failed, no `coverage/lcov.info` was written, so Sonar counted every new line as uncovered. I ran the same coverage locally and worked it out the way Sonar does: the PR's new code is at about **82.8%** with lines and branches combined. That should pass, but only just. The gaps are the SharedWorker path: the new lines in `eventsource.sharedworker.ts` and `worker.ts` aren't covered at all, and 7 of the 10 new lines in `notification.ts` aren't either. One more test there would give some room.

## Fix so far (not committed)

- `web_src/js/features/notification.test.ts`: `afterEach` now calls `syncNotificationFaviconDot(false)` so the test stops leaving the dot behind.
- `web_src/js/modules/favicon-status.test.ts`: a file-level `beforeEach` resets both badges, so a file that ran earlier can't break these tests again.

I checked it with those two files forced into one worker. Before the fix, `favicon-status.test.ts` fails; with it, all 9 tests pass. That was a native Windows run, since `wsync` only sees committed work. I'll run the full suite in WSL after you approve a commit.

Suggested commit: `test(notifications): reset the favicon dot between test files (#118)` with an `Assisted-by: Claude Code:claude-opus-5-5` trailer. For the PR's Test Evidence: AI changed those two test files, and only their setup/cleanup, not any expected values.

**Decision for you:** even with this fix, #161's CI will stay flaky until the `initGlobalShortcut` problem is fixed. How do you want to handle it?
- **(a) Fix it in this PR.** Make `initGlobalShortcut()` in `web_src/js/modules/shortcut.ts` skip setup if it has already run. It's a few lines, it doesn't change the real page (which calls it once), and it fixes the failures in both orders. But it touches a teammate's code, which is outside #118's scope.
- **(b) Open a separate hardening issue** (Sprint 3 D2 covers flaky tests) and fix it in its own PR. Then re-run #161's CI until it gets a green run.

I'd go with (b): it gives the team a D2 item and keeps #118 focused. Either way, if this fix finishes #118's work, remember to `specstory sync` afterwards.

## Branches and commits

- Branches: `feat/issue-<N>-short-description`, `fix/issue-<N>-short-description` or
  `chore/short-description` (`STUDENTS.md`). One issue per branch.
- Commit messages follow Conventional Commits and end with the issue number:
  `feat(repo): show empty state on releases page (#17)`. Add an
  `Assisted-by: AGENT_NAME:MODEL_VERSION` trailer when AI helped; never `Co-Authored-By` or
  `Signed-off-by` (`AGENTS.md`). A human approves every commit before it is made.

### Before each implementation: sync with main

Every new branch starts from an up-to-date `main`. AI sessions run this before writing any code:

```bash
git switch main
git pull origin main
git switch -c feat/issue-<N>-short-description
```

To pick up new work on `main` for a branch that already exists, **merge, don't rebase**. Rebasing
or squashing after review has started is not allowed (`docs/sprint0/standards.md`):

```bash
git fetch origin
git merge origin/main
```

Do this before opening the PR and again if `main` moves while it is in review. A merge pushed after
approval needs a new approval (see Reviews). Never merge another feature branch into yours.

### After merge: clean up

A PR is merged with a merge commit once its latest commit is approved, every review comment is
addressed and CI passes. Then:

```bash
git switch main
git pull origin main
git branch -d feat/issue-<N>-short-description               # local branch
git push origin --delete feat/issue-<N>-short-description    # or GitHub's "Delete branch" button
git fetch --prune                                            # drop stale remote-tracking refs
```

Also check that the issue closed (via `Closes #N`), that the issue and PR are on the sprint
milestone, and that the issue has its AI Assistance comment. Then run `specstory sync` and file the
session's log (see `ai-logs/README.md`).

## Issue format: feature (user story)

Template: `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/user-story.yaml`. The user story must meet INVEST: Independent,
Negotiable, Valuable, Estimable, Small, Testable.

```markdown
## User Story
As a <role>, I want <capability> so that <benefit>.

## User Scenario
<A short concrete walk-through: who, where in the UI, what they do, what they see.>

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1: Given <state>, when <action>, then <observable result>.
- [ ] AC2: ...
- [ ] AC3: ...            (at least 3; each has a clear pass/fail result)

## Out of Scope
- <What this issue deliberately does not do.>

## Open Questions
- <Unresolved questions, or "None".>

## Design Decision
**Decision:** <what was chosen>
**Alternatives Considered:** <at least two concrete options, and why each lost>
**Rationale:** <why this one>
**Consequences:** <trade-offs, follow-up work, what it makes harder>

## Scope
small | medium | large, and matching `scope:` label
<One or two sentences on why: the components it touches and how much change you expect.>
```

## Issue format: bug report

Template: `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug-report.yaml`. Also used by hardening issues that fix a
defect.

```markdown
## Observed Behavior
## Expected Behavior
## Steps to Reproduce
1. ...
## Additional Information
<Version or commit, browser/OS, logs, screenshots.>
## Design Decision
<Same four fields as above: Decision, Alternatives Considered, Rationale, Consequences.>
## Scope
<Same as above: size, label and one or two sentences on why.>
```

## Issue format: hardening task

No GitHub template; write it in a blank issue. Used by hardening issues that don't fix a defect,
such as a flaky test or a broken CI check (Sprint 3, D2).

```markdown
## Problem
<What is unreliable now, and how you know: failing test names, run counts, CI run links.>
## Goal
<What "fixed" means.>
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1: ...
## Evidence of Fix
<Which evidence from the table below the fix will show.>
## Design Decision
<Same four fields as above.>
## Scope
<Same as above: size, label and one or two sentences on why.>
```

### Hardening issues

Work that makes the existing system more reliable rather than adding a feature. Good sources: the
D8 baseline run (failing or flaky tests, broken CI checks on `main`); the "Introduced" and
"Encountered" Tech Debt fields of Sprint 1 and Sprint 2 PRs; bugs found in reviews or after
merging; and the upstream issue tracker for the parts of Gitea the team works on. It is scoped like
any other issue and must include evidence that the problem is fixed:

| Kind | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Bug fix | A test that fails before the fix and passes after |
| Flaky test | The root cause, and repeated runs before and after the fix (e.g. 20 for a unit test, 10 for E2E) |
| Broken or missing CI check | Links to CI runs before and after the fix |
| Failing tests in the baseline | Pass/fail counts before and after, and the cause of each group of failures |

The site doesn't say where the evidence goes: plan it in the issue (Evidence of Fix, or Additional
Information for a bug), then post the results on the issue and in the PR's Test Evidence once the
fix is in. Regenerating snapshots, reformatting code, or silencing a check without fixing its cause
counts as small at most.

### Design Decision and spec review

- **Design Decision (D3):** fill it in once you've picked an approach, before opening the PR. Put
  a second decision under another `### Decision 2` heading. If a PR changes the decision, update
  the issue body.
- **Spec review (D2):** before coding starts, a teammate posts a review comment **on the issue**.
  Start it with `Spec reviewed` so it is easy to find. The layout is the reviewer's choice, but the
  comment must say what was checked:
  1. each acceptance criterion: clear and testable, naming any that aren't;
  2. the cases considered (e.g. empty input, errors, permissions) and whether the ACs cover them;
  3. whether the scope fits the stated size;

  and end with an approval, or the problems for the author to fix in the spec. `Looks good!` with
  nothing about what was checked does not count. An optional layout:

  ```markdown
=====
# AI assistance disclosure — required format

Course rule, not an upstream Gitea one. Every contributor discloses their own AI use per issue,
**even when no AI was used**. Source: the course AI Log Instructions page and `CONTRIBUTING.md`
(AI Contribution Policy). Two separate places, both required. The rest of the PR and issue
format is in `COURSE-WORKFLOW.md`.

## 1. A comment on the issue

Posted by each contributor on the **issue** they worked, once their work is done. One comment per
person — never edit someone else's. Add later sessions by editing your own table.

```markdown
### AI Assistance — @your-github-username

**Role in this issue:** Implementation

| # | Tool | Log | What AI helped with |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | claude-code | [2026-09-24_claude-code_issue-52-impl.md](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/blob/main/ai-logs/sprint1/YourName/2026-09-24_claude-code_issue-52-impl.md) | Confirmed the files found during concept location, drafted the template change and tests, ran them |

**Attachments:** [2026-09-24_claude-code_issue-52-impl/](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/tree/main/ai-logs/sprint1/YourName/2026-09-24_claude-code_issue-52-impl)
```

- **Role** is one of Implementation, Code review, Testing, Other — pick the ones that apply and
  delete the rest, do not leave the slash list in place.
- **Tool** is the tool's name, e.g. `claude-code`, `claude-web`.
- **Log** is a full `https://github.com/...` link to the filed log. Relative paths break in issue
  comments. File naming is in `ai-logs/README.md`.
- **Attachments** only when the log has a companion folder; otherwise drop the line.
- **No AI used?** Keep the heading and role line and write `No AI used` in place of the table.

## 2. A short section in the pull request description — no log link

Reviewers read the PR, and the review rubric scores "AI transparency", so the PR says how AI was
used and how you verified it. It does **not** link or cite the AI log: from Sprint 1 on, the team
references logs in **issue comments only**, never in PR descriptions or PR comments (Sprint 1 page,
D5; later sprint pages also accept the PR, and the issue comment satisfies both).

```markdown
## AI assistance

Claude Code (claude-opus-5) drafted the handler and tests following the existing register/delete
code; I reviewed every line, ran the tests, checked the page by hand, and can explain each change.
AI log: see the AI Assistance comment on the linked issue.
```

Name the model, say what AI did and what you did, and point at the issue comment for the log. The
PR's Test Evidence section has its own **AI-written tests** line, which names the tests AI wrote or
changed and how you checked their expected values (`COURSE-WORKFLOW.md`, "Pull request format").

## Rules that make a disclosure wrong

- **Placeholders left in**: `@your-github-username` or the full `Implementation / Code review /
  Testing / Other` list means the comment was pasted unread.
- **A log link in a PR description or PR comment.** Log links live in the issue comment only.
- **A log link that 404s.** Until the log is merged to `main`, link the branch that holds it; switch
  to the `main` link once merged.
- **A log folder that is not your GitHub username** — `ai-logs/sprint1/jdonohue/` is wrong when the
  account is `Jack-Donohue`.
- **Claiming work AI did as your own, or the reverse.** The claim must match the log.
- **AI-written replies to reviewer questions on your own issue or PR.** `CONTRIBUTING.md` forbids it:
  the questions are for you.

## For AI agents drafting an issue or PR

Put section 2 in every PR description you draft, and draft the section 1 issue comment
separately, both filled in from the session you actually ran — never with placeholders. You may
draft the wording, but say plainly that the human must review and edit it before posting, and leave
the issue comment for them to post under their own account.

Closes #118

## What changed

- **Tab icon badge.** `favicon-status.ts` now knows about two badges that can own the tab icon: an Actions run's status and a new unread-notification dot. A single `renderFavicon()` picks one (run status first, then the dot, then the default icon). The dot reuses the run badge's position and white ring, and is filled with `--color-primary` so it matches the navbar's unread bubble. `RepoActionView.vue` is unchanged.
- **Desktop notification opt-in.** A new **Enable desktop notifications** button on the Notifications page (`notification_div.tmpl`, wired in `features/notification-desktop.ts`). The choice is stored per browser in `localUserSettings`. The browser's permission prompt is only requested from that click, and a denial shows "Desktop notifications are blocked by your browser." Clicking it again disables alerts.
- **One alert across tabs.** Every Gitea tab already shares one event stream through `eventsource.sharedworker.ts`. Tabs now tell the worker whether they are visible and what their count is. When the count goes up and no Gitea tab is visible, the worker asks exactly one tab (the one used most recently) to show the alert. The decision logic is a small DOM-free class in `modules/notification-alert.ts` so it can be unit tested.
- **Alert content.** Only a count ("You have N new notification(s)", counting since Gitea was last in view); clicking it focuses Gitea and opens `/notifications`. The text reaches every page as `data-` attributes on the navbar count.
- **Polling fallback.** When the shared worker or event stream is unavailable, a hidden tab that sees the count go up alerts on its own; all alerts share one notification tag so the browser shows one.
- New locale keys in `locale_en-US.json` only.

## Why

Users who leave Gitea in a background tab don't notice review requests and mentions until they switch back. This adds a passive badge (AC1, AC2) and opt-in, count-only desktop alerts that never prompt on their own, fire once across tabs and only when Gitea isn't visible (AC3–AC9).

## Design

Follows the three Design Decisions in #118: per-browser opt-in in local storage, count-only alerts, and a dot badge where Actions run status takes precedence. Added during implementation: the shared worker decides which tab alerts, so a visible Gitea tab suppresses alerts from hidden ones.

## Tech Debt

**Introduced:** The polling fallback can't coordinate tabs, so two hidden tabs that both detect an increase each create an alert. They share a notification tag, so the browser shows one, but a visible tab in the same browser doesn't suppress them. The shared-worker path only has manual test coverage.

**Encountered:** `UserEventsSharedWorker` closes its port on `beforeunload`, which can be cancelled (existing FIXME in `modules/worker.ts`). A tab whose unload is cancelled may stop reporting to the worker. Left as is, since it predates this change and also affects the stopwatch. The worker class also had no way to send a message without reaching into `sharedWorker.port`; I added a small `postMessage` method.

````markdown
## Problem

`web_src/js/modules/shortcut.test.ts` and `web_src/js/features/repo-issue-edit.test.ts` fail whenever vitest puts them in the same worker, and pass when it doesn't. Which files share a worker changes between runs, so the failure looks random.

**Root cause.** `vitest.config.ts` sets `isolate: false`, so test files in one worker share modules and the same `document`. Both files call `initGlobalShortcut()` (`repo-issue-edit.test.ts` at module level, `shortcut.test.ts` in `beforeAll`). Each call adds two more `keydown` listeners to `document`, and they all dispatch into the same shared `globalRegistry`. After the second call, every key press runs its shortcut twice.

**How I know:**

- CI: the `sonarqube` job on #161 failed with `repo-issue-edit.test.ts > r quotes the selection after the existing text, or only moves to the reply box`: `expected "vi.fn()" to be called 1 times, but got 2 times` (`moveCursorToEnd`, line 78). Run: https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/actions/runs/43088279012/job/130770579133. In the same commit's `frontend` job, that file passed. #161 doesn't change either test file or `shortcut.ts`, which are identical to `main`.
- Locally, forcing both files into one worker fails every time, in either order:
  ```bash
  pnpm exec vitest run web_src/js/modules/shortcut.test.ts web_src/js/features/repo-issue-edit.test.ts --no-file-parallelism
  ```
  One order fails `repo-issue-edit.test.ts` (1 test) and the other fails `shortcut.test.ts` (3 tests).
- Adding a temporary "already initialized" guard to `initGlobalShortcut()` makes the same command pass.

**Why it also breaks SonarCloud.** The `sonarqube` job runs vitest with coverage before the scan. When a test fails, vitest writes no `coverage/lcov.info`, so Sonar sees every new TypeScript line as uncovered (`new_coverage 0.0 < 80`) and the quality gate fails. That can happen on any PR, whatever it changes.

## Goal

The two files pass regardless of order or worker grouping, and a page that calls `initGlobalShortcut()` more than once still runs each shortcut once per key press.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: Given both files run in one worker (command above), when the run finishes, then all tests in both files pass, in both orders.
- [ ] AC2: Given `initGlobalShortcut()` has been called twice, when a registered shortcut key is pressed once, then its action runs exactly once (new unit test).
- [ ] AC3: Given the fix is in, when the full frontend suite (`pnpm exec vitest run`) runs 20 times, then every run passes both test files.
- [ ] AC4: No test is skipped, deleted or loosened to make this pass.

## Evidence of Fix

Flaky test: the root cause above, plus 20 runs of the full suite before and after the fix with pass/fail counts for these two files, and 10 runs of the forced same-worker command per order. Results go on this issue and in the PR's Test Evidence.

## Design Decision

Proposed; the implementer may change it and should update this section if they do.

**Decision:** Make `initGlobalShortcut()` idempotent with a module-level flag, so a second call returns without adding listeners.
**Alternatives Considered:**
1. *Set `isolate: true` in `vitest.config.ts`.* This removes the whole class of shared-state leaks, but upstream Gitea chose `isolate: false` for speed, so the suite gets much slower and our config drifts from upstream.
2. *Change only the tests*, e.g. remove the listeners in `afterAll`. `initGlobalShortcut()` returns no handle for removing its listeners, so this needs an API change anyway, and the next test file that calls it brings the bug back.
3. *Return a cleanup function from `initGlobalShortcut()`.* Works, but adds API surface just for tests, and every caller has to remember to use it.
**Rationale:** A real page calls `initGlobalShortcut()` once, so the guard doesn't change production behaviour. It fixes both orders and protects future test files, and it's the smallest change.
**Consequences:** A second call silently does nothing, so a test can't re-initialize with fresh listeners. Other shared state in `globalRegistry` is unchanged; tests still need to unregister the shortcuts they add (both files already do).

## Scope

small, `scope: small`. One guard in `web_src/js/modules/shortcut.ts`, one new unit test, and repeated runs for evidence. No production behaviour changes.

Found while debugging CI on #161 (#118).

# Mid-Sprint Check-in: @CarsonRackley

**Code PR:** [#161 — feat(notifications): badge tab icon and opt-in desktop alerts (#118)](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/pull/161) (open, ready for review)

## Question 1: What have you implemented so far, and what remains?

I implemented #118, my Sprint 2 carryover, in PR #161. The tab icon gets a dot while there are unread notifications, and Actions run status still wins on a run page. Desktop notifications are opt-in per browser, show only a count, and fire once across all open tabs, only when no Gitea tab is visible. The shared worker picks which tab alerts. Each AC has a unit test, and I checked them manually in the browser.

What remains: fix the frontend CI failure, merge `main` in, and get the PR approved and merged. My second issue, #156 (apply a suggestion as a commit), needs its spec revised after review before I start coding. I also still need to do mutation testing on #118 with StrykerJS.

## Question 2: What is one thing you learned about testing in your project?

I learned that tests passing on my machine doesn't mean they are independent. All 405 frontend tests passed locally, but in CI an existing favicon test failed: it expected the default icon and got my notification dot. Gitea's Vitest config sets `isolate: false`, so test files that run in the same worker share module state. My notification tests turned the dot on and never turned it off, and whether the favicon test ran after them depended on how files were split across workers. The fix was to reset the badge state before each favicon test and after each notification test. Now, any test that changes module-level state has to clean it up, because another file may run next with that state still set.

## Question 3: What is one risk to finishing your work by Nov 19, and what will you do about it?

The biggest risk is #156. Its spec review asked for changes, two of its ACs depend on customer questions on #151 that are still unanswered, and it builds on #154, which was merged, reverted and is back as an open PR. @arjunsb26's API work (#160) also waits on my service. To manage this, I will revise the spec and ask for re-review by Nov 14, and ask the customer on #151 for answers now. I will agree on the `ApplySuggestion` signature with Arjun this week, and write the service and its tests first, since they don't need #154's rendering. If there are no customer answers by Nov 16, I will pick a default, say so on the issue, and test against it.

#156 S3. Apply a single suggestion as a commit on the PR branch
author: vvchopra | labels: enhancement,scope: medium | milestone: Sprint 3 | assignees: CarsonRackley

=== BODY ===
### User Story

Labels: `enhancement`, `scope: medium` · Type: Feature · Part of #151 · Depends on S1

## User Story
As a PR author, I want to apply a reviewer's suggestion with one click so that Gitea commits the
change to my branch and I don't retype it.

### User Scenario

Ben sees Ana's suggestion and clicks **Apply suggestion**. A small form shows a default commit
message, "Apply suggestion from @ana on main.go", which he keeps. He confirms. The page reloads,
the PR has one more commit changing line 18, and the Files tab shows the new code.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: Given a single-line suggestion and a user who can push to the head branch, when they
  apply it, then exactly one commit is added to the head branch changing only that line, with the
  given (or default) commit message.
- [ ] AC2: Given a user who can't push to the head branch (read-only, or a fork PR without
  "Allow edits from maintainers"), when the PR is shown, then there is no Apply button, and a
  direct POST returns 403 and commits nothing (#151 AC3).
- [ ] AC3: Given the commented line's text at the current head differs from the line the
  suggestion was written against, when someone applies it, then nothing is committed and they see
  "This suggestion is outdated: the code changed since it was written."
- [ ] AC4: Given the head branch moved between page load and Apply (someone pushed, or another
  suggestion was applied), when Apply is submitted with the old head SHA, then nothing is
  committed and the user is asked to reload (concurrent applies, #151 open question).
- [ ] AC5: Given the PR is closed or merged, or its head branch was deleted, when the PR is shown,
  then there is no Apply button and a direct POST returns an error and commits nothing.
- [ ] AC6: Given the head branch is protected against this user's push, when they apply, then the
  protection error is shown and nothing is committed.
- [ ] AC7: Given a comment with zero or several suggestion blocks, when shown, then there is no
  Apply button.
- [ ] AC8: The commit's author and committer follow the customer's answer to question 1, and a
  test asserts them.

### Out of Scope

- Several suggestions at once (S6); API (S7); recording "applied" state (S4).

### Open Questions

- Customer questions 1, 2 and 4.
- Should the Apply form allow editing the commit message, or always use the default?

### Design Decision

**Decision:** A new `services/pull` function (`ApplySuggestion(ctx, doer, comment, expectedHeadSHA,
message)`) that reads the file at the current head, checks the target line still matches the line
in `Comment.Patch`, replaces it, and commits through `files_service.ChangeRepoFiles` with
`LastCommitID = expectedHeadSHA`. Permission is checked with the same head-branch write check the
web editor uses for PR branches, including `AllowMaintainerEdit`.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- *Apply with `git apply` on a patch built from the suggestion, in a temporary clone.* Handles
  fuzz, but fuzzy application can land the change on the wrong line, and it duplicates what
  `ChangeRepoFiles` already does (temp repo, hooks, protection checks, push).
- *Just replace line N without comparing contents.* Simple, but silently overwrites code if the
  file changed since the review (AC3).

**Rationale:** `ChangeRepoFiles` already enforces branch protection, runs hooks and fails on a
stale `LastCommitID`, which gives AC4 and AC6 for free. Comparing line contents makes outdated
suggestions fail safe.

**Consequences:** Applying a suggestion triggers the normal push path (CI, PR recheck,
`InvalidateCodeComments`). A suggestion whose line moved but didn't change is refused rather than
re-located; a later issue could add re-anchoring.

### Scope

medium

### Scope Justification

makes a whole new service function,

**Cases considered:**
- Covered: no push access, fork PR without maintainer edits, outdated line, concurrent apply, closed/merged PR, deleted branch, protected branch, zero or several suggestion blocks.
- Not covered:
  - a comment on an old-side (deleted) line. S1 (#154) AC7 renders those as a plain code block, so AC7 here should also say there is no Apply button.
  - the file was deleted or renamed at head, or the line number is now past the end of the file. Is that the AC3 message or something else?
  - a suggestion identical to the current line, which would make an empty commit.
  - the file's line endings (CRLF) and a missing final newline being kept.
  - an outdated (`Invalidated`) comment: is the button still shown and AC3 handles it at POST time, or is it hidden?
  - a signed-out viewer.
- Design note: `ChangeRepoFiles` with a stale `LastCommitID` only returns `ErrCommitIDDoesNotMatch` when that same file changed (`services/repository/files/update.go:393`). If another file changed, it commits on the old parent and the push is rejected as non-fast-forward, with a generic error. func editorHandleFileOperationError(ctx *context_service.Context, targetBranchName string, err error) {
	if errAs := util.ErrorAsTranslatable(err); errAs != nil {
		ctx.JSONError(errAs.Translate(ctx.Locale))
	} else if errAs, ok := errorAs[git.ErrNotExist](err); ok {
		ctx.JSONError(ctx.Tr("repo.editor.file_modifying_no_longer_exists", errAs.RelPath))
	} else if errAs, ok := errorAs[git_model.ErrLFSFileLocked](err); ok {
		ctx.JSONError(ctx.Tr("repo.editor.upload_file_is_locked", errAs.Path, errAs.UserName))
	} else if errAs, ok := errorAs[files_service.ErrFilenameInvalid](err); ok {
		ctx.JSONError(ctx.Tr("repo.editor.filename_is_invalid", errAs.Path))
	} else if errAs, ok := errorAs[files_service.ErrFilePathInvalid](err); ok {
		switch errAs.Type {
		case git.EntryModeSymlink:
			ctx.JSONError(ctx.Tr("repo.editor.file_is_a_symlink", errAs.Path))
		case git.EntryModeTree:
			ctx.JSONError(ctx.Tr("repo.editor.filename_is_a_directory", errAs.Path))
		case git.EntryModeBlob:
			ctx.JSONError(ctx.Tr("repo.editor.directory_is_a_file", errAs.Path))
		default:
			ctx.JSONError(ctx.Tr("repo.editor.filename_is_invalid", errAs.Path))
		}
	} else if errAs, ok := errorAs[files_service.ErrRepoFileAlreadyExists](err); ok {
		ctx.JSONError(ctx.Tr("repo.editor.file_already_exists", errAs.Path))
	} else if errAs, ok := errorAs[git.ErrBranchNotExist](err); ok {
		ctx.JSONError(ctx.Tr("repo.editor.branch_does_not_exist", errAs.Name))
	} else if errAs, ok := errorAs[git_model.ErrBranchAlreadyExists](err); ok {
		ctx.JSONError(ctx.Tr("repo.editor.branch_already_exists", errAs.BranchName))
	} else if files_service.IsErrCommitIDDoesNotMatch(err) {
		ctx.JSONError(ctx.Tr("repo.editor.commit_id_not_matching"))
	} else if files_service.IsErrCommitIDDoesNotMatch(err) || git.IsErrPushOutOfDate(err) {
		ctx.JSONError(ctx.Tr("repo.editor.file_changed_while_editing", ctx.Repo.RepoLink+"/compare/"+util.PathEscapeSegments(ctx.Repo.CommitID)+"..."+util.PathEscapeSegments(targetBranchName)))
	} else if errAs, ok := errorAs[*git.ErrPushRejected](err); ok {
		if errAs.Message == "" {
			ctx.JSONError(ctx.Tr("repo.editor.push_rejected_no_message"))
		} else {
			editorHandleFileOperationErrorRender(ctx, ctx.Locale.TrString("repo.editor.push_rejected"), ctx.Locale.TrString("repo.editor.push_rejected_summary"), errAs.Message)
		}
	} else if errors.Is(err, util.ErrNotExist) {
		ctx.JSONError(ctx.Tr("error.not_found"))
	} else {
		setting.PanicInDevOrTesting("unclear err %T: %v", err, err)
		editorHandleFileOperationErrorRender(ctx, ctx.Locale.TrString("repo.editor.failed_to_commit"), ctx.Locale.TrString("repo.editor.failed_to_commit_summary"), err.Error())
	}
}

```markdown
### User Story

Labels: `enhancement`, `scope: medium` · Type: Feature · Part of #151 · Depends on #154 (S1)

## User Story
As a PR author, I want to apply a reviewer's suggestion with one click so that Gitea commits the
change to my branch and I don't retype it.

### User Scenario

Ben sees Ana's suggestion and clicks **Apply suggestion**. A small form shows a default commit
message, "Apply suggestion from @ana on main.go", which he keeps. He confirms. The page reloads,
the PR has one more commit changing line 18, and the Files tab shows the new code.

### Acceptance Criteria

Errors from the Apply POST are returned the way Gitea's other web forms return them: HTTP 400 with
the message shown on the page, unless an AC says otherwise.

- [ ] AC1: Given a single-line suggestion and a user who can push to the head branch, when they
  apply it, then exactly one commit is added to the head branch changing only that line. The form
  is prefilled with the default message "Apply suggestion from @<reviewer> on <file>" and can be
  edited: the commit uses the submitted message, or the default if the message is submitted
  empty.
- [ ] AC2: Given a viewer who can't push to the head branch (read-only, or a fork PR without
  "Allow edits from maintainers"), when the PR is shown, then there is no Apply button, and a
  direct POST returns 403 and commits nothing (#151 AC3). A signed-out viewer sees no Apply
  button, and a direct POST redirects to sign-in and commits nothing. *Pending customer question 2
  on #151; see Open Questions for the default.*
- [ ] AC3: Given the commented line's text at the current head differs from the line the
  suggestion was written against, or the file was deleted or renamed at head, or the line number
  is now past the end of the file, when someone applies it, then nothing is committed and they see
  "This suggestion is outdated: the code changed since it was written."
- [ ] AC4: Given the head branch moved between page load and Apply (someone pushed, or another
  suggestion was applied), when Apply is submitted with the old head SHA, then nothing is
  committed and they see "This branch has new commits since the page was loaded. Reload the page
  and try again." This holds whether or not the new commits touched the suggestion's file.
- [ ] AC5: Given the PR is closed or merged, or its head branch was deleted, when the PR is shown,
  then there is no Apply button, and a direct POST commits nothing and returns 400 with
  "Suggestions can only be applied to an open pull request whose branch still exists."
- [ ] AC6: Given the head branch is protected against this user's push, when they apply, then
  nothing is committed and they see Gitea's existing message `Cannot commit to protected branch
  "<branch>".` (the same check and text as the web editor), not the raw pre-receive output.
- [ ] AC7: Given a comment with zero or several suggestion blocks, or a comment on an old-side
  (deleted) line, which #154 AC7 renders as an ordinary code block, when shown, then there is no
  Apply button.
- [ ] AC8: The commit's author and committer follow the customer's answer to question 1, and a
  test asserts them. *Pending customer question 1 on #151; see Open Questions for the default.*
- [ ] AC9: Given an outdated review comment (its code changed in a later push), when shown, then
  its suggestion has no Apply button. A POST from a page loaded before the change is handled by
  AC3/AC4.
- [ ] AC10: Given a suggestion identical to the current line, when someone applies it, then no
  commit is made and they see "This suggestion makes no changes to the code."
- [ ] AC11: Given a file with CRLF line endings or no final newline, when a suggestion on it is
  applied, then the changed line keeps the file's line ending and the file's final-newline state
  is unchanged; no other byte of the file changes.

### Out of Scope

- Several suggestions at once (S6); API (S7); recording "applied" state (S4).
- Suggestions on old-side (deleted) lines (customer question 5): they render as plain code blocks
  in #154, so there is nothing to apply. If the customer allows them, that's a follow-up issue.
- Resolving the review conversation on apply (customer question 3).

### Open Questions

- **Customer question 1 (commit author)**, for AC8: unanswered on #151. If there is no answer by
  Nov 16, the default is: the person who applied it is author and committer, with a
  `Co-authored-by:` trailer for the reviewer who wrote the suggestion.
- **Customer question 2 (who may apply)**, for AC2: unanswered on #151. Default if no answer by
  Nov 16: anyone who can push to the head branch, including maintainers on a fork PR with "Allow
  edits from maintainers" on.
- **Customer question 4 (applying your own suggestion):** unanswered on #151. Default if no answer
  by Nov 16: allowed; the permission rule in AC2 is the only check.
- ~~Should the Apply form allow editing the commit message?~~ Resolved: editable, prefilled with
  the default (AC1).

### Design Decision

**Decision:** A new `services/pull` function (`ApplySuggestion(ctx, doer, comment, expectedHeadSHA,
message)`) that first checks that `expectedHeadSHA` is still the head branch's commit (AC4) and
that the doer may commit to the branch, using the same check as the web editor (`CanCommitToBranch`;
AC6). It then reads the file at the current head, checks the target line still matches the line
in `Comment.Patch`, replaces it, and commits through `files_service.ChangeRepoFiles` with
`LastCommitID = expectedHeadSHA`. Permission is checked with the same head-branch write check the
web editor uses for PR branches, including `AllowMaintainerEdit`.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- *Apply with `git apply` on a patch built from the suggestion, in a temporary clone.* Handles
  fuzz, but fuzzy application can land the change on the wrong line, and it duplicates what
  `ChangeRepoFiles` already does (temp repo, hooks, protection checks, push).
- *Just replace line N without comparing contents.* Simple, but silently overwrites code if the
  file changed since the review (AC3).
- *Rely on `ChangeRepoFiles`'s `LastCommitID` check alone for AC4.* That check only fails when the
  same file changed since `LastCommitID` (`services/repository/files/update.go:393`). If another
  file changed, it commits on the stale parent and the push is rejected as out of date, which the
  web editor reports with its generic "file contents have changed" message, not AC4's.

**Rationale:** `ChangeRepoFiles` already runs hooks, re-checks branch protection on push and
handles the temp repo, so only the suggestion-specific checks are new. Checking the head SHA and
`CanCommitToBranch` up front gives AC4 and AC6 their own messages instead of whatever the push
returns. Comparing line contents makes outdated suggestions fail safe.

**Consequences:** Applying a suggestion triggers the normal push path (CI, PR recheck,
`InvalidateCodeComments`). A suggestion whose line moved but didn't change is refused rather than
re-located; a later issue could add re-anchoring. Any push to the branch, even one unrelated to
the suggestion's file, makes an open page's Apply fail with AC4 until it is reloaded.

### Scope

medium

### Scope Justification

One new service function in `services/pull` with unit tests, one web route and handler with the
permission and PR-state checks, the Apply button and commit-message form in the review comment
template, a few locale strings, and integration tests for the permission and error cases (AC2,
AC4–AC6). No schema change. Recording the applied state is S4.

Closes #154

## What changed

A ```` ```suggestion ```` block in a PR code comment now renders as a small diff headed
"Suggested change": the commented line in red, the block's lines in green.

- **Model:** `Comment.SuggestionOriginalLine()` (`models/issues/comment_suggestion.go`) returns the
  commented line from the comment's stored diff context (`Comment.Patch`, whose last line is always
  the commented line). It returns nothing for old-side comments, non-code comments and missing
  context.
- **Templates:** `repo/diff/comments.tmpl` and `repo/issue/view_content/conversation.tmpl` put that
  line in a `data-suggestion-original` attribute on the comment body, with the locale label
  `repo.diff.suggestion.title`. Only new-side code comments get it.
- **Frontend:** `web_src/js/markup/suggestion.ts` is registered in `markup/content.ts` next to the
  mermaid and math handlers. Inside bodies carrying the attribute, it replaces each
  `code.language-suggestion` block with the diff, built with `textContent` only. It runs before
  code-copy, so the diff gets no copy button.
- **CSS:** `web_src/css/markup/suggestion.css` uses the theme's diff row colours, so light and dark
  themes both work.

## Why

This is the first slice of #151: reviewers can propose an exact replacement for a line, and readers
see it as a change rather than as a bare code block. It satisfies AC1–AC9 of #154. Applying a
suggestion (S3), the editor button (S2) and multi-line ranges (S5) are separate issues.

// Copyright 2026 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

package issues

import (
	"strings"

	"gitea.dev/modules/optional"
)

// SuggestionOriginalLine returns the commented line as the reviewer saw it: the last line of the
// stored patch, since CutDiffAroundLine stops right after the commented line.
// Old-side comments return None until #151 decides whether they may carry suggestions.
func (c *Comment) SuggestionOriginalLine() optional.Option[string] {
	if c.Type != CommentTypeCode || c.Line <= 0 {
		return optional.None[string]()
	}
	patch := strings.TrimRight(c.Patch, "\n")
	last := patch[strings.LastIndexByte(patch, '\n')+1:]
	if last == "" || (last[0] != '+' && last[0] != ' ') {
		return optional.None[string]() // "-" is the other side; "@", "d", "\\" mean no code line
	}
	return optional.Some(last[1:])
}
=== templates
=== suggestion.ts
import {queryElems} from '../utils/dom.ts';

function makeLine(kind: 'removed' | 'added', text: string): HTMLElement {
  const row = document.createElement('div');
  row.className = `markup-suggestion-line ${kind}`;
  const marker = document.createElement('span');
  marker.className = 'markup-suggestion-marker';
  marker.textContent = kind === 'removed' ? '-' : '+';
  const code = document.createElement('code');
  code.textContent = text; // never innerHTML: suggestion text is user input
  row.append(marker, code);
  return row;
}

// Replaces ```suggestion blocks in a PR code comment with a diff against the commented line.
// The server only sets data-suggestion-original on new-side code comments, so plain comments keep a code block.
export function initMarkupCodeSuggestion(elMarkup: HTMLElement): void {
  const original = elMarkup.getAttribute('data-suggestion-original');
  if (original === null) return;
  const label = elMarkup.getAttribute('data-suggestion-label')!;
  queryElems(elMarkup, 'code.language-suggestion', (elCode) => {
    const block = elCode.closest('.code-block-container') ?? elCode.closest('pre')!;
    // an empty fence renders "" (delete the line); otherwise every line ends with "\n", so one blank line is "\n"
    const raw = elCode.textContent;
    const diff = document.createElement('div');
    diff.className = 'markup-suggestion';
    const header = document.createElement('div');
    header.className = 'markup-suggestion-header';
    header.textContent = label;
    diff.append(header, makeLine('removed', original));
    if (raw !== '') {
      for (const line of raw.replace(/\r?\n$/, '').split(/\r?\n/)) diff.append(makeLine('added', line));
    }
    block.replaceWith(diff);
  });
}
=== content.ts
```

<tool-use data-tool-type="generic" data-tool-name="AskUserQuestion"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **AskUserQuestion**</summary>
**S1 (#154, merged in PR #168) renders an EMPTY suggestion block as "delete the line" and a block with SEVERAL lines as "replace the line with N lines". S3's AC1 currently says "changing only that line". What should Apply do for those two cases?**

Options:
- **Support both, match S1 (Recommended)** - Apply does exactly what S1's diff shows: empty block deletes the line, N lines replace it. Add ACs for both. What the user sees is what gets committed.
- **Only 1→1, hide Apply otherwise** - Smaller S3; empty and multi-line blocks show S1's diff but no Apply button (new AC). Users see a change they can't apply until a later issue.
- **Delete yes, 1→N no** - Allow line deletion, hide Apply for blocks with several lines (leave to S5). Middle ground, but splits behaviour the reader can't predict from the diff.

**S1 only finds ```suggestion blocks in the browser; there is no Go parser. S3 needs one on the server (to read the suggested text on POST and to count blocks for AC7), and S4/S6 will reuse it. How should it parse?**

Options:
- **Goldmark AST (Recommended)** - Walk Gitea's own markdown parser's FencedCodeBlocks, as `Comment.SuggestionBlocks()` next to S1's `SuggestionOriginalLine()`. Agrees with what S1 renders (~~~ fences, longer fences, fences in lists, exact `suggestion` info word, S1 AC9).
- **Line scanner / regex** - Simpler and faster, but can disagree with the rendered page on edge cases (fences inside lists or blockquotes, ~~~, longer fences), so Apply could commit something different from the diff shown.

**Where should S3's Apply button come from, given S1 builds the suggestion diff in JavaScript from a `data-suggestion-original` attribute the server puts on the comment body?**

Options:
- **S1's JS adds it (Recommended)** - Server adds e.g. `data-suggestion-apply-url` + PR head SHA next to S1's attributes only when this viewer may apply; suggestion.ts puts the button in the diff header when there's exactly one block. One render path for both tabs, re-renders after edits (S1 AC8). No JS = no button, same as S1's fallback.
- **Server-rendered in templates** - Button in comments.tmpl and conversation.tmpl outside the markup. Works without JS, but needs the server parser at render time for every comment and is laid out apart from S1's diff.


**Answer:** Support both, match S1 (Recommended), Goldmark AST (Recommended), S1's JS adds it (Recommended)
</details></tool-use>

You're mostly right about code reviews. For the spec, I'd still get a quick sign-off, though not a full second review. From `.claude-students/COURSE-WORKFLOW.md`:

**Spec (#156):**
- D2 requires specs to be "spec-reviewed before coding starts", and the review format ends with **Verdict: Approved | Changes needed**.
- Nothing in the rules explicitly requires a second review after you revise.
- The catch is what's on the record. The only review on #156 ends with **"Changes needed"**, and nothing says it was approved afterwards. A grader checking D2 (20 points) would see a spec that was never approved before coding. Since then you've also added three ACs and two design decisions.
- So I wouldn't ask for a full re-review. One short comment from @controlled-opposition is enough, something like "Spec reviewed again, changes addressed. Verdict: Approved." Then you're safe to start.
- It's your call, but that comment takes them two minutes and protects 20 points.

**Code reviews:** yes, one thorough review is enough.
- The rules require one substantive review using the rubric, with a review comment posted. It's worth 2 points of the per-PR grade and can't be a bare approval.
- After that, every new push needs a **new approval** on the latest commit, including merging `main` in.
  - The course requires it ("any push after the approval… needs a new approval").
  - GitHub also enforces it: the `main` ruleset discards existing approvals when new commits are pushed.
- Those later approvals can be short. A one-line note on what changed since the last review is good practice.

For #161, the one review so far is from gitar-bot, which doesn't count. It still needs that first full rubric review from a teammate, then an approval on whatever commit is latest when you merge.

---
scope: stryker.config.mjs, stryker.vitest.config.ts
verified-at: b70fe3924a

# mutation testing — StrykerJS for the frontend, go-mutesting for Go

**Read when:** running a mutation tool on changed files, writing a personal config, or a run that
stops before mutating anything.
**Not here:** how each test tier runs -> `testing.md`; the course deliverable and its file names ->
`COURSE-WORKFLOW.md`.

## Responsibilities

| Side | Tool | Where it comes from |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `web_src/js` (Vitest) | StrykerJS with its Vitest runner | `package.json` devDependencies, `stryker.config.mjs` |
| Go packages | go-mutesting | `go install`, nothing in `go.mod` |

Gremlins is not used: its README warns that very big Go modules can take hours, and Gitea is one
module (`go.mod`).

## Key files

| Path | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `stryker.config.mjs` | Shared Stryker options: the Vitest plugin, ignore patterns read from `.gitignore`, runner, reporters. Names no files |
| `stryker.vitest.config.ts` | `vitest.config.ts` merged with `isolate: true`, used only by Stryker |
| `vitest.config.ts` | The normal Vitest config, with `isolate: false` |
| `.gitignore` | `/.stryker-tmp` (Stryker's sandbox), `/reports/mutation` (its reports), `/report.json` (go-mutesting's) |

## Conventions & invariants

- `stryker.config.mjs` sets no `mutate`. Personal configs import it, spread it, and change only
  report paths or similar; the files to mutate are passed on the command line with `--mutate`.
- Stryker copies the project into `.stryker-tmp/` before running. `stryker.config.mjs` feeds every
  `.gitignore` line to `ignorePatterns`, which Stryker matches with `.gitignore` semantics (`!`
  included), so the copy holds only what git tracks. `node_modules` is symlinked, not copied.
- `plugins` names `@stryker-mutator/vitest-runner` directly. Stryker's default `@stryker-mutator/*`
  search looks beside its own package, which pnpm keeps under `node_modules/.pnpm` without the
  runner, so the `vitest` option is then reported as unknown.
- The Vitest runner's `related` mode (on by default) runs only test files that import the mutated
  files, and `coverageAnalysis: 'perTest'` reruns only the tests covering each mutant.
- Stryker runs all related test files in one worker. With `vitest.config.ts`'s `isolate: false`,
  module state (such as a listener registered at import) leaks from one file into the next, so
  `stryker.vitest.config.ts` turns isolation on. Normal runs and CI keep `vitest.config.ts`.
- go-mutesting's built-in test step replaces the real source file with each mutant, runs that
  package's tests, and restores it. Only the package's own `_test.go` tests run, not `tests/`.
- go-mutesting always writes `report.json` to the directory it runs in; the `json_output` setting
  in its YAML config is not read. In its output, `PASS` means the mutant was killed.

## Recipes

**Run Stryker on some files.** From the repository root:
`pnpm exec stryker run <config> --mutate web_src/js/a.ts,web_src/js/b.ts`. The summary table is
printed at the end; `mutation.json` and `mutation.html` land in `reports/mutation/` unless the
config moves them. A run on one ~250-line module with ~40 related tests takes about a minute.

**Write a personal Stryker config.** A `.mjs` file that imports the shared one:

```js
import base from '<relative path>/stryker.config.mjs';
export default {...base, jsonReporter: {fileName: 'reports/mutation/<name>/mutation.json'}};
```

Paths inside it resolve from the directory Stryker runs in, so run it from the repository root.

**Run go-mutesting.**

1. Install: `go install github.com/avito-tech/go-mutesting/cmd/go-mutesting@master`. Its module
   path has no `/v2`, so its v2 tags cannot be installed by version, and building it needs the Go
   version its own `go.mod` asks for.
2. Run on files, with the Go version from `go.mod` so the tests match CI:
   `GOTOOLCHAIN=go<version> go-mutesting <file.go>... > <out>.txt`. The last line holds the score.
3. Check `git status`: no source file may be left changed. Move `report.json` where it belongs.

## Gotchas

- Stryker's "There were failed tests in the initial test run" means a related test fails on
  unchanged code. Rerun it with `pnpm exec vitest related <file> --run --no-file-parallelism` to see
  whether it only fails when files share a worker (an order-dependent test) or fails anyway.
- A Stryker `EISDIR ... copyfile` error comes from copying a symlinked directory; any such folder
  needs to be in `.gitignore` or `ignorePatterns`.
- Mutants that hit Stryker's timeout count as killed, and whether one times out can change between
  runs, so two runs of the same code can differ by a mutant or two.
- An interrupted go-mutesting run can leave a mutated source file behind. `git diff` shows it;
  `git restore <file>` undoes it.
- Each go-mutesting mutant recompiles and reruns the whole package's tests, so packages with
  database fixtures (`models/...`) are slow: time one `go test ./<pkg>/` first and multiply.
- Behaviour covered only by `tests/integration` shows up as surviving go-mutesting mutants.
- `make lint-js` lints the root `*.ts` files, not `.mjs` ones, and nothing under `docs/`
  (`Makefile`, `ESLINT_FILES`).

## Related

- `testing.md` — the test tiers the mutation tools run
- `build-and-tooling.md` — the lint and build targets

## Mutation testing (D6)

A mutation testing tool makes small changes to the code (*mutants*), such as flipping a condition
or a boundary value, and runs the tests against each one. If a test fails, the mutant is
**killed**. If every test passes, it **survived**: the tests didn't notice the change, which points
to a weak or missing test. An **equivalent** mutant behaves exactly like the original code, so no
test can kill it. Definitions are in the course Glossary.

**Which issue:** one of your issues whose PR changes source code and tests (CSCI 535: two, and the
small issue may be one of them). A tool is required; mutating code by hand doesn't count.

| Code changed | Tool |
| --- | --- |
| Frontend TypeScript (Vitest) | StrykerJS with the Vitest runner |
| Go backend | Gremlins or go-mutesting |

1. Run the tool on the **source files changed by your PR(s)** for that issue, not the whole
   project.
2. Analyse every surviving mutant: equivalent, or a gap in your tests? If more than 10 survive,
   analyse at least 10, starting with lines your PR added or changed.
3. Add or strengthen **at least one test that kills a survivor** that revealed a gap, and re-run
   the tool to confirm it is killed. If no survivor reveals a gap (all killed or equivalent), say so
   and justify it in the surviving-mutants table; that completes this step.
4. Answer the three questions in the write-up.

Files:

- Write-up: `docs/sprint3/mutation/<issue#>-<github-username>.md`, using the template below.
- Reports: machine-readable output of the first run and the re-run, as
  `docs/sprint3/mutation/reports/<issue#>-<github-username>-before.json` and `-after.json` (`.txt`
  for go-mutesting). StrykerJS: add `"json"` to `reporters`. Gremlins: `--output=<file>.json`.
  go-mutesting: save the terminal output to a text file. The scores in the write-up must match the
  reports, and the mutant your new test kills must show as killed in the "after" report.
- The tool configuration you used, committed and linked from the write-up. Reusing a teammate's
  setup is encouraged, as long as you run the tool yourself and credit them. The team's shared
  setup (go-mutesting for Go), its commands and its pitfalls: `.claude-students/docs/mutation-testing.md`.

Common problems:

- **The tool stops before mutating.** It first runs the selected tests on unchanged code and stops
  if any fail. Fix or exclude them first; the D8 baseline shows which ones fail already.
- **Tests run against built code.** Mutants in the source are never seen by tests that run on
  compiled output. Configure a rebuild, or pick tests that run on source.
- **Tests need services.** Start the database or service first. How each test type runs is in
  `.claude-students/docs/testing.md`.
- **False survivors.** When limiting which tests run, include the tests that cover the mutated
  files. Otherwise mutants they would catch show as survived or not covered. Check that the
  relevant tests ran before writing a new test for a survivor.
- **Blocked?** Ask teammates first. Then tell the TA **as early as possible**, with the errors and
  the AI log of what you tried; the TA may approve a different issue or area. Problems reported at
  the end of the sprint don't excuse a missing D6.

// Shared StrykerJS settings for mutation testing the frontend. It names no files: personal configs
// import it and the files to mutate are passed with --mutate, see .claude-students/docs/mutation-testing.md.
import {readFileSync} from 'node:fs';

// Stryker reads ignorePatterns with .gitignore semantics, so the sandbox only gets what git would track
const gitignored = readFileSync(new URL('.gitignore', import.meta.url), 'utf8')
  .split('\n').filter((line) => line && !line.startsWith('#'));

/** @type {import('@stryker-mutator/api/core').PartialStrykerOptions} */
export default {
  plugins: ['@stryker-mutator/vitest-runner'], // the default "@stryker-mutator/*" search misses it in pnpm's store
  ignorePatterns: gitignored, // local folders can also break the copy, e.g. the symlinked directory in .venv
  testRunner: 'vitest',
  vitest: {configFile: 'stryker.vitest.config.ts'}, // related mode (on by default) runs only tests that reach the mutated files
  coverageAnalysis: 'perTest',
  reporters: ['clear-text', 'progress', 'html', 'json'], // json is the report D6 commits
};

added = collections.defaultdict(set); f = None

    if l.startswith('+++ b/'): f = l[6:].strip()

        cov = m.get('coveredBy') or []
        byfile = collections.defaultdict(list)
        for t in cov: byfile[tests.get(t, ('?', t))[0]].append(tests.get(t, ('?', t))[1])
        for tf, names in byfile.items():
            print(f"  covered by {tf}: " + ' | '.join(names))
print("total", n)
EOF
wc -l "$S/survivors.txt"; head -c 20000 "$S/survivors.txt"

```ts

- **Run by:** all 8 tests in `notification-desktop.test.ts`, plus the poller tests "AC5 a hidden tab alerts…" and "polling keeps going…".
- **Why #2 matters:** `&&` groups left to right, so Stryker replaced the inner `(api && permission)` with `(api || permission)`. When the API exists, that part is always true.
- **If shipped:** all three drop the permission check, so the stored setting alone decides. That only matters when the setting is on but permission isn't granted: you opted in, then revoked permission in browser settings, which is exactly the case the comment on line 15 describes. The toggle would keep saying "Disable", and the code would keep creating notifications the browser won't show.
- **Why it survived:** every test that turns the setting on keeps permission at `'granted'`.

test('AC5 after notifications are read elsewhere while hidden, the next alert counts only the new one', () => {

## Pull request format

Template: `.github/pull_request_template.md`. Title uses Conventional Commits, e.g.
`fix(issues): keep label filter after search`. Description sections:

1. `Closes #<N>`, which links the issue and closes it on merge. Every code PR links its issue, and
   the PR goes on the `Sprint 3` milestone too.
2. **What changed:** the change in your own words.
3. **Why:** the problem, and which acceptance criteria (AC1…) it satisfies.
4. **Test Evidence:** required from Sprint 3. It replaces the old "How it was tested" section.
   Every behaviour change still needs a new or updated test.

   ```markdown
   ## Test Evidence

   | Acceptance criterion | Test(s) | Level | Source of expected value |
   |---|---|---|---|
   | AC1: ... | ... | ... | ... |

   **Not tested automatically, and why:** [...]

   **AI-written tests:** [Which tests were written or modified by AI, and how you checked that their expected values are correct. If none, write "None."]
   ```

   - **One row per acceptance criterion** from the issue; for a bug report, the Expected Behavior.
     A PR that changes no product behaviour (e.g. a CI change) writes `N/A` and why.
   - **Test(s):** the test name, plus the file if not obvious. For a manual check, write `Manual:`
     followed by the steps and what you saw. An AC tested both ways lists both in the same row.
   - **Level:** `unit`, `integration`, `E2E` or `manual`.
   - **Source of expected value:** `AC`, `issue discussion`, `docs`, `upstream behavior`, or
     `other` (explain). **Never the current output of your own code:** a test whose expected value
     was copied from what the code returns cannot detect that the code is wrong.
   - **Not tested automatically, and why:** only for ACs checked manually only.
   - AI may draft this section; the author checks that it is accurate.

5. **CI / manual verification:** CI status. If CI doesn't run your tests, the commands you ran and
   a summary of the results (passed, failed, skipped).
6. **Design:** one line pointing at the Design Decision in the issue, or a note on how it changed.
7. **Tech Debt:** required from Sprint 2. Both fields are required, and `None.` is a valid answer:

   ```markdown
   ## Tech Debt

   **Introduced:** <shortcuts, workarounds or design compromises this PR makes, and why>

   **Encountered:** <tech debt that was already there and that you ran into, and how you handled it>
   ```

8. **AI assistance:** format in `AI-ASSISTANCE.md` §2, with **no log link**.

Per-PR grading (20 points): correctness against the acceptance criteria 6; tests written or updated
appropriately, with the Test Evidence section complete, every AC covered and expected values
justified 6; description explains what and why, Tech Debt section present, issue linked 3; CI passes
or manual verification documented 3; reviewed with the rubric (including the test evidence row),
reviewer comment posted, merged only after an approval on the latest commit 2.
```
</details></tool-use>
