# services/pull and services/gitdiff — pull requests, review, diffs

**Read when:** touching PR creation, mergeability, merging, code review comments, or the diff
viewer.
**Not here:** the `PullRequest` row -> `models-issues.md`; issue-side logic -> `services-issue.md`.

## Responsibilities

| Package | Owns |
| --- | --- |
| `services/pull` | PR lifecycle: create, mergeability checking, merge, review, code comments, branch protection enforcement |
| `services/gitdiff` | parsing a git patch into the structures the diff viewer renders |
| `services/automerge`, `services/automergequeue` | "merge when checks pass" |
| `services/agit` | AGit flow — creating a PR by pushing a magic ref |

## Key files

| Path | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `services/pull/pull.go` | `NewPullRequest`, `ChangeTargetBranch`, `AddTestPullRequestTask`, `PushToBaseRepo`, `UpdateRef` |
| `services/pull/merge.go` | `Merge`, `SetMerged`, `MergedManually`, `IsUserAllowedToMerge`, `CheckPullBranchProtections`, `GetDefaultMergeMessage` |
| `services/pull/merge_merge.go`, `merge_squash.go`, `merge_rebase.go`, `merge_ff_only.go` | one file per merge style |
| `services/pull/check.go` | the mergeability queue: `AddPullRequestToCheckQueue`, `InitializePullRequests` |
| `services/pull/merge_tree.go` | conflict detection via `git merge-tree` |
| `services/pull/temp_repo.go` | `createTemporaryRepoForPR` — the scratch clone merges run in |
| `services/pull/patch.go` | `DownloadDiffOrPatch`, `AttemptThreeWayMerge`, `CheckFileProtection` |
| `services/pull/review.go` | `CreateCodeComment`, `SubmitReview`, `DismissReview`, `InvalidateCodeComments` |
| `services/pull/protected_branch.go` | `CreateOrUpdateProtectedBranch` |
| `services/gitdiff/gitdiff.go` | `Diff`, `DiffFile`, `DiffSection`, `DiffLine`, `ParsePatch`, `GetDiffForRender`, `GetDiffForAPI` |
| `services/gitdiff/gitdiff_excerpt.go` | expanding context lines in the viewer |
| `services/gitdiff/highlightdiff.go` | intra-line highlighting |

## Conventions & invariants

- **Mergeability is computed asynchronously.** Nothing recomputes it inline: a change pushes the PR
  id onto the worker queue in `check.go` via `AddPullRequestToCheckQueue`, and the result is
  written back to `PullRequest.Status`. The queue is unique-keyed, so pushing the same id twice is
  free. Code that needs a fresh answer must handle "not computed yet" rather than blocking.
- Merges do not run in the live repository. `createTemporaryRepoForPR` builds a scratch clone and
  the merge-style files operate there; only on success is the result pushed. A merge path that
  writes to the real repo directly is a bug.
- Merge styles are `repo_model.MergeStyle` values (`MergeStyleMerge`, `MergeStyleRebase`,
  `MergeStyleRebaseMerge`, `MergeStyleSquash`, `MergeStyleFastForwardOnly`) and each must be
  allowed by the repo's PR unit config — check with the unit accessors
  (`models-repo-and-git.md`), never by string comparison.
- `Merge` is not the permission check. `IsUserAllowedToMerge` and `CheckPullBranchProtections` sit
  beside it in `merge.go` but are separate calls the caller must make itself.
- **Merging and closing judge dependencies differently.** `CheckPullMergeable`
  (`services/pull/check.go`), which the web, API and automerge paths all call, returns
  `ErrDependenciesLeft` while `MergeBlockedByDependencies` (`models/issues/dependency.go`) finds an
  open issue or an unmerged pull request, and skips that check when `IsDependenciesEnabled` is off.
  `GetMergeBlockingDependencies` (`models/issues/dependency.go`) lists the same ones for the merge
  box (`routers/web/repo/pull_merge_box.go`): both use `mergeBlockingDependencyCond`, so the page and
  the check cannot disagree.
  Closing (`SetIssueAsClosed`, `models/issues/issue_update.go`) skips dependencies the same way and
  otherwise uses `IssueNoDependenciesLeft`, where a closed pull request counts as done. Changing one
  rule does not change the other.
- **Review comments are anchored to a commit, not to a line of the current head.** `CreateCodeComment`
  takes `latestCommitID` and a `treePath`; when the branch moves, `InvalidateCodeComments` marks
  the ones that no longer apply. A comment feature that stores only a line number will drift.
- `GetDiffForRender` and `GetDiffForAPI` are deliberately separate — the render path carries
  highlighting, escaping and a repo link for building URLs. Do not use the API one to build HTML.
- `notify_service.*` is called after the transaction, exactly as in `services-issue.md`.

## Recipes

**Add something to the diff viewer.** Extend `DiffFile`/`DiffSection`/`DiffLine` in
`services/gitdiff/gitdiff.go`, populate it in `ParsePatch` or `GetDiffForRender`, then render it in
the repo diff templates and wire the frontend behaviour (`frontend-js.md`).

**Add a merge style.** A `MergeStyle` constant and its unit-config flag in `models/repo`, a
`merge_<style>.go` implementation, a branch in `Merge`, the repo settings UI, and the locale keys.

**Change when a PR becomes mergeable.** The check itself is in `check.go` / `merge_tree.go`. Add
the trigger by calling `AddPullRequestToCheckQueue`, not by computing inline.

## Gotchas

- `services/pull` is the logic; the `PullRequest` *rows* are in `models/issues/pull.go`. The
  package named `models/pull` is only automerge and review state (`models-issues.md`).
- A PR's issue fields (title, labels, comments) go through `services/issue`. Only PR-specific
  behaviour lives here, so a "PR change" often touches both packages.
- `AddTestPullRequestTask` reads as a test helper. It is production code that queues PR rechecks
  after a push.
- Diff size is capped by the `maxLines` / `maxFiles` arguments to `ParsePatch`; a large diff is
  truncated rather than failing, so check the `Diff` flags before assuming completeness.

## Related

- `services-issue.md` — the shared issue behaviour and the notify convention
- `models-issues.md` — `PullRequest`, `Review`, `Comment`
- `services-repository.md` — the push path that triggers PR rechecks

# routers/web — the HTML route table and page handlers

**Read when:** adding or changing a page, a form POST, or a guard on a web route.
**Not here:** the `ctx` value itself -> `services-context.md`; form structs -> `services-forms-and-convert.md`; `/api/v1` JSON endpoints -> `routers-api-v1.md`.

## Responsibilities

- `routers/web/web.go` — `Routes` assembles the middleware chain; `registerWebRoutes` declares
  every HTML route in nested `m.Group` blocks.
- `routers/web/{repo,user,org,admin,auth,explore,feed,events,misc,healthcheck,devtest,shared}/` —
  the handlers themselves. `events` is the server-sent-events endpoint; `devtest` is the
  `/devtest` component gallery.
- `routers/common/` — middleware and helpers shared with the API layer.
- `modules/web/` — a thin chi wrapper: `NewRouter`, `BeforeRouting`, `AfterRouting`, `Mount`,
  `Bind`, `GetForm`.

## Key files

| Path | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `routers/web/web.go` | `Routes`, `registerWebRoutes`, `verifyAuthWithOptions` |
| `routers/web/repo/issue.go` | a representative handler set, and the `templates.TplName` constants |
| `routers/common/pagetmpl.go` | `PageGlobalData` — data every template can rely on |
| `routers/common/middleware.go` | `MustInitSessioner` |
| `routers/common/blockexpensive.go`, `qos.go` | `BlockExpensive`, `QoS` load shedding |
| `routers/common/errpage.go` | the panic/error page renderer |
| `modules/web/router.go` | `Bind`, `GetForm` |
| `services/context/context_response.go` | `HTML`, and the dev-only `ctx.Data["TemplateName"]` |
| `templates/base/footer_content.tmpl` | prints that template name in the page footer |

## Conventions & invariants

- A handler is `func Foo(ctx *context.Context)` from `gitea.dev/services/context`. It puts data in
  `ctx.Data`, then calls `ctx.HTML(http.StatusOK, tplFoo)`.
- Not every handler renders a template: one backing a JS-driven widget on an otherwise-HTML page
  calls `ctx.JSON` instead, e.g. `routers/web/repo/issue_suggestions.go`. That stays in
  `routers/web`, distinct from the `/api/v1` JSON layer (`routers-api-v1.md`).
- `tplFoo` is a package-level `templates.TplName` constant whose value is a path under `templates/`
  without the extension — `tplIssues templates.TplName = "repo/issue/list"`.
- `ctx.Data` is the only channel from handler to template. A template cannot reach anything the
  handler did not put there.
- Sign-in guards are local variables built at the top of `registerWebRoutes` from
  `verifyAuthWithOptions`: `reqSignIn`, `reqSignOut`, `optSignIn`, `optExploreSignIn`. A new guard
  is declared there too, not in a subpackage.
- Repo pages get `context.RepoAssignment` (see `services-context.md`), which fills `ctx.Repo`;
  ref-scoped pages add `context.RepoRefByType`.
- A POST that takes a form is registered as
  `m.Post("/path", web.Bind(forms.XxxForm{}), handler)`; the handler reads it back with
  `web.GetForm(ctx)`.
- The middleware chain in `Routes` is, in order: `chi_middleware.GetHead`, optional gzip,
  `common.MustInitSessioner`, `context.Contexter`, the web auth middleware, `goGet`,
  `common.PageGlobalData`, then `common.BlockExpensive` and `common.QoS`.

## Recipes

**Add a page.**

1. Handler in the matching `routers/web/<area>/` file, signature `func(ctx *context.Context)`.
2. A `templates.TplName` constant beside the other constants in that file.
3. The template file at the matching path under `templates/`.
4. The route inside the right `m.Group` in `registerWebRoutes`, with the guards that group needs.
5. Any user-visible string as a key in `options/locale/locale_en-US.json` — never a literal.

**Add a form POST.** Do the above, plus a form struct in `services/forms/` and `web.Bind` on the
route. See `services-forms-and-convert.md`.

**Find the template behind a page you are looking at.** Outside production, `ctx.HTML` sets
`ctx.Data["TemplateName"]` and `templates/base/footer_content.tmpl` prints it in the page footer, so
a dev instance names its own template on every page. Failing that, grep the visible string in
`options/locale/locale_en-US.json` for its key, then grep that key under `templates/`. To go the
other way, from a template to its handler, grep for the `TplName` value — the template path without
the extension.

## Gotchas

- The static routes registered on `routes` *before* the `mid` slice is assembled (`/assets/*`,
  `/avatars/*`, `/favicon.ico`, `/api/healthz`) deliberately bypass session and auth middleware.
  Do not add an authenticated route there.
- `registerWebRoutes` is long. Find your group by URL prefix rather than reading top to bottom, and
  add the route to the group that already carries the guards you need instead of re-listing them.
- `ctx.HTML` after something has already written the response is a bug; `ctx.Written()` reports
  whether that happened.
- The issue page loads each comment type's linked data in one `if … else if` chain over
  `issue.Comments` (`routers/web/repo/issue_view.go`). A new type's loading goes there as its own
  branch; a type matched by an earlier branch never reaches a later one. That chain is also where
  linked data the viewer may not see is dropped: a close comment's duplicate target is cleared
  unless `ctx.Repo.Permission.CanReadIssuesOrPulls` allows its kind, so templates never show it.
- A pull request's merge box is assembled in Go, not in its template. `prepareMergeBox`
  (`routers/web/repo/issue_view.go`) fills `pullMergeBoxData` (`routers/web/repo/pull.go`), and
  `ViewPullMergeBox` reruns it to reload the box alone, so the box cannot use data the sidebar put in
  `ctx.Data`. Blocker messages go in `infoCommitBlockers`, which when present hide
  `infoProtectionBlockers`; the merge buttons are `MergeFormProps`, drawn by
  `web_src/js/components/PullRequestMergeForm.vue`. A blocker nobody may override gets its own flag,
  which `prepareMergeBoxFormProps` (`routers/web/repo/pull_merge_form.go`) reads to drop the merge
  styles, as with `isBlockedByDependencies` (set in `routers/web/repo/pull_merge_box.go`); joining
  `hasOverridableBlockers` would keep the buttons for anyone allowed to bypass branch protection and
  offer "(When checks succeed)" to the rest. If "Manually merged" is the only style left, the form
  opens it in "(When checks succeed)" mode for a viewer without `canMergeNow` (`onMounted`), so offer
  it then only when `canMergeNow` holds.
- A handler branch that only logs an error still redirects as if it worked. `NewComment`
  (`routers/web/repo/issue_comment.go`) shows a flash only for the close refusals it maps, so every
  refusal a person can cause needs its own `ctx.Flash.Error(ctx.Tr(...))`.

## Related

- `services-context.md` — what `ctx` carries and the response helpers
- `routers-api-v1.md` — the JSON side of the same handlers
- `architecture.md` — where routing sits in the dependency direction

# services/repository — repository lifecycle, branches, file edits, push handling

**Read when:** creating/forking/transferring/deleting a repo, editing files through the web UI,
changing branch operations, or working on what happens after a push.
**Not here:** the `Repository` row -> `models-repo-and-git.md`; the git CLI wrapper -> `modules/git`; PR effects of a push -> `services-pull-and-gitdiff.md`.

## Responsibilities

| Area | Files |
| --- | --- |
| Lifecycle | `create.go`, `fork.go`, `adopt.go`, `transfer.go`, `delete.go`, `generate.go`, `template.go`, `migrate.go` |
| Branches | `branch.go` — create, rename, delete, sync-to-DB, default branch |
| File editing | `files/` — `update.go`, `upload.go`, `content.go`, `tree.go`, `patch.go`, `cherry_pick.go`, `temp_repo.go` |
| Push handling | `push.go` — `PushUpdates`, `PushUpdateAddDeleteTags` |
| Settings / access | `setting.go`, `collaboration.go`, `repo_team.go`, `hooks.go` |
| Derived data | `commitstatus/`, `archiver/`, `gitgraph/`, `contributors_graph.go`, `license.go`, `lfs.go`, `avatar.go` |
| `services/git` | `commit.go` (signature and status enrichment), `compare.go` (`GetCompareInfo`) |

## Key files

| Path | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `services/repository/create.go` | `CreateRepositoryDirectly` |
| `services/repository/fork.go` | `ForkRepository`, `ConvertForkToNormalRepository`, `FindForks` |
| `services/repository/transfer.go` | `ChangeRepositoryName`, `StartRepositoryTransfer`, `AcceptTransferOwnership` |
| `services/repository/delete.go` | `DeleteRepositoryDirectly` |
| `services/repository/branch.go` | `CreateNewBranch`, `RenameBranch`, `DeleteBranch`, `CanDeleteBranch`, `SyncBranchesToDB`, `SetRepoDefaultBranch` |
| `services/repository/push.go` | `PushUpdates` — the fan-out after every push |
| `routers/private/hook_post_receive.go` | the caller: `SyncBranchesToDB` then `PushUpdates` |
| `services/repository/files/update.go` | the web file editor's commit path |
| `services/git/compare.go` | `GetCompareInfo` — powers compare and PR views |

## Conventions & invariants

- **The push path is two steps, both driven by `routers/private/hook_post_receive.go`:** it calls
  `SyncBranchesToDB` to update the branch rows, then `PushUpdates` for the fan-out.
  `PushUpdates` runs `issue_service.UpdateIssuesCommit` (`services-issue.md`), queues PR rechecks
  with `pull_service.AddTestPullRequestTask` in a goroutine
  (`services-pull-and-gitdiff.md`), and calls `notify_service.PushCommits` / `CreateRef` /
  `DeleteRef` — which is how webhooks and Actions get triggered, since both register themselves as
  notifiers. New "on push" behaviour belongs in `PushUpdates`, not bolted onto a router.
- **Two sources of truth, deliberately.** Git on disk is authoritative for refs and commits;
  `models/git` rows are a queryable cache. When they disagree, git wins and the rows need
  resyncing — `AddAllRepoBranchesToSyncQueue` does that in bulk.
- File edits and patch application run in a temporary clone (`files/temp_repo.go`), the same
  pattern as PR merges. Never mutate a live repository's working state.
- The `*Directly` suffix (`CreateRepositoryDirectly`, `DeleteRepositoryDirectly`) means "no
  permission checks, no queueing — do it now". Callers must have done the authorisation. Do not
  reach for these from a router.
- Renames and transfers insert a `Redirect` row so old URLs keep working
  (`models-repo-and-git.md`).
- Branch deletion has a separate check function (`CanDeleteBranch`) from the action (`DeleteBranch`);
  call both.

## Recipes

**Do something on every push.** Add it to `PushUpdates` in `push.go`, guarded by whether it applies
to the ref type being pushed. Keep it cheap or hand it to a queue — this path is in the critical
latency of `git push`, which is why the existing PR recheck is fired in a goroutine.

**Add a file-editing operation.** Model it on `files/update.go`: build the temp repo, apply the
change, commit, push back, then let `PushUpdates` do the downstream work.

**Create a repo variant.** `CreateRepositoryDirectly` is the base; `ForkRepository`,
`AdoptRepository` and `GenerateGitContent` are the three existing variations to copy from.

## Gotchas

- Repo creation is not one transaction end to end — it writes rows *and* creates a directory on
  disk. Failure handling has to clean up both, which is why the existing functions look defensive.
- `services/git` is two small files of enrichment helpers. The actual git plumbing is
  `modules/git` / `modules/gitrepo`; do not add git command construction here.
- `SyncBranchesToDB` takes a `getCommit` callback so it can avoid reopening the repository — pass
  the one you already have rather than opening another.
- A repo with `IsEmpty` true has no default branch commit; code that assumes one panics on a
  freshly created repo.

## Related

- `models-repo-and-git.md` — the rows this package maintains
- `services-pull-and-gitdiff.md` — what a push does to open PRs
- `services-issue.md` — commit-message issue references

# modules/markup — rendering user content safely

**Read when:** changing how Markdown, code, mentions, issue references or emoji are rendered.
**Not here:** the page templates and their functions -> `templates.md`; diff rendering -> `services-pull-and-gitdiff.md`.

## Responsibilities

| Package | Owns |
| --- | --- |
| `modules/markup` | the render pipeline: markdown, orgmode, csv, console, jupyter and external renderers, plus post-processing and sanitisation |
| `modules/highlight` | syntax highlighting for code blocks and file views |
| `modules/emoji` | the emoji table and `:shortcode:` replacement |
| `modules/references` | parsing `#123`, `owner/repo#123` and `fixes #123` out of text |

## Key files

| Path | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `modules/markup/renderer.go`, `render.go` | the renderer registry and entry points |
| `modules/markup/markdown/` | the Markdown renderer (goldmark) |
| `modules/markup/orgmode/`, `csv/`, `console/`, `jupyter/`, `external/` | the other renderers |
| `modules/markup/html.go` and `html_*.go` | post-processing: links, mentions, issue refs, emoji, commits, code previews |
| `modules/markup/sanitizer.go`, `sanitizer_default.go`, `sanitizer_custom.go` | the HTML allow-list |
| `modules/markup/render_helper.go` | the per-context helper supplying repo-aware link building |
| `modules/references/` | the reference parsers used by both rendering and `services/issue` |

## Conventions & invariants

- **Rendering is two stages:** a renderer turns source into HTML, then the `html_*.go`
  post-processors rewrite that HTML (linkifying references, mentions, emoji, commit SHAs). A
  feature like "link issue numbers" belongs in post-processing, not in the Markdown renderer.
- **Everything passes through the sanitiser.** `sanitizer.go` holds the allow-list; output that
  needs a new tag or attribute must be allowed there explicitly. Never bypass it — this package's
  entire job is that user content cannot inject markup.
- Rendering needs context to build links (which repo, which branch), supplied by a render helper.
  `models/renderhelper` provides the concrete ones for repo, comment and wiki scope — that is why
  rendering a comment needs more than the raw string.
- `modules/references` is shared: the same parser that linkifies `#123` in a comment is what
  `services/issue`'s `UpdateIssuesCommit` uses to close issues from commit messages
  (`services-issue.md`). Change the grammar and both behaviours move.
- These packages are leaves in the dependency direction (`architecture.md`) — the helper indirection
  exists precisely so `modules/markup` need not import models.

## Recipes

**Linkify a new kind of reference.** Add the pattern to `modules/references`, then a post-processor
in `modules/markup/html_*.go`, then allow any new markup in the sanitiser.

**Support a new file type in the file view.** Add a renderer under `modules/markup/` and register
it in `renderer.go`; external tools go through `modules/markup/external/`.

**Change code highlighting.** `modules/highlight` — and note the CSS side lives in
`web_src/css/modules/chroma.css` (`frontend-css.md`).

## Gotchas

- Adding a tag to the sanitiser widens the XSS surface for every piece of user content in Gitea.
  Treat it as a security change, not a formatting one.
- Rendering happens on read, on every view. Anything expensive added to post-processing is paid on
  every issue page load.
- There are several sanitiser profiles (`default`, `description`, `custom`); make sure you are
  changing the one the call site uses.

## Related

- `templates.md` — the template functions that invoke rendering
- `services-issue.md` — commit-message references
## Conventions & invariants

**Two ways to wire a feature, and new code should prefer the second.**

1. *Page-load init:* export `initFoo()` from a `features/` file and add it to the array in
   `index.ts`. Every function in that array runs on **every** page, so it must find its elements
   and return immediately when they are absent.
2. *Declarative:* `registerGlobalInitFunc('initFoo', (el) => {...})` in the module, and
   `data-global-init="initFoo"` on the element in the template. For clicks,
   `registerGlobalEventFunc('click', 'onFoo', ...)` with `data-global-click="onFoo"`. This covers
   elements added to the DOM later and runs once per element (guarded by an internal
   `_giteaGlobalInited` flag), so re-adding a node does not re-initialise it.

`registerGlobalSelectorFunc(selector, handler)` also exists, but `observer.ts` marks it as "less
efficient and less maintainable" — it is for element types already on many pages, not new work.

- **Ordering rule:** every `registerGlobalInitFunc` must run *before* `initGlobalSelectorObserver`,
  which `index.ts` deliberately calls last. Registering after it throws.
- **One function per element.** `callGlobalInitFunc` in `observer.ts` looks the attribute up as a
  whole string, so `data-global-init` names exactly one function — space-separating two is an open
  TODO there, not a feature. To add behaviour to an element that already has one (the new-issue
  title in `templates/repo/issue/new_form.tmpl` carries `autoFocusEnd`), put the attribute on a
  wrapper and query for the inner element.
- Data fetching goes through the `fetch.ts` wrappers, never a raw `fetch`.
- Show and hide with `.tw-hidden` plus `showElem` / `hideElem` / `toggleElem`. In Vue use
  `v-if`/`v-show` instead (`frontend-vue-components.md`).
- Use `node.getAttribute`, not `node.dataset` (camel-casing surprises), and never bind
  user-provided data onto a DOM node.
- Custom DOM events are prefixed `ce-`, declared as an exported constant next to their emitter —
  see `EventEditorContentChanged` in `features/comp/EditorMarkdown.ts`.
- TypeScript, per `docs/guidelines-frontend.md`: `import type` for type-only imports,
  `@ts-expect-error` over `@ts-ignore`, `!` rather than `?.`/`??` when a value always exists, and
  `async` only on a function that actually awaits.
- One feature per file or directory; ids and classes are kebab-case with 2-3 feature keywords.

## Recipes

**Add behaviour to an element.** Register a global init func in the owning `features/` module and
put `data-global-init="yourFuncName"` on the element in its template. No change to `index.ts`.

**Add a whole-page feature.** New `features/<name>.ts` exporting `initName()`, an early return when
its root element is missing, then add the import and the array entry in `index.ts`.

**Profile a slow page.** `?_ui_performance_trace=1` prints per-init timings; over 500ms is logged.

**Look up an issue by its number.** `matchIssue` (`utils/match.ts`) is the `#` list's search: a
number comes back first (`services/issue/suggestion.go` → `GetSuggestion`), and the current issue
is left out. Keyword matches are limited to the kinds the viewer may read
(`routers/web/repo/issue_suggestions.go`), but the match by number (`GetIssueByIndex`) is not, so a
viewer who can't read pull requests still gets one typed by its number. The duplicate close
reason's preview in `features/repo-issue-status-button.ts` uses it.

**Add a keyboard shortcut.** Call `registerShortcut` (`modules/shortcut.ts`). One given an `element` exists while that element
is in the document, hidden or not; a clash with a live one throws. A link can declare one that follows it (`onShortcutLink`,
`templates/repo/header.tmpl`), live while it's rendered; markup rendered twice (navbar icons, `templates/base/head_navbar.tmpl`)
marks one copy. The `?` dialog (`templates/base/footer.tmpl`) can turn shortcuts off (WCAG 2.1.4); only `alwaysOn` ones still run.

**Run one test file.** `pnpm exec vitest <path-filter>` (`testing.md`).

## Gotchas

- A page-load init without its early return costs every page in Gitea; the 500ms warning catches it.
- Fomantic-UI (jQuery) is vendored and deprecated. Do not build new features on it, and do not mix
  it with Vue — Vue may use its CSS classes but not its JavaScript.
- Which menu to build on, Fomantic dropdown or `<aria-menu>` (`web_src/js/webcomponents/aria-menu.ts`),
  is decided in `web_src/js/modules/fomantic/aria.md`.
- `utils/` is for pure helpers. A function that reaches for `window` or a global selector belongs
  in `modules/` or `features/`.
- A feature can follow a comment box it did not create: the editor's change and upload events
  bubble (`features/comp/EditorMarkdown.ts`, `features/comp/EditorUpload.ts`), and
  `getComboMarkdownEditor` finds the editor, as `features/repo-issue-status-button.ts` does. But
  the editor attaches itself before its async `init` finishes, and calling it before then throws;
  read its textarea until an event arrives.
- Enter on a Fomantic dropdown item only fires a `click` when the item is a link or carries
  `js-aria-clickable` (`web_src/js/modules/fomantic/dropdown.ts`), so a plain click listener on other
  items never hears a keyboard pick. The close reason menu in `templates/repo/issue/view_content.tmpl`
  marks its items; an `<aria-menu>` item needs no class, as Enter and Space call its `click()`.
- After a click on a Fomantic dropdown item, the dropdown keeps the focus, so focusing something
  else from your click handler needs `setTimeout(..., 0)`.
- `createTippy` (`modules/tippy.ts`) moves a popup to `document.body`, so inputs in it leave their
  `<form>` and are not sent. Keep their values in hidden fields inside the form, as the close reason
  popups in `features/repo-issue-status-button.ts` do.

## Related
## Conventions & invariants

- A Go package whose tests touch the database needs a `main_test.go` containing
  `func TestMain(m *testing.M) { unittest.MainTest(m) }`. Without it the test DB is never
  initialised.
- Every DB-backed test calls `unittest.PrepareTestDatabase()` first, which reloads the fixtures, so
  tests do not depend on each other's writes.
- Adding a row to `models/fixtures/*.yml` means keeping denormalised counter columns
  (`num_issues`, `num_closed_issues`, ...) consistent, or `CheckConsistencyFor` fails.
- Handler tests use `contexttest.MockContext` rather than constructing a `context.Context`
  by hand — see `services/context` for what the real one carries.
- Integration tests need Git LFS installed. The database comes from `GITEA_TEST_DATABASE`; empty
  defaults to SQLite, which is what you want locally.
- Frontend tests are Vitest, not Jest. Playwright is only for the e2e tier.

## Recipes

**Run one test.**

```sh
go test -run '^TestName$' ./modulepath/   # or: make test-backend#TestName
pnpm exec vitest <path-filter>
GITEA_TEST_E2E_FLAGS='<filepath>' make test-e2e
```

**Add a DB-backed unit test.** Put `*_test.go` beside the code; add `main_test.go` with
`unittest.MainTest(m)` if the package has none; call `unittest.PrepareTestDatabase()`; load rows
with `unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean`; add fixture rows only if no existing row fits.

**Add an integration test.** New `tests/integration/<feature>_test.go`; `defer tests.PrepareTestEnv(t)()`
at the top of the test; drive it through HTTP the way the neighbouring tests do. Do not add a
`TestMain` — `integration_test.go` already owns it.

**Check a flash message in an integration test.** After the request,
`session.GetCookieFlashMessage().ErrorMsg` (`tests/integration/integration_test.go`) holds the
rendered text. Compare the exact string: a missing locale key renders as the key and then fails.

**Add a migration test.** Alongside the migration in `models/migrations/`, with its own fixtures
under `models/migrations/fixtures/`; helpers in `models/migrations/migrationtest/`.

## Gotchas

- `GITEA_TEST_LOG_SQL=1` logs every SQL statement — the fastest way to see what a failing DB test
  actually queried.
- Fixture repos leave `EnableDependencies` out of their issues config (`models/fixtures/repo_unit.yml`),
  so dependencies read as off and block nothing. A test that needs them turns them on with
  `repo_model.UpdateRepoUnitConfig` (`tests/integration/pull_merge_dependency_test.go`).
- `contexttest.MockContext` sets `translation.MockLocale`, whose `Tr` returns the key and its
  arguments, and unit tests load no icons, so `svg.RenderHTML` prints `<span>name(size/class)</span>`
  (`modules/svg/svg.go`).
  To check English text, call `translation.InitLocales` and set both `ctx.Locale` and
  `ctx.TemplateContext["Locale"]`: templates keep the locale the context was created with
  (`services/context/context.go` → `NewTemplateContextForWeb`; `routers/web/repo/issue_view_test.go`).
- `GITEA_TEST_E2E_TIMEOUT_FACTOR` multiplies e2e timeouts (default 4 on CI, 1 locally); a test that
  only passes with a raised factor is a flaky test, not a slow machine.
- A handful of Go unit tests fail on native Windows for platform reasons (symlinks, temp-file
  cleanup). Run the suite on Linux, macOS, WSL2 or the `.devcontainer` (`STUDENTS.md` §6).
- `tests/integration` and `tests/e2e` share one Gitea instance per run, so a test that leaves state
  behind breaks later tests rather than itself.
- `loginUser` cannot get past the TOTP step, so it never signs in a user who has 2FA. Sign in first,
  then insert the `TwoFactor` row (`tests/integration/org_two_factor_test.go`); the session stays valid.
- `unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &Foo{ID: 1, Bar: x})` turns the bean into the `WHERE`, and
  XORM leaves out zero-valued and `xorm:"-"` fields, so those are never checked. To verify a stored
  value, load by ID and compare fields (`models/issues/issue_close_reason_test.go`).

func PrepareCommitFormOptions(ctx *Context, doer *user_model.User, targetRepo *repo_model.Repository, doerRepoPerm access_model.Permission, refName git.RefName) (*CommitFormOptions, error) {
	if !refName.IsBranch() {
		// it shouldn't happen because middleware already checks
		return nil, util.NewInvalidArgumentErrorf("ref %q is not a branch", refName)
	}

	originRepo := targetRepo
	branchName := refName.ShortName()
	// TODO: CanMaintainerWriteToBranch is a bad name, but it really does what "CanWriteToBranch" does
	if !issues_model.CanMaintainerWriteToBranch(ctx, doerRepoPerm, branchName, doer) {
		targetRepo = repo_model.GetForkedRepo(ctx, doer.ID, targetRepo.ID)
		if targetRepo == nil {
			return &CommitFormOptions{NeedFork: true}, nil
		}
		// now, we get our own forked repo; it must be writable by us.
	}
	submitToForkedRepo := targetRepo.ID != originRepo.ID
	err := targetRepo.GetBaseRepo(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}

	protectedBranch, err := git_model.GetFirstMatchProtectedBranchRule(ctx, targetRepo.ID, branchName)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	canPushWithProtection := true
	protectionRequireSigned := false
	if protectedBranch != nil {
		protectedBranch.Repo = targetRepo
		canPushWithProtection = protectedBranch.CanUserPush(ctx, doer)
		protectionRequireSigned = protectedBranch.RequireSignedCommits
		// If branch-wide push is restricted, allow direct commit when the
		// URL-derived tree path matches an unprotected file pattern. The
		// pre-receive hook re-checks every path the commit actually touches
		// (e.g. rename source and destination).
		if !canPushWithProtection && ctx.Repo.TreePath != "" && protectedBranch.UnprotectedFilePatterns != "" {
			globs := protectedBranch.GetUnprotectedFilePatterns()
			if protectedBranch.IsUnprotectedFile(globs, ctx.Repo.TreePath) {
				canPushWithProtection = true
			}
		}
	}

	targetGitRepo, closer, err := gitrepo.RepositoryFromContextOrOpen(ctx, targetRepo)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	defer closer.Close()

	willSign, signKey, _, err := asymkey_service.SignCRUDAction(ctx, doer, targetGitRepo, refName.String())
	wontSignReason := ""
	if asymkey_service.IsErrWontSign(err) {
		wontSignReason = string(err.(*asymkey_service.ErrWontSign).Reason)
	} else if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}

	canCommitToBranch := !submitToForkedRepo /* same repo */ && targetRepo.CanEnableEditor() && canPushWithProtection
	if protectionRequireSigned {
		canCommitToBranch = canCommitToBranch && willSign
	}

	canCreateBasePullRequest := targetRepo.BaseRepo != nil && targetRepo.BaseRepo.UnitEnabled(ctx, unit_model.TypePullRequests)
	canCreatePullRequest := targetRepo.UnitEnabled(ctx, unit_model.TypePullRequests) || canCreateBasePullRequest

	opts := &CommitFormOptions{
		TargetRepo:            targetRepo,
		WillSubmitToFork:      submitToForkedRepo,
		CanCommitToBranch:     canCommitToBranch,
		UserCanPush:           canPushWithProtection,
		RequireSigned:         protectionRequireSigned,

func getViewPullHeadBranchCommitID(ctx *context.Context, pull *issues_model.PullRequest) (string, error) {
	switch pull.Flow {
	case issues_model.PullRequestFlowGithub:
		if pull.HeadRepo == nil {
			return "", util.ErrNotExist
		}
		headGitRepo, err := gitrepo.RepositoryFromRequestContextOrOpen(ctx, pull.HeadRepo)
		if err != nil {
			return "", err
		}
		return headGitRepo.GetRefCommitID(git.RefNameFromBranch(pull.HeadBranch).String())
	case issues_model.PullRequestFlowAGit:
		baseGitRepo, err := gitrepo.RepositoryFromRequestContextOrOpen(ctx, pull.BaseRepo)
		if err != nil {
			return "", err
		}
		return baseGitRepo.GetRefCommitID(pull.GetGitHeadRefName())
	}
	setting.PanicInDevOrTesting("invalid pull request flow type: %v", pull.Flow)
	return "", util.ErrNotExist
}

func (g *ASTTransformer) transformFencedCodeblock(v *ast.FencedCodeBlock, reader text.Reader) {
	// * Some engines support a meta syntax for appending the filename after the language, separated by a colon
	//   * https://www.glukhov.org/documentation-tools/markdown/markdown-codeblocks/
	// * Some engines support additional "options" after the language, separated by a space or comma: ```rust,ignore```
	//   * https://docs.readme.com/rdmd/docs/code-blocks
	//   * https://next-book.vercel.app/reference/fencedcode
	if v.Info == nil {
		return
	}
	info := v.Info.Segment.Value(reader.Source())
	newEnd := -1
	for i, b := range info {
		if b == ' ' || b == ',' || b == ':' {
			newEnd = i
			break
		}
	}
	if newEnd != -1 {
		start := v.Info.Segment.Start
		v.Info = ast.NewTextSegment(text.NewSegment(start, start+newEnd))
	}
}

// SpecializedMarkdown sets up the Gitea specific markdown extensions
func SpecializedMarkdown(ctx *markup.RenderContext) *GoldmarkRender {
	// TODO: it could use a pool to cache the renderers to reuse them with different contexts
	// at the moment it is fast enough (see the benchmarks)
	r := &GoldmarkRender{ctx: ctx}
	r.goldmarkMarkdown = goldmark.New(
		goldmark.WithParser(goldmarkDefaultParser()),
		goldmark.WithExtensions(
			extension.NewTable(extension.WithTableCellAlignMethod(extension.TableCellAlignAttribute)),
			extension.Strikethrough,
			extension.TaskList,
			extension.DefinitionList,
			common.FootnoteExtension,
			highlighting.NewHighlighting(
				highlighting.WithFormatOptions(
					chromahtml.WithClasses(true),
					chromahtml.PreventSurroundingPre(true),
				),
				highlighting.WithWrapperRenderer(r.highlightingRenderer),
			),
			math.NewExtension(&ctx.RenderInternal, math.Options{
				Enabled:                  setting.Markdown.EnableMath,
				ParseInlineDollar:        setting.Markdown.MathCodeBlockOptions.ParseInlineDollar,
				ParseInlineParentheses:   setting.Markdown.MathCodeBlockOptions.ParseInlineParentheses, // this is a bad syntax "\( ... \)", it conflicts with normal markdown escaping
				ParseBlockDollar:         setting.Markdown.MathCodeBlockOptions.ParseBlockDollar,
				ParseBlockSquareBrackets: setting.Markdown.MathCodeBlockOptions.ParseBlockSquareBrackets, //  this is a bad syntax "\[ ... \]", it conflicts with normal markdown escaping
			}),
		),
		goldmark.WithParserOptions(
			parser.WithAttribute(),
			parser.WithASTTransformers(util.Prioritized(NewASTTransformer(&ctx.RenderInternal), 10000)),
		),
		goldmark.WithRendererOptions(html.WithUnsafe()),
	)

	// Override the original Tasklist renderer!
	r.goldmarkMarkdown.Renderer().AddOptions(
		renderer.WithNodeRenderers(util.Prioritized(NewHTMLRenderer(&ctx.RenderInternal), 10)),
	)

	return r
}

// render calls goldmark render to convert Markdown to HTML

The cycle is real: `services/repository/files` imports `services/pull` (`update.go:28`, `cherry_pick.go:18`). So `ApplySuggestion` can't live in `services/pull` as Decision 1 says while also calling `ChangeRepoFiles`; Go doesn't allow import cycles.

Here's the plan, in five steps. Each step ends in its own commit for you to approve:

1. **Parser (Decision 2).** Add `Comment.SuggestionBlocks()` next to #154's `SuggestionOriginalLine()`. It parses the comment with Gitea's own goldmark setup, whose fenced-code step already cuts the info string at a space, comma or colon, the same rule as #154 AC9. Go unit tests: no block, one, two, `~~~`, a longer fence, `Suggestion` with a capital S, and fences inside a list or quote.
2. **Line replacement.** A pure function covering ACs 3, 10, 11 and 12, with unit tests: the line no longer matches, or is past the end of the file; the suggestion makes no change; CRLF line endings and a missing final newline are preserved; an empty block deletes the line; one blank line replaces it with a blank line; several lines replace it in order.
3. **Service.** `ApplySuggestion` runs the checks in order:
   - the PR is open and its head branch exists (AC5);
   - the user can write to the head branch, via `CanMaintainerWriteToBranch` on the **head repo's** permission (AC2);
   - the head commit still matches the page's (AC4);
   - branch protection, via `GetFirstMatchProtectedBranchRule` + `CanUserPush` (AC6);
   - the line comparison (AC3), the replacement and the no-op check (AC10);
   - then `ChangeRepoFiles` with `LastCommitID` set.

   The commit's author and committer follow AC8's default (the person applying, plus a `Co-authored-by:` trailer for the reviewer).
4. **Route and templates.** A `POST …/pulls/{index}/files/reviews/comments/{id}/apply` route (sign-in required, inside the not-archived group). The attributes are set from the Files tab, the Conversation tab and `renderConversation`, so a newly posted comment gets them without a reload. Integration tests cover AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4, AC5, AC6 and AC8, sharing one PR setup to stay fast.
5. **Frontend.** `suggestion.ts` draws the button and an editable message form when there's exactly one block, posts the form, reloads the page on success, and shows the error message otherwise. Vitest tests for each of those.

**#156 Design Decision 1 puts ApplySuggestion in services/pull, but services/repository/files (ChangeRepoFiles) already imports services/pull, so services/pull calling ChangeRepoFiles is a Go import cycle. Where should ApplySuggestion live? (The issue's Decision 1 gets updated to match.)**

Options:
- **services/repository/files (Recommended)** - New suggestion.go beside ChangeRepoFiles. It is a file edit on a branch, and files already depends on services/pull for its errors, so no cycle. Update Decision 1 + add the cycle as an alternative that lost.
- **New services/pull/suggestion pkg** - Subpackage importing both services/pull and files. Keeps it under 'pull' in name, but adds a one-file package unlike Gitea's existing layout.
- **In the web handler** - Router calls ChangeRepoFiles directly (routers may import both). No new package, but the business rules sit in a router and are harder to unit test.

**AGit-flow pull requests (created by pushing to refs/for/...) have no head branch, so ChangeRepoFiles can't commit to them. The #156 spec doesn't mention them. How should they behave?**

Options:
- **Treat like AC5 (Recommended)** - No Apply button; a direct POST gets AC5's 400 'Suggestions can only be applied to an open pull request whose branch still exists.' Add AGit to AC5's text and to Out of Scope.
- **Out of scope, no AC** - Hide the button for AGit PRs and note it in Out of Scope only, without a tested AC.

**AC1's default commit message is "Apply suggestion from @<reviewer> on <file>". For a file in a subfolder, what should <file> be?**

Options:
- **Full path (Recommended)** - "Apply suggestion from @ana on routers/web/repo/pull.go": unambiguous when two files share a name, matches what the diff header shows.
- **File name only** - "Apply suggestion from @ana on pull.go": shorter, matches the User Scenario's "main.go" wording exactly, but ambiguous across folders.

**When Apply fails (AC3 outdated, AC4 branch moved, AC6 protected, AC10 no change), where should the user see the message?**

Options:
- **Inside the apply form (Recommended)** - Shown under the message box in the suggestion header, next to what failed; the form stays open so they can reload or cancel. Easy to assert in Vitest.
- **Error toast** - Gitea's showErrorToast at the top of the page. Consistent with other fetch errors, but detached from the suggestion it refers to.


**Answer:** services/repository/files (Recommended), Treat like AC5 (Recommended), Full path (Recommended), Inside the apply form (Recommended)

```text
- [ ] AC5: Given the PR is closed or merged, or its head branch was deleted, when the PR is shown,
  then there is no Apply button, and a direct POST commits nothing and returns 400 with
  "Suggestions can only be applied to an open pull request whose branch still exists."
### Out of Scope

- Several suggestions at once (S6); API (S7); recording "applied" state (S4).
- Suggestions on old-side (deleted) lines (customer question 5): they render as plain code blocks
  in #154, so there is nothing to apply. If the customer allows them, that's a follow-up issue.
- Resolving the review conversation on apply (customer question 3).
- Applying without JavaScript: like #154's no-JavaScript fallback, the suggestion is then a plain
  code block with no Apply button.
- Suggestions spanning several commented lines (S5). A one-line comment whose block has several
  lines is in scope (AC12).

### Design Decision

**Decision:** A new `services/pull` function (`ApplySuggestion(ctx, doer, comment, expectedHeadSHA,
message)`) that first checks that `expectedHeadSHA` is still the head branch's commit (AC4) and
that the doer may commit to the branch, using the same check as the web editor (`CanCommitToBranch`;
AC6). It then reads the file at the current head, checks the target line still matches
`Comment.SuggestionOriginalLine()` from #154 (ignoring a trailing `\r` on both sides, so CRLF files
compare correctly), replaces it with the block's lines, and commits through
`files_service.ChangeRepoFiles` with
`LastCommitID = expectedHeadSHA`. Permission is checked with the same head-branch write check the
web editor uses for PR branches, including `AllowMaintainerEdit`.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- *Apply with `git apply` on a patch built from the suggestion, in a temporary clone.* Handles
  fuzz, but fuzzy application can land the change on the wrong line, and it duplicates what
  `ChangeRepoFiles` already does (temp repo, hooks, protection checks, push).
- *Just replace line N without comparing contents.* Simple, but silently overwrites code if the
  file changed since the review (AC3).
- *Rely on `ChangeRepoFiles`'s `LastCommitID` check alone for AC4.* That check only fails when the
  same file changed since `LastCommitID` (`services/repository/files/update.go:393`). If another
  file changed, it commits on the stale parent and the push is rejected as out of date, which the
  web editor reports with its generic "file contents have changed" message, not AC4's.

**Rationale:** `ChangeRepoFiles` already runs hooks, re-checks branch protection on push and
handles the temp repo, so only the suggestion-specific checks are new. Checking the head SHA and
`CanCommitToBranch` up front gives AC4 and AC6 their own messages instead of whatever the push
returns. Comparing line contents makes outdated suggestions fail safe.

**Consequences:** Applying a suggestion triggers the normal push path (CI, PR recheck,
`InvalidateCodeComments`). A suggestion whose line moved but didn't change is refused rather than
re-located; a later issue could add re-anchoring. Any push to the branch, even one unrelated to
```

func TestCommentSuggestionOriginalLine(t *testing.T) {
	const header = "diff --git a/main.go b/main.go\n--- a/main.go\n+++ b/main.go\n@@ -1,3 +1,3 @@\n"
	cases := []struct {
		name     string
		typ      issues_model.CommentType
		line     int64
		patch    string
		expected optional.Option[string]
	}{
		{"added line keeps indentation", issues_model.CommentTypeCode, 3, header + " package main\n-\treturn nil\n+\treturn err", optional.Some("\treturn err")},
		{"context line", issues_model.CommentTypeCode, 2, header + " package main\n func main() {}", optional.Some("func main() {}")},
		{"trailing newline in patch", issues_model.CommentTypeCode, 2, header + " package main\n+x := 1\n", optional.Some("x := 1")},
		{"blank context line", issues_model.CommentTypeCode, 2, header + " package main\n ", optional.Some("")},
		{"CRLF kept", issues_model.CommentTypeCode, 1, header + "+foo\r", optional.Some("foo\r")},
		{"old side is not supported", issues_model.CommentTypeCode, -2, header + " package main\n-\treturn nil", optional.None[string]()},
		{"removed line on new side is inconsistent", issues_model.CommentTypeCode, 2, header + " package main\n-gone", optional.None[string]()},
		{"empty patch", issues_model.CommentTypeCode, 2, "", optional.None[string]()},
		{"header only", issues_model.CommentTypeCode, 2, header, optional.None[string]()},
		{"not a code comment", issues_model.CommentTypeComment, 2, header + "+x", optional.None[string]()},
	}
	for _, c := range cases {
		t.Run(c.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			comment := &issues_model.Comment{Type: c.typ, Line: c.line, Patch: c.patch}
			assert.Equal(t, c.expected, comment.SuggestionOriginalLine())
		})
	}
}

```go
// Copyright 2026 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

package markdown

import (
	"context"
	"strings"

	"gitea.dev/modules/markup"
	giteautil "gitea.dev/modules/util"

	"github.com/yuin/goldmark/ast"
	"github.com/yuin/goldmark/parser"
	"github.com/yuin/goldmark/text"
)

// FencedCodeBlocks returns the text of each fenced code block whose language is lang. It parses the
// source the way render does, so callers find exactly the blocks the rendered page shows.
func FencedCodeBlocks(ctx context.Context, source []byte, lang string) []string {
	rctx := markup.NewRenderContext(ctx)
	buf := giteautil.NormalizeEOL(source)
	rc := &RenderConfig{Meta: markup.RenderMetaAsDetails}
	buf, _ = ExtractMetadataBytes(buf, rc) // front matter is not part of the rendered body
	pc := newParserContext(rctx)
	pc.Set(renderConfigKey, rc)
	doc := SpecializedMarkdown(rctx).goldmarkMarkdown.Parser().Parse(text.NewReader(buf), parser.WithContext(pc))

	var blocks []string
	_ = ast.Walk(doc, func(n ast.Node, entering bool) (ast.WalkStatus, error) {
		code, ok := n.(*ast.FencedCodeBlock)
		if !entering || !ok {
			return ast.WalkContinue, nil
		}
		// the AST transformer has already cut the info string at its first space, comma or colon
		if string(code.Language(buf)) == lang {
			var sb strings.Builder
			for i := range code.Lines().Len() {
				seg := code.Lines().At(i)
				sb.Write(seg.Value(buf)) // Value keeps the indentation a list or quote leaves inside the block
			}
			blocks = append(blocks, sb.String())
		}
		return ast.WalkSkipChildren, nil
	})
	return blocks
}

```

var (
	// ErrSuggestionOutdated means the commented line no longer reads as it did when the suggestion was written (#156 AC3)
	ErrSuggestionOutdated = errors.New("the suggestion is outdated")
	// ErrSuggestionNoChange means applying the suggestion would leave the file as it is (#156 AC10)
	ErrSuggestionNoChange = errors.New("the suggestion makes no changes")
)

// applySuggestionToContent replaces line lineNum (1-based) of content with the suggestion's lines, the way
// #154 draws the diff: "" deletes the line, "\n" leaves one blank line, otherwise one line per suggestion line.
// original is the line the suggestion was written against; content and original may use CRLF.
func applySuggestionToContent(content string, lineNum int, original, suggestion string) (string, error) {
	lines := strings.SplitAfter(content, "\n") // every element but the last keeps its "\n"
	if lines[len(lines)-1] == "" {
		lines = lines[:len(lines)-1] // content ended with a newline
	}
	idx := lineNum - 1
	if idx < 0 || idx >= len(lines) {
		return "", ErrSuggestionOutdated
	}

	target := lines[idx]
	ending := ""
	switch {
	case strings.HasSuffix(target, "\r\n"):
		ending = "\r\n"
	case strings.HasSuffix(target, "\n"):
		ending = "\n"
	}
	if strings.TrimSuffix(target, ending) != strings.TrimSuffix(original, "\r") {
		return "", ErrSuggestionOutdated
	}

	var replacement string
	if suggestion != "" {
		innerEnding := ending
		if innerEnding == "" { // the last line has no newline, so new lines in between take the file's own
			innerEnding = "\n"
			if strings.Contains(content, "\r\n") {
				innerEnding = "\r\n"
			}
		}
		newLines := strings.Split(strings.TrimSuffix(suggestion, "\n"), "\n")
		replacement = strings.Join(newLines, innerEnding) + ending
	}

	before := strings.Join(lines[:idx], "")
	if replacement == "" && ending == "" && idx > 0 {
		// deleting a last line that has no newline: the line before it becomes last and loses its newline,
		// so the file still ends without one (#156 AC11)
		prev := lines[idx-1]
		before = strings.Join(lines[:idx-1], "") + strings.TrimSuffix(strings.TrimSuffix(prev, "\n"), "\r")
	}
	result := before + replacement + strings.Join(lines[idx+1:], "")
	if result == content {
		return "", ErrSuggestionNoChange
	}
	return result, nil
}

All 18 cases of step 2 pass on the first run, and `gofmt` is clean. Nothing is committed yet.

**`services/repository/files/suggestion.go` (new):**
- Two errors the route will turn into the spec's messages:
  - `ErrSuggestionOutdated` gives AC3's "This suggestion is outdated: the code changed since it was written."
  - `ErrSuggestionNoChange` gives AC10's "This suggestion makes no changes to the code."
- `applySuggestionToContent(content, lineNum, original, suggestion)` is a pure function with no git or database access, which is why it can be tested on its own:
  - **AC3:** it rejects the change if the line is past the end of the file (or the file is empty), or if the line's text differs from what the suggestion was written against. Trailing whitespace counts as a difference. A trailing `\r` is ignored on both sides, so CRLF files compare correctly.
  - **AC12:** it replaces the line exactly as #154 draws it. An empty block deletes it, `"\n"` leaves one blank line, and several lines replace it in order.
  - **AC11:** new lines use the line ending of the line they replace (CRLF stays CRLF). A last line without a final newline stays without one.
  - **AC10:** if the result equals the original file, it returns `ErrSuggestionNoChange`.

**One interpretation to confirm:** when a suggestion **deletes the last line of a file that has no final newline** (`"a\nb"` → delete `b`), I return `"a"`, not `"a\n"`. That keeps AC11's "final-newline state is unchanged", but it means the line *before* also loses its newline character. The alternative is `"a\n"`, which leaves that previous line alone but gives the file a final newline it didn't have. AC11 reads to me as the first, so that's what the test expects ("AC11 deleting a last line without a final newline"). Tell me if you read it the other way.

import (
)
)
func CreateCodeComment(ctx *context.Context) {
	form := web.GetForm(ctx).(*forms.CodeCommentForm)
	issue := GetActionIssue(ctx)
	if ctx.Written() {
		return
	}
	if !issue.IsPull {
		return
	}

	if ctx.HasError() {
		ctx.Flash.Error(ctx.GetErrMsg())
		ctx.Redirect(fmt.Sprintf("%s/pulls/%d/files", ctx.Repo.RepoLink, issue.Index))
		return
	}

	signedLine := form.Line
	if form.Side == "previous" {
		signedLine *= -1
	}

	var attachments []string
	if setting.Attachment.Enabled {
		attachments = form.Files
	}

	comment, err := pull_service.CreateCodeComment(ctx,
		ctx.Doer,
		ctx.Repo.GitRepo,
		issue,
		signedLine,
		form.Content,
		form.TreePath,
		!form.SingleReview,
		form.Reply,
		form.LatestCommitID,
		attachments,
	)
	if err != nil {
		ctx.ServerError("CreateCodeComment", err)
		return
	}

	if comment == nil {
		log.Trace("Comment not created: %-v #%d[%d]", ctx.Repo.Repository, issue.Index, issue.ID)
		ctx.Redirect(fmt.Sprintf("%s/pulls/%d/files", ctx.Repo.RepoLink, issue.Index))
		return
	}

	log.Trace("Comment created: %-v #%d[%d] Comment[%d]", ctx.Repo.Repository, issue.Index, issue.ID, comment.ID)

	renderConversation(ctx, comment, form.Origin)
}

// UpdateResolveConversation add or remove an Conversation resolved mark
func renderConversation(ctx *context.Context, comment *issues_model.Comment, origin string) {
	ctx.Data["PageIsPullFiles"] = origin == "diff"

	showOutdatedComments := origin == "timeline" || GetShowOutdatedComments(ctx)
	comments, err := issues_model.FetchCodeCommentsByLine(ctx, comment.Issue, ctx.Doer, comment.TreePath, comment.Line, showOutdatedComments)
	if err != nil {
		ctx.ServerError("FetchCodeCommentsByLine", err)
		return
	}
	if len(comments) == 0 {
		// if the comments are empty (deleted, outdated, etc), it's better to tell the users that it is outdated
		ctx.HTML(http.StatusOK, tplConversationOutdated)
		return
	}

	if err := comments.LoadAttachments(ctx); err != nil {
		ctx.ServerError("LoadAttachments", err)
		return
	}

	ctx.Data["IsAttachmentEnabled"] = setting.Attachment.Enabled
	upload.AddUploadContext(ctx, "comment")

	ctx.Data["comments"] = comments
	if ctx.Data["CanMarkConversation"], err = issues_model.CanMarkConversation(ctx, comment.Issue, ctx.Doer); err != nil {
		ctx.ServerError("CanMarkConversation", err)
		return
	}
	ctx.Data["Issue"] = comment.Issue
	if err = comment.Issue.LoadPullRequest(ctx); err != nil {
		ctx.ServerError("comment.Issue.LoadPullRequest", err)
		return
	}
	pullHeadCommitID, err := ctx.Repo.GitRepo.GetRefCommitID(comment.Issue.PullRequest.GetGitHeadRefName())
	if err != nil {
		ctx.ServerError("GetRefCommitID", err)
		return
	}
	ctx.Data["AfterCommitID"] = pullHeadCommitID
	ctx.Data["CanBlockUser"] = func(blocker, blockee *user_model.User) bool {
		return user_service.CanBlockUser(ctx, ctx.Doer, blocker, blockee)
	}

	switch origin {
	case "diff":
		ctx.HTML(http.StatusOK, tplDiffConversation)
	case "timeline":
		ctx.HTML(http.StatusOK, tplTimelineConversation)
	default:
		ctx.HTTPError(http.StatusBadRequest, "Unknown origin: "+origin)
	}
}

// SubmitReview creates a review out of the existing pending review or creates a new one if no pending review exist

package integration

	files_service "gitea.dev/services/repository/files"

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

func TestPullReviewSuggestionAttribute(t *testing.T) {
	onGiteaRun(t, func(t *testing.T, u *url.URL) {
		user2 := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &user_model.User{ID: 2})
		repo, err := repo_service.CreateRepositoryDirectly(t.Context(), user2, user2, repo_service.CreateRepoOptions{
			Name:             "test_suggestion",
			Readme:           "Default",
			AutoInit:         true,
			ObjectFormatName: git.Sha1ObjectFormat.Name(),
			DefaultBranch:    "master",
		}, true)
		require.NoError(t, err)

		_, err = files_service.ChangeRepoFiles(t.Context(), repo, user2, &files_service.ChangeRepoFilesOptions{
			NewBranch: "suggestion-branch",
			Files: []*files_service.ChangeRepoFile{{
				Operation:     "update",
				TreePath:      "README.md",
				ContentReader: strings.NewReader("# Title\n\treturn err\n"),
			}},
		})
		require.NoError(t, err)

		session := loginUser(t, "user2")
		testPullCreate(t, session, "user2", "test_suggestion", false, "master", "suggestion-branch", "Suggestion PR")
		pr := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.PullRequest{BaseRepoID: repo.ID, HeadBranch: "suggestion-branch"})
		require.NoError(t, pr.LoadIssue(t.Context()))
		commentURL := fmt.Sprintf("/user2/test_suggestion/pulls/%d/files/reviews/comments", pr.Issue.Index)

		postComment := func(t *testing.T, origin, side, line string, extra map[string]string) *HTMLDoc {
			values := map[string]string{
				"origin":        origin,
				"content":       "```suggestion\n\treturn nil\n```",
				"side":          side,
				"line":          line,
				"path":          "README.md",
				"single_review": "true",
			}
			maps.Copy(values, extra)
			req := NewRequestWithValues(t, "POST", commentURL, values)
			return NewHTMLParser(t, session.MakeRequest(t, req, http.StatusOK).Body)
		}

		for _, origin := range []string{"diff", "timeline"} { // repo/diff/comments.tmpl and view_content/conversation.tmpl
			t.Run(origin, func(t *testing.T) {
				markup := postComment(t, origin, "proposed", "2", nil).Find(".render-content.markup[data-suggestion-original]").First()
				require.Equal(t, 1, markup.Length())
				assert.Equal(t, "\treturn err", markup.AttrOr("data-suggestion-original", ""))
				assert.Equal(t, "Suggested change", markup.AttrOr("data-suggestion-label", ""))
			})
		}

		t.Run("reply in the thread gets the attribute", func(t *testing.T) {
			first := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Comment{IssueID: pr.IssueID, Type: issues_model.CommentTypeCode, Line: 2, TreePath: "README.md"}, unittest.OrderBy("id ASC"))
			doc := postComment(t, "diff", "proposed", "2", map[string]string{"reply": strconv.FormatInt(first.ReviewID, 10)})
			markups := doc.Find(".render-content.markup[data-suggestion-original]")
			assert.Equal(t, doc.Find(".render-content.markup").Length(), markups.Length()) // every comment in the thread, reply included
			assert.Equal(t, "\treturn err", markups.Last().AttrOr("data-suggestion-original", ""))
		})

		t.Run("old side gets no attribute", func(t *testing.T) {
			doc := postComment(t, "diff", "previous", "1", nil)
			require.Equal(t, 1, doc.Find(".render-content.markup code.language-suggestion").Length()) // the comment did render
			assert.Equal(t, 0, doc.Find("[data-suggestion-original]").Length())
		})
	})
}

// Copyright 2026 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

package integration

import (
	"fmt"
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"
	"net/url"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	git_model "gitea.dev/models/git"
	issues_model "gitea.dev/models/issues"
	"gitea.dev/models/unittest"
	user_model "gitea.dev/models/user"
	"gitea.dev/modules/git"
	"gitea.dev/modules/gitrepo"
	issue_service "gitea.dev/services/issue"
	repo_service "gitea.dev/services/repository"
	files_service "gitea.dev/services/repository/files"

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

// The subtests share one pull request and run in order: each later one starts from the branch the earlier ones left.
func TestPullReviewApplySuggestion(t *testing.T) {
	onGiteaRun(t, func(t *testing.T, u *url.URL) {
		user2 := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &user_model.User{ID: 2}) // owns the repository, so can push
		user4 := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &user_model.User{ID: 4}) // signed in, cannot push
		repo, err := repo_service.CreateRepositoryDirectly(t.Context(), user2, user2, repo_service.CreateRepoOptions{
			Name:             "test_apply_suggestion",
			Readme:           "Default",
			AutoInit:         true,
			ObjectFormatName: git.Sha1ObjectFormat.Name(),
			DefaultBranch:    "master",
		}, true)
		require.NoError(t, err)
		_, err = files_service.ChangeRepoFiles(t.Context(), repo, user2, &files_service.ChangeRepoFilesOptions{
			NewBranch: "suggestion-branch",
			Files: []*files_service.ChangeRepoFile{{
				Operation:     "update",
				TreePath:      "README.md",
				ContentReader: strings.NewReader("# Title\n\treturn err\n"),
			}},
		})
		require.NoError(t, err)

		ownerSession := loginUser(t, "user2")
		readerSession := loginUser(t, "user4")
		testPullCreate(t, ownerSession, "user2", "test_apply_suggestion", false, "master", "suggestion-branch", "Suggestion PR")
		pr := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.PullRequest{BaseRepoID: repo.ID, HeadBranch: "suggestion-branch"})
		require.NoError(t, pr.LoadIssue(t.Context()))
		pullURL := fmt.Sprintf("/user2/test_apply_suggestion/pulls/%d", pr.Issue.Index)

		gitRepo, err := gitrepo.OpenRepository(t.Context(), repo)
		require.NoError(t, err)
		defer gitRepo.Close()
		headCommit := func(t *testing.T) *git.Commit {
			commit, err := gitRepo.GetBranchCommit("suggestion-branch")
			require.NoError(t, err)
			return commit
		}
		readme := func(t *testing.T) string {
			blob, err := headCommit(t).GetBlobByPath("README.md")
			require.NoError(t, err)
			content, err := blob.GetBlobContent(1024)
			require.NoError(t, err)
			return content
		}

		// user4 reviews line 2, as #154's tests do
		suggest := func(t *testing.T, content string) *issues_model.Comment {
			req := NewRequestWithValues(t, "POST", pullURL+"/files/reviews/comments", map[string]string{
				"origin":        "diff",
				"content":       content,
				"side":          "proposed",
				"line":          "2",
				"path":          "README.md",
				"single_review": "true",
			})
			readerSession.MakeRequest(t, req, http.StatusOK)
			return unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Comment{IssueID: pr.IssueID, Type: issues_model.CommentTypeCode, Content: content})
		}
		apply := func(t *testing.T, session *TestSession, comment *issues_model.Comment, head, message string, status int) *httptest.ResponseRecorder {
			req := NewRequestWithValues(t, "POST", fmt.Sprintf("%s/files/reviews/comments/%d/apply", pullURL, comment.ID), map[string]string{
				"head_commit_id": head,
				"message":        message,
			})
			return session.MakeRequest(t, req, status)
		}
		errorMessage := func(t *testing.T, resp *httptest.ResponseRecorder) string {
			return DecodeJSON(t, resp, &struct {
				ErrorMessage string `json:"errorMessage"`
			}{}).ErrorMessage
		}
		applyAttrs := func(t *testing.T, session *TestSession, page string) *HTMLDoc {
			return NewHTMLParser(t, session.MakeRequest(t, NewRequest(t, "GET", page), http.StatusOK).Body)
		}

		useNil := suggest(t, "```suggestion\n\treturn nil\n```")
		startHead := headCommit(t).ID.String()

		t.Run("AC1 someone who can push gets Apply with the PR's head and the default message", func(t *testing.T) {
			for _, page := range []string{pullURL + "/files", pullURL} { // Files and Conversation tabs
				markup := applyAttrs(t, ownerSession, page).Find(".render-content.markup[data-suggestion-apply-url]")
				require.Equal(t, 1, markup.Length(), page)
				assert.Equal(t, fmt.Sprintf("%s/files/reviews/comments/%d/apply", pullURL, useNil.ID), markup.AttrOr("data-suggestion-apply-url", ""))
				assert.Equal(t, startHead, markup.AttrOr("data-suggestion-apply-head", ""))
				assert.Equal(t, "Apply suggestion from @user4 on README.md", markup.AttrOr("data-suggestion-apply-message", ""))
			}
		})

		t.Run("AC2 a viewer who cannot push gets no button and a 403", func(t *testing.T) {
			assert.Equal(t, 0, applyAttrs(t, readerSession, pullURL+"/files").Find("[data-suggestion-apply-url]").Length())
			apply(t, readerSession, useNil, startHead, "", http.StatusForbidden)
			assert.Equal(t, startHead, headCommit(t).ID.String())
		})

		t.Run("AC2 a signed-out viewer gets no button and is sent to sign in", func(t *testing.T) {
			anonymous := emptyTestSession(t)
			assert.Equal(t, 0, applyAttrs(t, anonymous, pullURL+"/files").Find("[data-suggestion-apply-url]").Length())
			resp := apply(t, anonymous, useNil, startHead, "", http.StatusSeeOther)
			assert.Contains(t, resp.Header().Get("Location"), "/user/login")
			assert.Equal(t, startHead, headCommit(t).ID.String())
		})

		t.Run("AC7 a comment with two suggestion blocks cannot be applied", func(t *testing.T) {
			twoBlocks := suggest(t, "```suggestion\na\n```\nor\n```suggestion\nb\n```")
			apply(t, ownerSession, twoBlocks, startHead, "", http.StatusNotFound)
			assert.Equal(t, startHead, headCommit(t).ID.String())
		})

		t.Run("AC10 a suggestion identical to the line commits nothing", func(t *testing.T) {
			same := suggest(t, "```suggestion\n\treturn err\n```")
			resp := apply(t, ownerSession, same, startHead, "", http.StatusBadRequest)
			assert.Equal(t, "This suggestion makes no changes to the code.", errorMessage(t, resp))
			assert.Equal(t, startHead, headCommit(t).ID.String())
		})

		t.Run("AC4 an old head commit is refused", func(t *testing.T) {
			baseHead, err := gitRepo.GetBranchCommitID("master")
			require.NoError(t, err)
			resp := apply(t, ownerSession, useNil, baseHead, "", http.StatusBadRequest)
			assert.Equal(t, "This branch has new commits since the page was loaded. Reload the page and try again.", errorMessage(t, resp))
			assert.Equal(t, startHead, headCommit(t).ID.String())
		})

		t.Run("AC6 a protected branch is refused with the web editor's message", func(t *testing.T) {
			require.NoError(t, git_model.UpdateProtectBranch(t.Context(), repo, &git_model.ProtectedBranch{
				RepoID:   repo.ID,
				RuleName: "suggestion-branch",
				CanPush:  false,
			}, git_model.WhitelistOptions{}))
			rule, err := git_model.GetFirstMatchProtectedBranchRule(t.Context(), repo.ID, "suggestion-branch")
			require.NoError(t, err)
			defer func() { require.NoError(t, git_model.DeleteProtectedBranch(t.Context(), repo, rule.ID)) }()

			resp := apply(t, ownerSession, useNil, startHead, "", http.StatusBadRequest)
			assert.Equal(t, `Cannot commit to protected branch "suggestion-branch".`, errorMessage(t, resp))
			assert.Equal(t, startHead, headCommit(t).ID.String())
		})

		coAuthor := fmt.Sprintf("Co-authored-by: %s <%s>", user4.GitName(), user4.GetEmail())

		t.Run("AC1 AC8 applying adds one commit that changes only that line, with the given message", func(t *testing.T) {
			apply(t, ownerSession, useNil, startHead, "Return nil instead", http.StatusOK)
			commit := headCommit(t)
			require.Equal(t, 1, commit.ParentCount())
			parent, err := commit.ParentID(0)
			require.NoError(t, err)
			assert.Equal(t, startHead, parent.String())
			assert.Equal(t, "# Title\n\treturn nil\n", readme(t))
			assert.Equal(t, "Return nil instead\n\n"+coAuthor, strings.TrimSpace(commit.CommitMessage))
			// customer question 1's default: the person who applied it authors and commits
			assert.Equal(t, user2.GetEmail(), commit.Author.Email)
			assert.Equal(t, user2.GetEmail(), commit.Committer.Email)
		})

		t.Run("AC1 an empty message gets the default", func(t *testing.T) {
			before := headCommit(t).ID.String()
			addComment := suggest(t, "```suggestion\n\treturn nil // done\n```")
			apply(t, ownerSession, addComment, before, "", http.StatusOK)
			assert.Equal(t, "# Title\n\treturn nil // done\n", readme(t))
			assert.Equal(t, "Apply suggestion from @user4 on README.md\n\n"+coAuthor, strings.TrimSpace(headCommit(t).CommitMessage))
		})

		t.Run("AC3 a suggestion whose line has changed is outdated", func(t *testing.T) {
			before := headCommit(t).ID.String()
			resp := apply(t, ownerSession, useNil, before, "", http.StatusBadRequest) // written against "\treturn err"
			assert.Equal(t, "This suggestion is outdated: the code changed since it was written.", errorMessage(t, resp))
			assert.Equal(t, before, headCommit(t).ID.String())
		})

		t.Run("AC5 a closed pull request gets no button and an error", func(t *testing.T) {
			before := headCommit(t).ID.String()
			pending := suggest(t, "```suggestion\n\treturn nil // closed\n```")
			require.NoError(t, issue_service.CloseIssue(t.Context(), pr.Issue, user2, ""))
			assert.Equal(t, 0, applyAttrs(t, ownerSession, pullURL+"/files").Find("[data-suggestion-apply-url]").Length())
			resp := apply(t, ownerSession, pending, before, "", http.StatusBadRequest)
			assert.Equal(t, "Suggestions can only be applied to an open pull request whose branch still exists.", errorMessage(t, resp))
			assert.Equal(t, before, headCommit(t).ID.String())
		})
	})
}

func (c *CommitMessage) MessageUTF8() string {
	if c.messageUTF8 == nil {
		bs := charset.ToUTF8(util.UnsafeStringToBytes(c.MessageRaw), charset.ConvertOpts{ErrorReplacement: []byte{'?'}})
		c.messageUTF8 = new(util.UnsafeBytesToString(bs))
	}
	return *c.messageUTF8
}

func (c *CommitMessage) MessageTitle() string {
	if c.messageTitle == nil {
		s, _, _ := strings.Cut(strings.TrimSpace(c.MessageUTF8()), "\n")
		c.messageTitle = new(strings.TrimSpace(s))

The integration test compiles. Steps 3 and 4 are written and the whole tree builds and vets cleanly, but nothing has run end to end. Integration tests need WSL, and `wsync` only sees committed work, so I need your OK for a local commit before I can run them.

**Step 3, the service (`services/repository/files/suggestion.go`):**
- **`CanApplySuggestions(ctx, doer, pr)`** checks everything that doesn't depend on the comment, and returns the head commit:
  - the PR is open, not merged, and created the normal way, not with AGit (AC5);
  - the head repo and branch still exist (AC5);
  - the user can write to the head branch, using the head repo's permission and including "Allow edits from maintainers" (AC2).
- **`ApplySuggestion`** runs the rest in order:
  - the comment belongs to this PR, is on the new side, and has exactly one block (AC7);
  - the head commit matches the page's (AC4);
  - branch protection, using the web editor's own check (AC6);
  - it reads the file at the head; a deleted or renamed file counts as outdated (AC3);
  - the step 2 line replacement (AC3, AC10, AC11, AC12);
  - then it commits through `ChangeRepoFiles`.

  An empty message gets the default. When the reviewer isn't the person applying, a `Co-authored-by:` trailer is added (AC8's default), using the reviewer's no-reply address if they keep their email private.
- **New errors** for each outcome, plus `Comment.SuggestionCommitMessage()`, which the service and the templates share so the default message can't differ between them.

**Step 4, route, handler and templates:**
- **Route:** `POST …/pulls/{index}/files/reviews/comments/{id}/apply` with `reqSignIn`, in the review group that already blocks archived repos. The form takes `head_commit_id` (required) and `message`.
- **Handler responses:**
  - success: 200 (JSON OK);
  - AC2, viewer can't push: **403**;
  - AC7, nothing to apply: **404**;
  - AC3, AC4, AC5 and AC10: **400** with the spec's exact message;
  - AC6: 400 with the web editor's `Cannot commit to protected branch "…".`;
  - anything else, such as a pre-receive hook rejection, goes through the web editor's existing error handler.
- **Where the template data is set:** `prepareSuggestionApply` sets the head commit and apply link for the Files tab (`viewPullFiles`), the Conversation tab (`issue_view.go`) and a newly posted comment (`renderConversation`).
- **Templates:** both comment templates add the apply URL, head commit, default message and four button labels next to #154's attributes. They do this only when #154 marked the comment as a suggestion, the viewer may apply, and the comment isn't outdated (AC9).
- **Locale:** 7 new keys in `locale_en-US.json`. The four error messages are copied from the ACs.

**Integration test `TestPullReviewApplySuggestion`** (written by Claude Code; expected values from the ACs). It has one shared PR. user4 (can't push) writes the suggestions and user2 (owner) applies them. Its 11 subtests, in order:
1. AC1: the owner sees the attributes on both tabs, with the right head commit and default message.
2. AC2: user4 sees no button and gets a 403.
3. AC2: a signed-out viewer sees no button and is redirected to sign-in.
4. AC7: two blocks gives a 404.
5. AC10: an identical line gives a 400.
6. AC4: an old head commit gives a 400.
7. AC6: a protected branch gives a 400.
8. AC1 + AC8: one new commit, changing only that line, with the custom message, the reviewer's `Co-authored-by` trailer, and user2 as author and committer.
9. AC1: an empty message gives the default.
10. AC3: the first suggestion is now outdated.
11. AC5: a closed PR shows no button and the POST gets a 400.

Each refusal also checks that the branch didn't move.

**Gaps:**
- **Comments shown by expanding hidden diff context get no button.** That view (`ExcerptBlob`) renders comments through the same template, but its handler doesn't set the data. The comment still renders as #154 draws it.
- **AC9 isn't integration-tested.** Comments are marked outdated by a background queue after a push, so a test that waits for that would be slow and flaky. The template condition (`not .Invalidated`) covers it.
- **The deleted-or-renamed-file case of AC3 is in the code but not tested.** Line past the end and changed line are unit-tested in step 2.
- **The integration test will likely take much more than 2 seconds.** #154's took about 9s for repo and PR setup. I'll report the real time.

import {initMarkupCodeSuggestion} from './suggestion.ts';

function makeMarkup(attrs: Record<string, string>, body: string): HTMLElement {
  const el = document.createElement('div');
  el.className = 'render-content markup';
  for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(attrs)) el.setAttribute(k, v);
  el.innerHTML = body;
  return el;
}

function codeBlock(text: string, lang = 'suggestion'): string {
  return `<div class="code-block-container code-overflow-scroll"><pre class="code-block"><code class="chroma language-${lang} display">${text}</code></pre></div>`;
}

const attrs = {'data-suggestion-original': '\treturn err', 'data-suggestion-label': 'Suggested change'};

function rows(el: Element) {
  return Array.from(el.querySelectorAll('.markup-suggestion-line'), (row) => ({
    kind: row.classList.contains('removed') ? 'removed' : 'added',
    text: row.querySelector('code')!.textContent,
  }));
}

test('renders the original line as removed and each block line as added', () => {
  const el = makeMarkup(attrs, `<p>try this</p>${codeBlock('\treturn fmt.Errorf("x: %w", err)\n\treturn nil\n')}`);
  initMarkupCodeSuggestion(el);
  expect(el.querySelector('.code-block-container')).toBeNull();
  const diff = el.querySelector('.markup-suggestion')!;
  expect(diff.querySelector('.markup-suggestion-header')!.textContent).toEqual('Suggested change');
  expect(rows(diff)).toEqual([
    {kind: 'removed', text: '\treturn err'},
    {kind: 'added', text: '\treturn fmt.Errorf("x: %w", err)'},
    {kind: 'added', text: '\treturn nil'},
  ]);
  expect(el.querySelector('p')!.textContent).toEqual('try this');
});

test('empty block only removes the line', () => {
  const el = makeMarkup(attrs, codeBlock(''));
  initMarkupCodeSuggestion(el);
  expect(rows(el)).toEqual([{kind: 'removed', text: '\treturn err'}]);
});

test('one blank line replaces the line with a blank line', () => {
  const el = makeMarkup(attrs, codeBlock('\n')); // what the renderer emits for a fence holding one blank line
  initMarkupCodeSuggestion(el);
  expect(rows(el)).toEqual([{kind: 'removed', text: '\treturn err'}, {kind: 'added', text: ''}]);
});

test('capitalised Suggestion is an ordinary code block', () => {
  const el = makeMarkup(attrs, codeBlock('x\n', 'Suggestion'));
  initMarkupCodeSuggestion(el);
  expect(el.querySelector('.markup-suggestion')).toBeNull();
});

test('each block gets its own diff against the same line', () => {
  const el = makeMarkup(attrs, codeBlock('a\n') + codeBlock('b\n'));
  initMarkupCodeSuggestion(el);
  const diffs = el.querySelectorAll('.markup-suggestion');
  expect(diffs).toHaveLength(2);
  expect(rows(diffs[1])).toEqual([{kind: 'removed', text: '\treturn err'}, {kind: 'added', text: 'b'}]);
});

test('HTML in a suggestion stays text', () => {
  const el = makeMarkup(attrs, codeBlock('&lt;img src=x onerror=alert(1)&gt;\n'));
  initMarkupCodeSuggestion(el);
  expect(el.querySelector('img')).toBeNull();
  expect(rows(el)[1].text).toEqual('<img src=x onerror=alert(1)>');
});

test('without the attribute nothing changes', () => {
  const el = makeMarkup({}, codeBlock('x\n'));
  const before = el.innerHTML;
  initMarkupCodeSuggestion(el);
  expect(el.innerHTML).toEqual(before);
});

test('other languages are left alone', () => {
  const el = makeMarkup(attrs, codeBlock('x\n', 'go'));
  initMarkupCodeSuggestion(el);
  expect(el.querySelector('.markup-suggestion')).toBeNull();
});
