# Claude in Chrome browser automation

You have access to browser automation tools (mcp__claude-in-chrome__*) for interacting with web pages in Chrome. Follow these guidelines for effective browser automation.

## Loading deferred tools

If the mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load every tool you expect to need in ONE ToolSearch call — the select query accepts a comma-separated list — never one call per tool. Start with the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting.

## GIF recording

When performing multi-step browser interactions that the user may want to review or share, use mcp__claude-in-chrome__gif_creator to record them.

You must ALWAYS:
* Capture extra frames before and after taking actions to ensure smooth playback
* Name the file meaningfully to help the user identify it later (e.g., "login_process.gif")

## Console log debugging

You can use mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_console_messages to read console output. Console output may be verbose. If you are looking for specific log entries, use the 'pattern' parameter with a regex-compatible pattern. This filters results efficiently and avoids overwhelming output. For example, use pattern: "[MyApp]" to filter for application-specific logs rather than reading all console output.

## Alerts and dialogs

IMPORTANT: Do not trigger JavaScript alerts, confirms, prompts, or browser modal dialogs through your actions. These browser dialogs block all further browser events and will prevent the extension from receiving any subsequent commands. Instead, when possible, use console.log for debugging and then use the mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_console_messages tool to read those log messages. If a page has dialog-triggering elements:
1. Avoid clicking buttons or links that may trigger alerts (e.g., "Delete" buttons with confirmation dialogs)
2. If you must interact with such elements, warn the user first that this may interrupt the session
3. Use mcp__claude-in-chrome__javascript_tool to check for and dismiss any existing dialogs before proceeding

If you accidentally trigger a dialog and lose responsiveness, inform the user they need to manually dismiss it in the browser.

## Avoid rabbit holes and loops

When using browser automation tools, stay focused on the specific task. If you encounter any of the following, stop and ask the user for guidance:
- Unexpected complexity or tangential browser exploration
- Browser tool calls failing or returning errors after 2-3 attempts
- No response from the browser extension
- Page elements not responding to clicks or input
- Pages not loading or timing out
- Unable to complete the browser task despite multiple approaches

Explain what you attempted, what went wrong, and ask how the user would like to proceed. Do not keep retrying the same failing browser action or explore unrelated pages without checking in first.

## Tab context and session startup

IMPORTANT: At the start of each browser automation session, call mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp first to get information about the user's current browser tabs. Use this context to understand what the user might want to work with before creating new tabs.

Never reuse tab IDs from a previous/other session. Follow these guidelines:
1. Only reuse an existing tab if the user explicitly asks to work with it
2. Otherwise, create a new tab with mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp
3. If a tool returns an error indicating the tab doesn't exist or is invalid, call tabs_context_mcp to get fresh tab IDs
4. When a tab is closed by the user or a navigation error occurs, call tabs_context_mcp to see what tabs are available

args — `wsl -d Debian --exec bash -c '...' name args` passes them intact. `~/.bashrc` returns early
for non-interactive shells, so scripts must export the toolchain PATH themselves.
`~/gitea/custom/conf/app.ini` runs a WSL Gitea on 127.0.0.1:3001 (SQLite) for PR reviews.

Toolchain installed under `$HOME/.local` (no sudo): Go 1.26.4 (`~/.local/go`), Node 26.7.0
(`~/.local/node`), pnpm 11.9.0 via corepack 0.36.0, plus apt `make` 4.3, `libatomic1`, `curl`,
`xz-utils`. `~/.bashrc` exports the PATH and `CGO_ENABLED=0` under a `# gitea-toolchain` marker.

**Measured 2026-09-03 — WSL is dramatically faster for Go tooling:**
| task | Windows | WSL2 |
|---|---|---|
| `make lint-go` | 75 min → timeout, then 23 min → killed | **3m42s, "0 issues"** |
| `TAGS=bindata make generate-go` | 2m13s | **9s** |
| `make build` (frontend+backend) | ~4 min backend only | **2m28s** total |

**How to apply:** run tests and lint (`make lint-go`, `make test-backend`, vitest, `make test-e2e`) in
WSL via `wsync <cmd>`. Carson now runs the Gitea app from WSL too (Windows app on :3000 retired). See [[gitea-lint-on-windows]] for why, and [[gitea-toolchain-setup]] for the Windows side.

**`make lint-templates` needs `uv`** (2026-10-01): apt `pipx` installed (as root), then `pipx install uv`
as carsonrackley → `~/.local/bin/uv`. `wsync-wsl`'s PATH line omits `~/.local/bin`, so run
`wsync bash -c 'PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH" make lint-templates'` unless Carson adds it to the script.
Root also has a stray uv in `/root/.local/bin` (unused). `make lint-json` fails in `~/gitea` while the
local server has written `data/indexers/*.json` (gitignored runtime data) — not a code problem.

`make frontend` only rebuilds when `web_src/` or the vite/tailwind configs change, NOT templates. A
new `tw-*` class used only in a `.tmpl` renders at 0px until you `wsync rm -f
public/assets/.vite/manifest.json && wsync make frontend` and restart `./gitea web`.

Note: running `wsl.exe -- bash -c '...'` from the Claude Bash tool mangles quotes; write the script
to the scratchpad and run `wsl.exe -d Debian -- bash /mnt/c/...`, with `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1` set.
```

wsl-status.sh
set -e
cd ~/gitea
B=http://127.0.0.1:3001/api/v1
CREDS=/mnt/c/Users/carso/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/7ba6e69ad1da6bbf/7264a519-9b2f-4a91-9af2-12e5eefa19a8/scratchpad/sugg-demo-creds.txt

echo "--- restart server on the new binary"
pkill -f "gitea web" || true
sleep 2
setsid nohup ./gitea web > /tmp/gitea-web.log 2>&1 < /dev/null &
for i in $(seq 1 60); do [ "$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://127.0.0.1:3001/)" = 200 ] && break; sleep 1; done
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "server: %{http_code}\n" http://127.0.0.1:3001/

echo "--- users"
: > "$CREDS"
for u in sugg-owner sugg-reviewer sugg-forker; do
  p="Sg-$(head -c 24 /dev/urandom | base64 | tr -dc A-Za-z0-9 | head -c 16)"
  ./gitea --config custom/conf/app.ini admin user create --username "$u" --password "$p" --email "$u@demo.localhost" --must-change-password=false >/dev/null
  echo "$u $p" >> "$CREDS"
done
OWN="sugg-owner:$(awk '/^sugg-owner /{print $2}' "$CREDS")"
REV="sugg-reviewer:$(awk '/^sugg-reviewer /{print $2}' "$CREDS")"
FRK="sugg-forker:$(awk '/^sugg-forker /{print $2}' "$CREDS")"
api() { curl -s -f -u "$1" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -X "$2" "$B$3" -d "$4"; }
b64() { printf '%b' "$1" | base64 -w0; }

echo "--- repo with app.go and a CRLF file on main"
api "$OWN" POST /user/repos '{"name":"suggest-demo","auto_init":true,"default_branch":"main"}' >/dev/null
api "$OWN" POST /repos/sugg-owner/suggest-demo/contents "{\"branch\":\"main\",\"message\":\"add files\",\"files\":[{\"operation\":\"create\",\"path\":\"app.go\",\"content\":\"$(b64 'package main\n\nfunc run() error {\n\treturn nil\n}\n')\"},{\"operation\":\"create\",\"path\":\"crlf.txt\",\"content\":\"$(b64 'one\r\ntwo\r\nthree\r\n')\"}]}" >/dev/null

echo "--- feature branch changes both files, PR #1"
api "$OWN" POST /repos/sugg-owner/suggest-demo/contents "{\"branch\":\"main\",\"new_branch\":\"feature\",\"message\":\"change both\",\"files\":[{\"operation\":\"update\",\"path\":\"app.go\",\"sha\":\"$(api "$OWN" GET /repos/sugg-owner/suggest-demo/contents/app.go '' | sed -n 's/.*"sha":"\([0-9a-f]*\)".*/\1/p' | head -1)\",\"content\":\"$(b64 'package main\n\nfunc run() error {\n\treturn err\n}\n')\"},{\"operation\":\"update\",\"path\":\"crlf.txt\",\"sha\":\"$(api "$OWN" GET /repos/sugg-owner/suggest-demo/contents/crlf.txt '' | sed -n 's/.*"sha":"\([0-9a-f]*\)".*/\1/p' | head -1)\",\"content\":\"$(b64 'one\r\ntwo!\r\nthree\r\n')\"}]}" >/dev/null
api "$OWN" POST /repos/sugg-owner/suggest-demo/pulls '{"head":"feature","base":"main","title":"Same-repo PR for suggestions"}' | sed -n 's/.*"number":\([0-9]*\).*/PR number: \1/p' | head -1

echo "--- reviewer suggests on both files"
api "$REV" POST /repos/sugg-owner/suggest-demo/pulls/1/reviews '{"event":"COMMENT","body":"","comments":[{"path":"app.go","new_position":4,"body":"Return nil here:\n```suggestion\n\treturn nil\n```"},{"path":"crlf.txt","new_position":2,"body":"```suggestion\nTWO\n```"}]}' | sed -n 's/.*"comments_count":\([0-9]*\).*/review comments: \1/p'

echo "--- fork PR with maintainer edits on"
api "$FRK" POST /repos/sugg-owner/suggest-demo/forks '{}' >/dev/null
sleep 2
api "$FRK" POST /repos/sugg-forker/suggest-demo/contents "{\"branch\":\"main\",\"new_branch\":\"fork-feature\",\"message\":\"fork change\",\"files\":[{\"operation\":\"update\",\"path\":\"app.go\",\"sha\":\"$(api "$FRK" GET /repos/sugg-forker/suggest-demo/contents/app.go '' | sed -n 's/.*"sha":"\([0-9a-f]*\)".*/\1/p' | head -1)\",\"content\":\"$(b64 'package main\n\nfunc run() error {\n\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"x\")\n}\n')\"}]}" >/dev/null
api "$FRK" POST /repos/sugg-owner/suggest-demo/pulls '{"head":"sugg-forker:fork-feature","base":"main","title":"Fork PR for suggestions"}' | sed -n 's/.*"number":\([0-9]*\).*/PR number: \1/p' | head -1
api "$FRK" PATCH /repos/sugg-owner/suggest-demo/pulls/2 '{"allow_maintainer_edit":true}' | grep -o '"allow_maintainer_edit":[a-z]*'
api "$OWN" POST /repos/sugg-owner/suggest-demo/pulls/2/reviews '{"event":"COMMENT","body":"","comments":[{"path":"app.go","new_position":4,"body":"```suggestion\n\treturn errors.New(\"x\")\n```"}]}' | sed -n 's/.*"comments_count":\([0-9]*\).*/fork review comments: \1/p'
echo "--- done"

Closes #118

## What changed

- **Tab icon badge.** `favicon-status.ts` now knows about two badges that can own the tab icon: an Actions run's status and a new unread-notification dot. A single `renderFavicon()` picks one (run status first, then the dot, then the default icon). The dot reuses the run badge's position and white ring, and is filled with `--color-primary` so it matches the navbar's unread bubble. `RepoActionView.vue` is unchanged.
- **Desktop notification opt-in.** A new **Enable desktop notifications** button on the Notifications page (`notification_div.tmpl`, wired in `features/notification-desktop.ts`). The choice is stored per browser in `localUserSettings`. The browser's permission prompt is only requested from that click, and a denial shows "Desktop notifications are blocked by your browser." Clicking it again disables alerts.
- **One alert across tabs.** Every Gitea tab already shares one event stream through `eventsource.sharedworker.ts`. Tabs now tell the worker whether they are visible and what their count is. When the count goes up and no Gitea tab is visible, the worker asks exactly one tab (the one used most recently) to show the alert. The decision logic is a small DOM-free class in `modules/notification-alert.ts` so it can be unit tested.
- **Alert content.** Only a count ("You have N new notification(s)", counting since Gitea was last in view); clicking it focuses Gitea and opens `/notifications`. The text reaches every page as `data-` attributes on the navbar count.
- **Polling fallback.** When the shared worker or event stream is unavailable, a hidden tab that sees the count go up alerts on its own; all alerts share one notification tag so the browser shows one.
- New locale keys in `locale_en-US.json` only.

## Why

Users who leave Gitea in a background tab don't notice review requests and mentions until they switch back. This adds a passive badge (AC1, AC2) and opt-in, count-only desktop alerts that never prompt on their own, fire once across tabs and only when Gitea isn't visible (AC3–AC9).

## Test Evidence

| Acceptance criterion | Test(s) | Level | Source of expected value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AC1: badge dot while unread, default icon back at 0 without a reload | `favicon-status.test.ts`: "AC1 unread notifications add a dot and reading them all restores the default icon"; "the dot uses the primary color". Manual: new notification took the count 0→1 live and both favicon links got the dot; marking all read took it to 0 and restored `favicon.svg`/`favicon.png` with no navigation; loading a repo page with 1 unread showed the dot on load | unit, manual | AC; Decision 3 (dot, same color as navbar badge) |
| AC2: run status wins over the badge on an Actions run page | `favicon-status.test.ts`: "AC2 an Actions run status wins over the dot, and the dot returns when the run page is left"; "AC2 leaving a run page with nothing unread restores the default icon". Manual: on a waiting run with 1 unread the icon showed `waiting`, and it stayed `waiting` when the count rose to 2 live | unit, manual | AC; Decision 3 |
| AC3: never enabled → no alert, no prompt on its own | `notification-desktop.test.ts`: "AC3 never enabled: no alert and no permission prompt"; "AC3 permission granted for something else does not turn alerts on by itself". Manual: permission stayed `default` until the button was clicked | unit, manual | AC; Decision 1 (alternative b rejected) |
| AC4: denied → page says blocked, setting stays off | `notification-desktop.test.ts`: "AC4 denying the browser prompt says it is blocked and leaves the setting off". Manual: clicked Enable, blocked Chrome's prompt; blocked message shown, setting `false`, still shown after reload | unit, manual | AC |
| AC5: hidden tab, count up → one count-only alert | `notification-alert.test.ts`: "AC5 a count increase while every tab is hidden alerts once…"; `notification-desktop.test.ts`: "AC5 the alert says how many new notifications there are and nothing else". Manual: both tabs hidden, 3→4 gave one alert, body "You have 1 new notification" | unit, manual | AC; Decision 2 |
| AC6: several tabs → one alert | `notification-alert.test.ts`: "AC6 several hidden tabs get one alert, sent to the tab used last". Manual: two hidden Gitea tabs, one alert in total, from the tab used last | unit, manual | AC |
| AC7: visible tab, same or lower count → no alert | `notification-alert.test.ts`: "AC7 no alert while any Gitea tab is visible"; "AC7 no alert when the count stays the same or goes down". Manual: count rose while tabs were visible, no alert; count fell 4→0 while hidden, no alert | unit, manual | AC |
| AC8: clicking the alert focuses Gitea and opens `/notifications` | `notification-desktop.test.ts`: "AC8 clicking the alert focuses Gitea and opens the notifications page". Manual: dispatched the alert's click event; the tab moved from the issues list to `/notifications` | unit, manual | AC |
| AC9: disable → no more alerts | `notification-desktop.test.ts`: "AC9 disabling stops further alerts". Manual: clicked Disable (permission still granted), hidden count rise gave no alert | unit, manual | AC |

Also checked manually: with `EVENT_SOURCE_UPDATE_TIME = -1` (polling fallback), a hidden tab that polled showed the same count-only alert (issue's Open Question 2).

**Not tested automatically, and why:** the shared-worker wiring (tabs reporting visibility, the worker routing `notification-alert` to one tab) has no automated test: it needs real browser tabs with real visibility, and an E2E test would need permission grants across several tabs. Its decision logic is unit tested in `notification-alert.test.ts`, and the wiring was checked manually for AC5–AC7 and AC9 above. Manual counts were taken by wrapping `window.Notification` in each tab to record every alert created.

**AI-written tests:** all tests above were written by Claude Code: the four new tests in `web_src/js/modules/favicon-status.test.ts`, and the new files `web_src/js/modules/notification-alert.test.ts` and `web_src/js/features/notification-desktop.test.ts`. Expected values come from the issue's ACs and Design Decisions (dot color, run status precedence, count-only text, per-browser opt-in), not from running the code. I checked each assertion against the AC it names. Commit 9c59e00 (also Claude Code) only changes test setup and cleanup: `notification.test.ts` turns the dot off after each test, and `favicon-status.test.ts` resets both badges before each test. No expected value changed.

## CI / manual verification

Ran in WSL on the branch head:

- `pnpm exec vitest run`: 65 files, 405 tests passed
- `make lint-js` (eslint + vue-tsc): passed
- `make lint-templates`: 578 files, 0 errors
- no trailing whitespace in the commit
- after 9c59e00: `pnpm exec vitest run` passed all 66 files; `notification.test.ts` then `favicon-status.test.ts` in one worker (`--no-file-parallelism`), the order that failed CI, passes (it failed before the commit); eslint on both files passes

Manual browser checks against a local build (`make build`, SQLite) are in the Test Evidence table.

## Design

Follows the three Design Decisions in #118: per-browser opt-in in local storage, count-only alerts, and a dot badge where Actions run status takes precedence. Added during implementation: the shared worker decides which tab alerts, so a visible Gitea tab suppresses alerts from hidden ones.

## Tech Debt

**Introduced:** The polling fallback can't coordinate tabs, so two hidden tabs that both detect an increase each create an alert. They share a notification tag, so the browser shows one, but a visible tab in the same browser doesn't suppress them. The shared-worker path only has manual test coverage.

**Encountered:** `UserEventsSharedWorker` closes its port on `beforeunload`, which can be cancelled (existing FIXME in `modules/worker.ts`). A tab whose unload is cancelled may stop reporting to the worker. Left as is, since it predates this change and also affects the stopwatch. The worker class also had no way to send a message without reaching into `sharedWorker.port`; I added a small `postMessage` method. Vitest's `isolate: false` lets test files share module state: this PR's `notification.test.ts` leaked the unread dot into `favicon-status.test.ts` (fixed here), and a pre-existing flaky pair, `shortcut.test.ts` and `repo-issue-edit.test.ts`, can fail the `sonarqube` job and with it the SonarCloud gate. That pair is tracked in #171.

## AI assistance

Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5) helped plan the design after I located the concept files (`notification.ts`, `favicon-status.ts`, `notification_div.tmpl`), wrote the implementation and the tests, ran lint and tests, and drove the manual browser checks with Claude in Chrome. I chose the cross-tab approach and badge color, approved each commit, handled the browser permission prompts myself, reviewed every change, and can explain each line. AI log: see the AI Assistance comment on the linked issue.

S3. Apply a single suggestion as a commit on the PR branch
Sprint 3
### User Story

Labels: `enhancement`, `scope: medium` · Type: Feature · Part of #151 · Depends on #154 (S1, merged in #168)

## User Story
As a PR author, I want to apply a reviewer's suggestion with one click so that Gitea commits the
change to my branch and I don't retype it.

### User Scenario

Ben sees Ana's suggestion and clicks **Apply suggestion**. A small form shows a default commit
message, "Apply suggestion from @ana on main.go", which he keeps. He confirms. The page reloads,
the PR has one more commit changing line 18, and the Files tab shows the new code.

### Acceptance Criteria

Errors from the Apply POST are returned the way Gitea's other web forms return them: HTTP 400 with
the message shown on the page, unless an AC says otherwise.

- [ ] AC1: Given a suggestion on a single line, in a review comment or a reply in its thread, and
  a user who can push to the head branch, when they apply it, then exactly one commit is added to
  the head branch that replaces only that line, exactly as #154's diff shows it (AC12). The form
  is prefilled with the default message "Apply suggestion from @<reviewer> on <file>" and can be
  edited: the commit uses the submitted message, or the default if the message is submitted
  empty.
- [ ] AC2: Given a viewer who can't push to the head branch (read-only, or a fork PR without
  "Allow edits from maintainers"), when the PR is shown, then there is no Apply button, and a
  direct POST returns 403 and commits nothing (#151 AC3). A signed-out viewer sees no Apply
  button, and a direct POST redirects to sign-in and commits nothing. *Pending customer question 2
  on #151; see Open Questions for the default.*
- [ ] AC3: Given the commented line's text at the current head differs from the line the
  suggestion was written against, or the file was deleted or renamed at head, or the line number
  is now past the end of the file, when someone applies it, then nothing is committed and they see
  "This suggestion is outdated: the code changed since it was written."
- [ ] AC4: Given the head branch moved between page load and Apply (someone pushed, or another
  suggestion was applied), when Apply is submitted with the old head SHA, then nothing is
  committed and they see "This branch has new commits since the page was loaded. Reload the page
  and try again." This holds whether or not the new commits touched the suggestion's file. The
  head SHA sent is the PR's head when the page loaded, even when the Files tab is showing a single
  earlier commit.
- [ ] AC5: Given the PR is closed or merged, its head branch was deleted, or it was created with
  AGit flow (so it has no head branch), when the PR is shown, then there is no Apply button, and a direct POST commits nothing and returns 400 with
  "Suggestions can only be applied to an open pull request whose branch still exists."
- [ ] AC6: Given the head branch is protected against this user's push, when they apply, then
  nothing is committed and they see Gitea's existing message `Cannot commit to protected branch
  "<branch>".` (the same check and text as the web editor), not the raw pre-receive output.
- [ ] AC7: Given a comment with zero or several suggestion blocks, or a comment on an old-side
  (deleted) line, which #154 AC7 renders as an ordinary code block, when shown, then there is no
  Apply button.
- [ ] AC8: The commit's author and committer follow the customer's answer to question 1, and a
  test asserts them. *Pending customer question 1 on #151; see Open Questions for the default.*
- [ ] AC9: Given an outdated review comment (its code changed in a later push), when shown, then
  its suggestion has no Apply button. A POST from a page loaded before the change is handled by
  AC3/AC4.
- [ ] AC10: Given a suggestion identical to the current line, when someone applies it, then no
  commit is made and they see "This suggestion makes no changes to the code."
- [ ] AC11: Given a file with CRLF line endings or no final newline, when a suggestion on it is
  applied, then the changed line keeps the file's line ending and the file's final-newline state
  is unchanged; no other byte of the file changes.
- [ ] AC12: Given the suggestion block is empty, has one blank line, or has several lines, when it
  is applied, then the commit deletes the line, replaces it with a blank line, or replaces it with
  those lines in order, matching #154 AC2's diff. No line before or after it changes.

### Out of Scope

- Several suggestions at once (S6); API (S7); recording "applied" state (S4).
- Suggestions on old-side (deleted) lines (customer question 5): they render as plain code blocks
  in #154, so there is nothing to apply. If the customer allows them, that's a follow-up issue.
- Resolving the review conversation on apply (customer question 3).
- Applying without JavaScript: like #154's no-JavaScript fallback, the suggestion is then a plain
  code block with no Apply button.
- Suggestions spanning several commented lines (S5). A one-line comment whose block has several
  lines is in scope (AC12).
- AGit-flow pull requests (pushed to `refs/for/...`): there is no head branch to commit to, so they
  get no Apply button (AC5).

### Open Questions

- **Customer question 1 (commit author)**, for AC8: unanswered on #151. If there is no answer by
  Nov 16, the default is: the person who applied it is author and committer, with a
  `Co-authored-by:` trailer for the reviewer who wrote the suggestion.
- **Customer question 2 (who may apply)**, for AC2: unanswered on #151. Default if no answer by
  Nov 16: anyone who can push to the head branch, including maintainers on a fork PR with "Allow
  edits from maintainers" on.
- **Customer question 4 (applying your own suggestion):** unanswered on #151. Default if no answer
  by Nov 16: allowed; the permission rule in AC2 is the only check.
- ~~Should the Apply form allow editing the commit message?~~ Resolved: editable, prefilled with
  the default (AC1).

### Design Decision

**Decision:** A new `ApplySuggestion(ctx, doer, comment, expectedHeadSHA, message)` in
`services/repository/files`, next to `ChangeRepoFiles`, that first checks that `expectedHeadSHA` is
still the head branch's commit (AC4) and that the doer may commit to the branch, using the same
protected-branch check the web editor builds its `CanCommitToBranch` from
(`GetFirstMatchProtectedBranchRule` and `CanUserPush`; AC6). It then reads the file at the current head, checks the target line still matches
`Comment.SuggestionOriginalLine()` from #154 (ignoring a trailing `\r` on both sides, so CRLF files
compare correctly), replaces it with the block's lines, and commits through
`ChangeRepoFiles` with
`LastCommitID = expectedHeadSHA`. Permission is checked with the same head-branch write check the
web editor uses for PR branches, including `AllowMaintainerEdit`.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- *Apply with `git apply` on a patch built from the suggestion, in a temporary clone.* Handles
  fuzz, but fuzzy application can land the change on the wrong line, and it duplicates what
  `ChangeRepoFiles` already does (temp repo, hooks, protection checks, push).
- *Just replace line N without comparing contents.* Simple, but silently overwrites code if the
  file changed since the review (AC3).
- *Rely on `ChangeRepoFiles`'s `LastCommitID` check alone for AC4.* That check only fails when the
  same file changed since `LastCommitID` (`services/repository/files/update.go:393`). If another
  file changed, it commits on the stale parent and the push is rejected as out of date, which the
  web editor reports with its generic "file contents have changed" message, not AC4's.
- *Put `ApplySuggestion` in `services/pull` (this decision's first version).* `services/repository/files`
  already imports `services/pull` (`update.go`, `cherry_pick.go`), so `services/pull` calling
  `ChangeRepoFiles` would be an import cycle, which Go does not allow.

**Rationale:** `ChangeRepoFiles` already runs hooks, re-checks branch protection on push and
handles the temp repo, so only the suggestion-specific checks are new. Checking the head SHA and
`CanCommitToBranch` up front gives AC4 and AC6 their own messages instead of whatever the push
returns. Comparing line contents makes outdated suggestions fail safe.

**Consequences:** Applying a suggestion triggers the normal push path (CI, PR recheck,
`InvalidateCodeComments`). A suggestion whose line moved but didn't change is refused rather than
re-located; a later issue could add re-anchoring. Any push to the branch, even one unrelated to
the suggestion's file, makes an open page's Apply fail with AC4 until it is reloaded.

### Decision 2: reading suggestion blocks on the server

**Decision:** Add `Comment.SuggestionBlocks()` in `models/issues/comment_suggestion.go`, next to
#154's `SuggestionOriginalLine()`. It parses `Comment.Content` with Gitea's own goldmark markdown
parser and returns the text of each fenced code block whose first info word is exactly
`suggestion`. The Apply POST reads the suggested text from it (the client never sends the text),
and AC7's "exactly one block" rule counts with it. S4 and S6 can reuse it.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- *A line scanner or regex over the raw markdown.* Simpler and faster, but it can disagree with
  the rendered page on fences inside lists or blockquotes, `~~~` fences, longer fences and info
  strings (#154 AC9), so Apply could commit something other than the diff on screen.
- *Have the browser send the suggestion text with the POST.* No parser needed, but the commit would
  hold whatever the request says rather than what the comment says.

**Rationale:** Only goldmark is guaranteed to find the same blocks the page renders, so what the
reader sees is what gets committed.

**Consequences:** Parsing the comment costs a markdown parse per Apply and per comment shown with
an Apply button. The parser lives in the model package and must be kept in step with any future
change to how #154 recognises suggestion blocks.

### Decision 3: where the Apply button comes from

**Decision:** The server adds a `data-suggestion-apply-url` attribute and the PR's head SHA next to
#154's `data-suggestion-original` on the comment body, only when this viewer may apply (AC2, AC5,
AC9; old-side comments already get no attribute, AC7). #154's `web_src/js/markup/suggestion.ts`
then adds the Apply button and commit-message form to the diff header when the comment has
exactly one suggestion block. The server re-checks every condition on POST.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- *Render the button in `repo/diff/comments.tmpl` and `conversation.tmpl`, outside the markup.*
  Works without JavaScript, but the server would need to parse every comment at render time to
  count blocks, and the button would sit apart from the diff it applies, laid out twice.
- *A separate frontend handler that finds #154's rendered diffs.* Keeps #154's file untouched, but
  depends on its generated markup and runs as a second pass over the same comments.

**Rationale:** It follows #154's own design (the server supplies data attributes, the browser
draws the suggestion), covers both tabs with one code path, and re-renders after a comment is
edited (#154 AC8).

**Consequences:** No JavaScript means no button (Out of Scope). Changes to `suggestion.ts` must
keep #154's tests passing, and S4's "applied" marker will probably go in the same header.

### Scope

medium

### Scope Justification

One new service function in `services/repository/files` and a goldmark-based `Comment.SuggestionBlocks()` in
`models/issues`, both with unit tests; one web route and handler with the permission and PR-state
checks; two data attributes in #154's two comment templates; the Apply button and commit-message
form in #154's `suggestion.ts` with Vitest tests; a few locale strings; and integration tests for
the permission and error cases (AC2, AC4–AC6) sharing one PR setup to keep them fast. No schema
change. Recording the applied state is S4.

---
_Revised after the spec review by @controlled-opposition; changes drafted with Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5) for @CarsonRackley._

+// prepareSuggestionApply tells the comment templates whether the viewer may apply suggestions on this pull

+func prepareSuggestionApply(ctx *context.Context, issue *issues_model.Issue) {

+		log.Error("LoadPullRequest: %v", err)
+		return
+	}
+	headCommitID, err := files_service.CanApplySuggestions(ctx, ctx.Doer, issue.PullRequest)
+	if err != nil {
+		if !errors.Is(err, files_service.ErrSuggestionPermission) && !errors.Is(err, files_service.ErrSuggestionPullClosed) {

+		return

+	ctx.Data["SuggestionApplyHeadCommitID"] = headCommitID
+	ctx.Data["SuggestionApplyLink"] = fmt.Sprintf("%s/pulls/%d/files/reviews/comments", ctx.Repo.RepoLink, issue.Index)
+}
+
+// ApplySuggestion commits a review comment's suggestion to the pull request's head branch (#156)
+func ApplySuggestion(ctx *context.Context) {
+	form := web.GetForm(ctx).(*forms.ApplySuggestionForm)
+	issue := GetActionIssue(ctx)
+	if ctx.Written() {
+		return
+	}
+	if !issue.IsPull {
+		ctx.NotFound(nil)
+		return
+	}
+	if ctx.HasError() {
+		ctx.JSONError(ctx.GetErrMsg())
+		return
+	}
+	comment, err := issues_model.GetCommentByID(ctx, ctx.PathParamInt64("id"))
+	if issues_model.IsErrCommentNotExist(err) {
+		ctx.NotFound(err)
+		return
+	} else if err != nil {
+		ctx.ServerError("GetCommentByID", err)
+		return
+	}
+	if err := issue.LoadPullRequest(ctx); err != nil {
+		ctx.ServerError("LoadPullRequest", err)
+		return
+	}
+
+	err = files_service.ApplySuggestion(ctx, ctx.Doer, issue.PullRequest, comment, form.HeadCommitID, form.Message)
+	var errProtected files_service.ErrSuggestionProtectedBranch
+	switch {
+	case err == nil:

+	default:

`````markdown
Closes #156

Part of #151. Builds on #154 (S1, merged in #168).

## What changed

- **Reading suggestions on the server.** `FencedCodeBlocks()` in `modules/markup/markdown/fenced_code.go` walks a comment with Gitea's own goldmark parser. `Comment.SuggestionBlocks()` in `models/issues/comment_suggestion.go` uses it to return the text of each ```` ```suggestion ```` block. The POST never takes the suggestion text from the browser; it reads it from the stored comment (Decision 2).
- **Replacing the line.** `applySuggestionToContent()` in `services/repository/files/suggestion.go` checks that the commented line still matches the line the suggestion was written against, then swaps in the block's lines. It keeps the file's line ending (LF or CRLF) and its final-newline state (AC3, AC10–AC12).
- **Committing it.** `ApplySuggestion()` in the same file checks the PR is open with a head branch, the doer may push (including maintainer edits on a fork PR), the head SHA the page loaded is still the branch head, and the branch protection rule. It then commits through `ChangeRepoFiles` with `LastCommitID` set to that SHA (Decision 1). The commit uses the submitted message or, if empty, "Apply suggestion from @<reviewer> on <file path>". The person who applied it is author and committer, and a `Co-authored-by:` trailer credits the reviewer.
- **Route and handler.** `POST /{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{index}/files/reviews/comments/{id}/apply` (`reqSignIn`) in `routers/web/repo/pull_review.go`. Each refusal returns 400 with its message, the way other web forms do; no push permission returns 403.
- **When the button shows.** `prepareSuggestionApply()` runs for the Files tab, the Conversation tab and a newly posted review comment. It sets the apply URL and the PR's head SHA only for a viewer who may push. The two comment templates then add the `data-suggestion-apply-*` attributes to a non-outdated, new-side comment (Decision 3).
- **Button and form.** `web_src/js/markup/suggestion.ts` adds **Apply suggestion** to #154's diff header when a comment has exactly one suggestion block. Clicking it opens an inline form with the editable default message, **Commit suggestion** and **Cancel**. Success reloads the page; a refusal shows the server's message under the form.
- 7 new locale keys under `repo.diff.suggestion.*` in `locale_en-US.json`. The protected-branch case reuses the web editor's `repo.editor.cannot_commit_to_protected_branch`.

## Why

Reviewers can already write suggestions (#154), but the author still has to retype each one. This lets anyone who can push to the head branch commit a single-line suggestion in one click, safely: it refuses when the code or branch has moved on, and when the viewer has no push permission or the branch is protected (AC1–AC12).

**Not tested automatically, and why:**
- **AC9** has only a manual check. Comments are marked outdated asynchronously after a push (`InvalidateCodeComments`), so an integration test would have to wait on a background queue. The template condition is `not .Invalidated`, the same flag that shows the Outdated label.
- **AC2 fork case** (maintainer edits on/off) is manual only. The permission check is the same `CanMaintainerWriteToBranch` path the web editor uses, and the integration test covers the read-only and signed-out cases.
- **AC3 deleted/renamed file** and **AC5 merged PR, deleted branch, AGit PR** go through the same code paths as the tested cases (file not found at head → outdated; PR not open or no head branch → closed message) but have no test of their own.

**AI-written tests:** All the tests above were written by Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5):
- `TestCommentSuggestionBlocks` in `models/issues/comment_suggestion_test.go` (16 cases)
- `TestApplySuggestionToContent` in `services/repository/files/suggestion_test.go` (18 cases)
- `TestPullReviewApplySuggestion` in `tests/integration/pull_review_suggestion_apply_test.go` (11 subtests)
- 8 new tests in `web_src/js/markup/suggestion.test.ts` (the `applying a suggestion` block)

Expected values come from the ACs, the Open Questions defaults (AC2, AC8) and the web editor's existing message (AC6). Two came from elsewhere. The unclosed-fence case ("x\n") was checked against what Gitea's markdown renderer outputs for the same input. Deleting a last line that has no final newline giving `a` was my decision during review. I checked each assertion against the AC it names.

## Design

Follows the three Design Decisions in #156: `ApplySuggestion` in `services/repository/files` (moved from `services/pull` during the spec review to avoid an import cycle), goldmark-based `Comment.SuggestionBlocks()`, and server-set data attributes that #154's `suggestion.ts` turns into the button. Added during implementation: a POST for a comment that isn't a single new-side suggestion returns 404, since there is no button that could have sent it.

## Tech Debt

**Introduced:**
- `TestPullReviewApplySuggestion` takes about 5s, over the 2s target. The 11 subtests share one repo and PR to keep it down, but each apply is a real git commit and push.
- Right after an apply, comments are invalidated asynchronously, so a page reloaded within a second or two can still show Apply on the applied suggestion. Clicking it then gets the AC3 "outdated" refusal and commits nothing.
- Comments shown in expanded context ("Expand" on the Files tab, the `ExcerptBlob` handler) don't get the Apply button, because that handler doesn't call `prepareSuggestionApply`. Reloading the page shows them normally.

**Encountered:** `conversation.tmpl` is rendered from two handlers with different `ctx.Data` (its existing `FIXME: DIFF-CONVERSATION-DATA`). The apply data therefore has to be set in each handler that renders comments, which is why `ExcerptBlob` is missed above. I left the FIXME as is. `ChangeRepoFiles`'s `LastCommitID` check only catches changes to the same file (`update.go`), so AC4 has its own head-SHA check before calling it (Decision 1).

Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5) helped revise the spec after the review, wrote the implementation and all the tests listed above, ran lint and tests in WSL, and drove the manual browser checks and screenshots with Claude in Chrome. I approved each commit, reviewed every change, and can explain each line. AI log: see the AI Assistance comment on the linked issue.

var (
	// ErrSuggestionNotApplicable means the comment has no suggestion that can be applied: not a new-side code comment
	// on this pull request, or not exactly one suggestion block (#156 AC7)
	ErrSuggestionNotApplicable = errors.New("the comment has no suggestion to apply")

// ApplySuggestion commits the comment's single suggestion to the pull request's head branch, replacing the
// commented line. expectedHeadSHA is the head commit the page showed; message may be empty for the default.
func ApplySuggestion(ctx context.Context, doer *user_model.User, pr *issues_model.PullRequest, comment *issues_model.Comment, expectedHeadSHA, message string) error {
	original := comment.SuggestionOriginalLine()
	if comment.IssueID != pr.IssueID || !original.Has() {
		return ErrSuggestionNotApplicable
	}
	blocks := comment.SuggestionBlocks(ctx)
	if len(blocks) != 1 {
		return ErrSuggestionNotApplicable
	}

	headCommitID, err := CanApplySuggestions(ctx, doer, pr)

31		ErrSuggestionOutdated = errors.New("the suggestion is outdated")
32		// ErrSuggestionNoChange means applying the suggestion would leave the file as it is (#156 AC10)
33		ErrSuggestionNoChange = errors.New("the suggestion makes no changes")
34	)
35	
36	// ErrSuggestionProtectedBranch means branch protection stops the doer from pushing to the head branch (#156 AC6)
37	type ErrSuggestionProtectedBranch struct {
38		Branch string
39	}
40	
41	func (err ErrSuggestionProtectedBranch) Error() string {
42		return fmt.Sprintf("branch %q is protected", err.Branch)
43	}
44	
45	// CanApplySuggestions checks what does not depend on the comment: the pull request is open, has a head branch
46	// (AGit pull requests have none) and the doer can push to it. It returns the head branch's commit ID.
47	func CanApplySuggestions(ctx context.Context, doer *user_model.User, pr *issues_model.PullRequest) (string, error) {
48		if doer == nil {
49			return "", ErrSuggestionPermission
50		}
51		if err := pr.LoadIssue(ctx); err != nil {
52			return "", err
53		}
54		if pr.HasMerged || pr.Issue.IsClosed || pr.Flow != issues_model.PullRequestFlowGithub {
55			return "", ErrSuggestionPullClosed
56		}
57		if err := pr.LoadHeadRepo(ctx); err != nil {
58			return "", err
59		}
60		if pr.HeadRepo == nil {
61			return "", ErrSuggestionPullClosed // the fork was deleted
62		}
63		headPerm, err := access_model.GetDoerRepoPermission(ctx, pr.HeadRepo, doer)
64		if err != nil {
65			return "", err
66		}
67		// includes "Allow edits from maintainers" on fork pull requests
68		if !issues_model.CanMaintainerWriteToBranch(ctx, headPerm, pr.HeadBranch, doer) {
69			return "", ErrSuggestionPermission
70		}
71		headGitRepo, closer, err := gitrepo.RepositoryFromContextOrOpen(ctx, pr.HeadRepo)
72		if err != nil {
73			return "", err
74		}
75		defer closer.Close()
76		headCommitID, err := headGitRepo.GetBranchCommitID(pr.HeadBranch)
77		if git.IsErrNotExist(err) {
78			return "", ErrSuggestionPullClosed // the head branch was deleted
79		}
80		return headCommitID, err
81	}
82	
83	// ApplySuggestion commits the comment's single suggestion to the pull request's head branch, replacing the
84	// commented line. expectedHeadSHA is the head commit the page showed; message may be empty for the default.
85	func ApplySuggestion(ctx context.Context, doer *user_model.User, pr *issues_model.PullRequest, comment *issues_model.Comment, expectedHeadSHA, message string) error {
86		original := comment.SuggestionOriginalLine()
87		if comment.IssueID != pr.IssueID || !original.Has() {
88			return ErrSuggestionNotApplicable
89		}
90		blocks := comment.SuggestionBlocks(ctx)
91		if len(blocks) != 1 {
92			return ErrSuggestionNotApplicable
93		}
94	
95		headCommitID, err := CanApplySuggestions(ctx, doer, pr)
96		if err != nil {
97			return err
98		}
99		if headCommitID != expectedHeadSHA {
100			return ErrSuggestionHeadMoved
101		}
102	
103		// the web editor's check, so the user gets our message rather than the pre-receive hook's output
104		protectedBranch, err := git_model.GetFirstMatchProtectedBranchRule(ctx, pr.HeadRepo.ID, pr.HeadBranch)
105		if err != nil {
106			return err
107		}
108		if protectedBranch != nil {
109			protectedBranch.Repo = pr.HeadRepo
110			canPush := protectedBranch.CanUserPush(ctx, doer)
111			if !canPush && protectedBranch.UnprotectedFilePatterns != "" {
112				canPush = protectedBranch.IsUnprotectedFile(protectedBranch.GetUnprotectedFilePatterns(), comment.TreePath)
113			}
114			if !canPush {
115				return ErrSuggestionProtectedBranch{Branch: pr.HeadBranch}
116			}
117		}
118	
119		headGitRepo, closer, err := gitrepo.RepositoryFromContextOrOpen(ctx, pr.HeadRepo)
120		if err != nil {
121			return err
122		}
123		defer closer.Close()
124		headCommit, err := headGitRepo.GetCommit(headCommitID)
125		if err != nil {
126			return err
127		}
128		blob, err := headCommit.GetBlobByPath(comment.TreePath)
129		if git.IsErrNotExist(err) {
130			return ErrSuggestionOutdated // deleted or renamed since the review
131		} else if err != nil {
132			return err
133		}
134		content, err := blob.GetBlobContent(blob.Size())
135		if err != nil {
136			return err
137		}
138		newContent, err := applySuggestionToContent(content, int(comment.Line), original.Value(), blocks[0])
139		if err != nil {
140			return err
141		}
142	
143		if err := comment.LoadPoster(ctx); err != nil {
144			return err
145		}
146		if strings.TrimSpace(message) == "" {
147			message = comment.SuggestionCommitMessage()
148		}
149		// customer question 1 on #151 is open; the spec's default: the doer authors and commits, the reviewer is credited
150		if comment.Poster.ID != doer.ID {
151			sig := comment.Poster.NewGitSig()
152			message = fmt.Sprintf("%s\n\n%s: %s <%s>", strings.TrimRight(message, "\n"), git.CoAuthoredByTrailer, sig.Name, sig.Email)
153		}
154	
155		_, err = ChangeRepoFiles(ctx, pr.HeadRepo, doer, &ChangeRepoFilesOptions{
156			LastCommitID: expectedHeadSHA,
157			OldBranch:    pr.HeadBranch,
158			NewBranch:    pr.HeadBranch,
159			Message:      message,
160			Files: []*ChangeRepoFile{{
161				Operation:     "update",
162				TreePath:      comment.TreePath,
163				FromTreePath:  comment.TreePath,
164				ContentReader: strings.NewReader(newContent),
165			}},
166		})
167		if IsErrCommitIDDoesNotMatch(err) {
168			return ErrSuggestionHeadMoved // someone pushed between our check and the commit
169		}
170		return err
171	}
172	
173	// applySuggestionToContent replaces line lineNum (1-based) of content with the suggestion's lines, the way
174	// #154 draws the diff: "" deletes the line, "\n" leaves one blank line, otherwise one line per suggestion line.
175	// original is the line the suggestion was written against; content and original may use CRLF.
176	func applySuggestionToContent(content string, lineNum int, original, suggestion string) (string, error) {
177		lines := strings.SplitAfter(content, "\n") // every element but the last keeps its "\n"
178		if lines[len(lines)-1] == "" {
179			lines = lines[:len(lines)-1] // content ended with a newline
180		}
181		idx := lineNum - 1
182		if idx < 0 || idx >= len(lines) {
183			return "", ErrSuggestionOutdated
184		}
185	
186		target := lines[idx]
187		ending := ""
188		switch {
189		case strings.HasSuffix(target, "\r\n"):
190			ending = "\r\n"
191		case strings.HasSuffix(target, "\n"):
192			ending = "\n"
193		}
194		if strings.TrimSuffix(target, ending) != strings.TrimSuffix(original, "\r") {
195			return "", ErrSuggestionOutdated
196		}
197	
198		var replacement string
199		if suggestion != "" {
200			innerEnding := ending
201			if innerEnding == "" { // the last line has no newline, so new lines in between take the file's own
202				innerEnding = "\n"
203				if strings.Contains(content, "\r\n") {
204					innerEnding = "\r\n"
205				}
206			}
207			newLines := strings.Split(strings.TrimSuffix(suggestion, "\n"), "\n")
208			replacement = strings.Join(newLines, innerEnding) + ending
209		}
210	
211		before := strings.Join(lines[:idx], "")
212		if replacement == "" && ending == "" && idx > 0 {
213			// deleting a last line that has no newline: the line before it becomes last and loses its newline,
214			// so the file still ends without one (#156 AC11)
215			prev := lines[idx-1]
216			before = strings.Join(lines[:idx-1], "") + strings.TrimSuffix(strings.TrimSuffix(prev, "\n"), "\r")
217		}
218		result := before + replacement + strings.Join(lines[idx+1:], "")
219		if result == content {
220			return "", ErrSuggestionNoChange
221		}
222		return result, nil
223	}
224

// Copyright 2026 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

package issues

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"strings"

	"gitea.dev/modules/markup/markdown"
	"gitea.dev/modules/optional"
)

// SuggestionOriginalLine returns the commented line as the reviewer saw it: the last line of the
// stored patch, since CutDiffAroundLine stops right after the commented line.
// Old-side comments return None until #151 decides whether they may carry suggestions.
func (c *Comment) SuggestionOriginalLine() optional.Option[string] {
	if c.Type != CommentTypeCode || c.Line <= 0 {
		return optional.None[string]()
	}
	patch := strings.TrimRight(c.Patch, "\n")
	last := patch[strings.LastIndexByte(patch, '\n')+1:]
	if last == "" || (last[0] != '+' && last[0] != ' ') {
		return optional.None[string]() // "-" is the other side; "@", "d", "\\" mean no code line
	}
	return optional.Some(last[1:])
}

// SuggestionBlocks returns the text of each ```suggestion block in the comment, found the way the
// rendered page finds them (#154 AC9). An empty block is "", one blank line is "\n".
func (c *Comment) SuggestionBlocks(ctx context.Context) []string {
	return markdown.FencedCodeBlocks(ctx, []byte(c.Content), "suggestion")
}

// SuggestionCommitMessage is the default message for committing the comment's suggestion (#156 AC1).
// The poster must be loaded.
func (c *Comment) SuggestionCommitMessage() string {
	return fmt.Sprintf("Apply suggestion from @%s on %s", c.Poster.Name, c.TreePath)
}

// Copyright 2026 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

package markdown

import (
	"context"
	"strings"

	"gitea.dev/modules/markup"
	giteautil "gitea.dev/modules/util"

	"github.com/yuin/goldmark/ast"
	"github.com/yuin/goldmark/parser"
	"github.com/yuin/goldmark/text"
)

// FencedCodeBlocks returns the text of each fenced code block whose language is lang. It parses the
// source the way render does, so callers find exactly the blocks the rendered page shows.
func FencedCodeBlocks(ctx context.Context, source []byte, lang string) []string {
	rctx := markup.NewRenderContext(ctx)
	buf := giteautil.NormalizeEOL(source)
	rc := &RenderConfig{Meta: markup.RenderMetaAsDetails}
	buf, _ = ExtractMetadataBytes(buf, rc) // front matter is not part of the rendered body
	pc := newParserContext(rctx)
	pc.Set(renderConfigKey, rc)
	doc := SpecializedMarkdown(rctx).goldmarkMarkdown.Parser().Parse(text.NewReader(buf), parser.WithContext(pc))

	var blocks []string
	_ = ast.Walk(doc, func(n ast.Node, entering bool) (ast.WalkStatus, error) {
		code, ok := n.(*ast.FencedCodeBlock)
		if !entering || !ok {
			return ast.WalkContinue, nil
		}
		// the AST transformer has already cut the info string at its first space, comma or colon
		if string(code.Language(buf)) == lang {
			var sb strings.Builder
			for i := range code.Lines().Len() {
				seg := code.Lines().At(i)
				sb.Write(seg.Value(buf)) // Value keeps the indentation a list or quote leaves inside the block
			}
			blocks = append(blocks, sb.String())
		}
		return ast.WalkSkipChildren, nil
	})
	return blocks
}

func testNewLabel(t *testing.T) {

func testNewLabelInvalidColor(t *testing.T) {

func (l MockLocale) TrString(format string, args ...any) (ret string) {
	ret = format + ":"
	for _, arg := range args {
		// usually there is no arg or at most 1-2 args, so a simple string concatenation is more efficient
		switch v := arg.(type) {
		case string:
			ret += v + ","
		default:
			ret += fmt.Sprint(v) + ","
		}
	}
	return ret[:len(ret)-1]
}

func (l MockLocale) Tr(format string, args ...any) (ret template.HTML) {
	ret = template.HTML(html.EscapeString(format)) + ":"
	for _, arg := range args {
		// usually there is no arg or at most 1-2 args, so a simple string concatenation is more efficient
		switch v := arg.(type) {
		case template.HTML:
			ret += v + ","
		case string:
			ret += template.HTML(html.EscapeString(v)) + ","
		default:
			ret += template.HTML(html.EscapeString(fmt.Sprint(v))) + ","
		}
	}
	return ret[:len(ret)-1]

// LoadRepo load a repo into a test context.
func LoadRepo(t *testing.T, ctx gocontext.Context, repoID int64) {
	var doer *user_model.User
	var repo *context.Repository
	switch ctx := ctx.(type) {
	case *context.Context:
		repo = ctx.Repo
		doer = ctx.Doer
	case *context.APIContext:
		repo = ctx.Repo
		doer = ctx.Doer
	default:
		assert.FailNow(t, "context is not *context.Context or *context.APIContext")
	}

	repo.Repository = unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &repo_model.Repository{ID: repoID})
	var err error
	repo.Owner, err = user_model.GetUserByID(ctx, repo.Repository.OwnerID)
	assert.NoError(t, err)
	repo.RepoLink = repo.Repository.Link()
	repo.Permission, err = access_model.GetDoerRepoPermission(ctx, repo.Repository, doer)
	assert.NoError(t, err)
}

// LoadRepoCommit loads a repo's commit into a test context.
func LoadRepoCommit(t *testing.T, ctx gocontext.Context) {
	var repo *context.Repository
	switch ctx := ctx.(type) {
	case *context.Context:
		repo = ctx.Repo
	case *context.APIContext:
		repo = ctx.Repo
	default:
		assert.FailNow(t, "context is not *context.Context or *context.APIContext")
	}

	gitRepo, err := gitrepo.OpenRepository(ctx, repo.Repository)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	t.Cleanup(func() {
		gitRepo.Close()
	})
	if repo.RefFullName == "" {
		repo.RefFullName = git_module.RefNameFromBranch(repo.Repository.DefaultBranch)
	}
	if repo.RefFullName.IsPull() {
		repo.BranchName = repo.RefFullName.ShortName()
	}
	repo.Commit, err = gitRepo.GetCommit(repo.RefFullName.String())
	require.NoError(t, err)
}

// LoadUser load a user into a test context
func LoadUser(t *testing.T, ctx gocontext.Context, userID int64) {
	doer := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &user_model.User{ID: userID})
	switch ctx := ctx.(type) {
	case *context.Context:
		ctx.Doer = doer
		ctx.IsSigned = true
	case *context.APIContext:
		ctx.Doer = doer
		ctx.IsSigned = true
	default:
		assert.FailNow(t, "context is not *context.Context or *context.APIContext")
	}
}

func TestFencedCodeBlocks(t *testing.T) {
	cases := []struct {
		name     string
		source   string
		lang     string
		expected []string
	}{

		{"an indented code block has no language", "    x := 1\n", "go", nil},
		{"two backticks are not a fence", "``go\nx\n``", "go", nil},
		{"a fence inside a longer fence is content", "````md\n```go\nx\n```\n````", "go", nil},
	}
	for _, c := range cases {
		t.Run(c.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			assert.Equal(t, c.expected, markdown.FencedCodeBlocks(t.Context(), []byte(c.source), c.lang))
		})
	}
}

// The checks before the commit (#156), against fixture pull request 2: user2/repo1, head branch2, whose README.md
// has "And change for branch2" on line 5. The commit itself needs git hooks, so it is in the integration test.
func TestApplySuggestion(t *testing.T) {
	unittest.PrepareTestEnv(t)
	const branch2Head = "985f0301dba5e7b34be866819cd15ad3d8f508ee" // tests/gitea-repositories-meta/user2/repo1.git
	const masterHead = "65f1bf27bc3bf70f64657658635e66094edbcb4d"
	repo := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &repo_model.Repository{ID: 1})
	owner := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &user_model.User{ID: 2})  // owns repo1
	reader := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &user_model.User{ID: 4}) // cannot push to repo1
	loadPR := func(t *testing.T, id int64) *issues_model.PullRequest {
		pr := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.PullRequest{ID: id})
		require.NoError(t, pr.LoadIssue(t.Context()))
		return pr
	}
	suggest := func(pr *issues_model.PullRequest, treePath, original, content string) *issues_model.Comment {
		return &issues_model.Comment{
			Type: issues_model.CommentTypeCode, IssueID: pr.IssueID, PosterID: 4, TreePath: treePath, Line: 5,
			Patch: "@@ -4,1 +4,2 @@\n \n+" + original, Content: content,
		}
	}
	const fix = "```suggestion\nAnd a change for branch2\n```"

	t.Run("AC1 someone who can push gets the head branch's commit", func(t *testing.T) {
		head, err := CanApplySuggestions(t.Context(), owner, loadPR(t, 2))
		require.NoError(t, err)
		assert.Equal(t, branch2Head, head)
	})

	cannotApply := []struct {
		name   string
		doer   *user_model.User
		change func(pr *issues_model.PullRequest)
		err    error
	}{
		{"AC2 signed out", nil, nil, ErrSuggestionPermission},
		{"AC2 cannot push", reader, nil, ErrSuggestionPermission},
		{"AC5 closed", owner, func(pr *issues_model.PullRequest) { pr.Issue.IsClosed = true }, ErrSuggestionPullClosed},
		{"AC5 merged", owner, func(pr *issues_model.PullRequest) { pr.HasMerged = true }, ErrSuggestionPullClosed},
		{"AC5 AGit flow", owner, func(pr *issues_model.PullRequest) { pr.Flow = issues_model.PullRequestFlowAGit }, ErrSuggestionPullClosed},
		{"AC5 head branch deleted", owner, func(pr *issues_model.PullRequest) { pr.HeadBranch = "deleted-branch" }, ErrSuggestionPullClosed},
	}
	for _, c := range cannotApply {
		t.Run(c.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			pr := loadPR(t, 2)
			if c.change != nil {
				c.change(pr)
			}
			_, err := CanApplySuggestions(t.Context(), c.doer, pr)
			assert.ErrorIs(t, err, c.err)
			// ApplySuggestion makes the same check before anything else that touches the branch
			assert.ErrorIs(t, ApplySuggestion(t.Context(), c.doer, pr, suggest(pr, "README.md", "And change for branch2", fix), branch2Head, ""), c.err)
		})
	}

	refused := []struct {
		name    string
		comment func(pr *issues_model.PullRequest) *issues_model.Comment
		head    string
		err     error
	}{
		{"AC7 a comment from another pull request", func(pr *issues_model.PullRequest) *issues_model.Comment {
			c := suggest(pr, "README.md", "And change for branch2", fix)
			c.IssueID = 2
			return c
		}, branch2Head, ErrSuggestionNotApplicable},
		{"AC7 an old-side comment", func(pr *issues_model.PullRequest) *issues_model.Comment {
			c := suggest(pr, "README.md", "And change for branch2", fix)
			c.Line = -5
			return c
		}, branch2Head, ErrSuggestionNotApplicable},
		{"AC7 no suggestion block", func(pr *issues_model.PullRequest) *issues_model.Comment {
			return suggest(pr, "README.md", "And change for branch2", "looks good")
		}, branch2Head, ErrSuggestionNotApplicable},
		{"AC7 two suggestion blocks", func(pr *issues_model.PullRequest) *issues_model.Comment {
			return suggest(pr, "README.md", "And change for branch2", fix+"\nor\n"+fix)
		}, branch2Head, ErrSuggestionNotApplicable},
		{"AC4 the page showed an older head", func(pr *issues_model.PullRequest) *issues_model.Comment {
			return suggest(pr, "README.md", "And change for branch2", fix)
		}, masterHead, ErrSuggestionHeadMoved},
		{"AC3 the file was deleted or renamed", func(pr *issues_model.PullRequest) *issues_model.Comment {
			return suggest(pr, "gone.md", "And change for branch2", fix)
		}, branch2Head, ErrSuggestionOutdated},
		{"AC3 the line changed", func(pr *issues_model.PullRequest) *issues_model.Comment {
			return suggest(pr, "README.md", "And an older change for branch2", fix)
		}, branch2Head, ErrSuggestionOutdated},
		{"AC10 the suggestion is the line as it is", func(pr *issues_model.PullRequest) *issues_model.Comment {
			return suggest(pr, "README.md", "And change for branch2", "```suggestion\nAnd change for branch2\n```")
		}, branch2Head, ErrSuggestionNoChange},
	}
	for _, c := range refused {
		t.Run(c.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			pr := loadPR(t, 2)
			assert.ErrorIs(t, ApplySuggestion(t.Context(), owner, pr, c.comment(pr), c.head, ""), c.err)
		})
	}

	t.Run("AC6 a protected branch", func(t *testing.T) {
		rule := &git_model.ProtectedBranch{RepoID: repo.ID, RuleName: "branch2", CanPush: false}
		require.NoError(t, git_model.UpdateProtectBranch(t.Context(), repo, rule, git_model.WhitelistOptions{}))
		defer func() { require.NoError(t, git_model.DeleteProtectedBranch(t.Context(), repo, rule.ID)) }()

		pr := loadPR(t, 2)
		err := ApplySuggestion(t.Context(), owner, pr, suggest(pr, "README.md", "And change for branch2", fix), branch2Head, "")
		var errProtected ErrSuggestionProtectedBranch
		require.ErrorAs(t, err, &errProtected)
		assert.Equal(t, "branch2", errProtected.Branch)

		// like the web editor, a file matching the rule's unprotected patterns may still be changed,
		// so this one gets past protection and stops at its outdated line instead
		rule.UnprotectedFilePatterns = "README.md"
		require.NoError(t, git_model.UpdateProtectBranch(t.Context(), repo, rule, git_model.WhitelistOptions{}))
		err = ApplySuggestion(t.Context(), owner, pr, suggest(pr, "README.md", "And an older change for branch2", fix), branch2Head, "")
		assert.ErrorIs(t, err, ErrSuggestionOutdated)
	})
}

// Copyright 2026 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

package repo

import (
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"
	"strconv"
	"testing"

	"gitea.dev/models/db"
	git_model "gitea.dev/models/git"
	issues_model "gitea.dev/models/issues"
	repo_model "gitea.dev/models/repo"
	"gitea.dev/models/unittest"
	"gitea.dev/modules/test"
	"gitea.dev/modules/web"
	"gitea.dev/services/context"
	"gitea.dev/services/contexttest"
	"gitea.dev/services/forms"

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

// The Apply POST's responses (#156), against fixture pull request 2: user2/repo1 #3, head branch2, whose
// README.md has "And change for branch2" on line 5. The mock locale returns message keys, not their text.
func TestApplySuggestion(t *testing.T) {
	unittest.PrepareTestEnv(t)
	const branch2Head = "985f0301dba5e7b34be866819cd15ad3d8f508ee" // tests/gitea-repositories-meta/user2/repo1.git
	const masterHead = "65f1bf27bc3bf70f64657658635e66094edbcb4d"
	repo := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &repo_model.Repository{ID: 1})
	comment := func(t *testing.T, original, content string) int64 {
		c := &issues_model.Comment{
			Type: issues_model.CommentTypeCode, IssueID: 3, PosterID: 4, TreePath: "README.md", Line: 5,
			Patch: "@@ -4,1 +4,2 @@\n \n+" + original, Content: content,
		}
		require.NoError(t, db.Insert(t.Context(), c))
		return c.ID
	}
	fix := comment(t, "And change for branch2", "```suggestion\nAnd a change for branch2\n```")

	apply := func(t *testing.T, doerID, index, commentID int64, head string) (*context.Context, *httptest.ResponseRecorder) {
		ctx, resp := contexttest.MockContext(t, "user2/repo1/pulls/3/files/reviews/comments/apply")
		contexttest.LoadUser(t, ctx, doerID)
		contexttest.LoadRepo(t, ctx, repo.ID)
		ctx.SetPathParam("index", strconv.FormatInt(index, 10))
		ctx.SetPathParam("id", strconv.FormatInt(commentID, 10))
		web.SetForm(ctx, &forms.ApplySuggestionForm{HeadCommitID: head})
		ApplySuggestion(ctx)
		return ctx, resp
	}
	refused := func(t *testing.T, resp *httptest.ResponseRecorder, ctx *context.Context, message string) {
		assert.Equal(t, http.StatusBadRequest, ctx.Resp.WrittenStatus())
		assert.Equal(t, message, test.ParseJSONError(resp.Body.Bytes()).ErrorMessage)
	}

	t.Run("AC1 the page gets the head commit and the apply link for someone who can push", func(t *testing.T) {
		ctx, _ := contexttest.MockContext(t, "user2/repo1/pulls/3/files")
		contexttest.LoadUser(t, ctx, 2)
		contexttest.LoadRepo(t, ctx, repo.ID)
		issue := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Issue{ID: 3})
		prepareSuggestionApply(ctx, issue)
		assert.Equal(t, branch2Head, ctx.Data["SuggestionApplyHeadCommitID"])
		assert.Equal(t, "/user2/repo1/pulls/3/files/reviews/comments", ctx.Data["SuggestionApplyLink"])
	})

	t.Run("AC2 the page gets nothing for someone who cannot push", func(t *testing.T) {
		ctx, _ := contexttest.MockContext(t, "user2/repo1/pulls/3/files")
		contexttest.LoadUser(t, ctx, 4)
		contexttest.LoadRepo(t, ctx, repo.ID)
		prepareSuggestionApply(ctx, unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Issue{ID: 3}))
		assert.NotContains(t, ctx.Data, "SuggestionApplyHeadCommitID")
	})

	t.Run("AC2 someone who cannot push gets a 403", func(t *testing.T) {
		ctx, _ := apply(t, 4, 3, fix, branch2Head)
		assert.Equal(t, http.StatusForbidden, ctx.Resp.WrittenStatus())
	})

	t.Run("an issue that is not a pull request is not found", func(t *testing.T) {
		ctx, _ := apply(t, 2, 1, fix, branch2Head) // repo1 #1 is an issue
		assert.Equal(t, http.StatusNotFound, ctx.Resp.WrittenStatus())
	})

	t.Run("a comment that does not exist is not found", func(t *testing.T) {
		ctx, _ := apply(t, 2, 3, 999999, branch2Head)
		assert.Equal(t, http.StatusNotFound, ctx.Resp.WrittenStatus())
	})

	t.Run("AC7 a comment with two suggestion blocks is not found", func(t *testing.T) {
		twoBlocks := comment(t, "And change for branch2", "```suggestion\na\n```\nor\n```suggestion\nb\n```")
		ctx, _ := apply(t, 2, 3, twoBlocks, branch2Head)
		assert.Equal(t, http.StatusNotFound, ctx.Resp.WrittenStatus())
	})

	t.Run("AC4 the head moved", func(t *testing.T) {
		ctx, resp := apply(t, 2, 3, fix, masterHead)
		refused(t, resp, ctx, "repo.diff.suggestion.head_moved")
	})

	t.Run("AC3 the line changed", func(t *testing.T) {
		outdated := comment(t, "And an older change for branch2", "```suggestion\nAnd a change for branch2\n```")
		ctx, resp := apply(t, 2, 3, outdated, branch2Head)
		refused(t, resp, ctx, "repo.diff.suggestion.outdated")
	})

	t.Run("AC10 the suggestion changes nothing", func(t *testing.T) {
		same := comment(t, "And change for branch2", "```suggestion\nAnd change for branch2\n```")
		ctx, resp := apply(t, 2, 3, same, branch2Head)
		refused(t, resp, ctx, "repo.diff.suggestion.no_change")
	})

	t.Run("AC6 a protected branch gets the web editor's message", func(t *testing.T) {
		rule := &git_model.ProtectedBranch{RepoID: repo.ID, RuleName: "branch2", CanPush: false}
		require.NoError(t, git_model.UpdateProtectBranch(t.Context(), repo, rule, git_model.WhitelistOptions{}))
		defer func() { require.NoError(t, git_model.DeleteProtectedBranch(t.Context(), repo, rule.ID)) }()
		ctx, resp := apply(t, 2, 3, fix, branch2Head)
		refused(t, resp, ctx, "repo.editor.cannot_commit_to_protected_branch:branch2")
	})

	t.Run("AC5 a closed pull request", func(t *testing.T) {
		_, err := db.GetEngine(t.Context()).ID(3).Cols("is_closed").Update(&issues_model.Issue{IsClosed: true})
		require.NoError(t, err)
		ctx, resp := apply(t, 2, 3, fix, branch2Head)
		refused(t, resp, ctx, "repo.diff.suggestion.pull_closed")
	})
}

Carson's setup (2026-09-14): **all code edits happen in this Windows `Gitea` folder** (logged
SpecStory sessions launch here). WSL Debian `~/gitea` is a **test runner only** — never edit there.
Native Windows test runs produce Windows-only failures, and lint is ~20x slower, so don't trust them.

**Run tests/lint/build with `wsync` from the Bash tool (Git Bash):**
```bash
wsync pnpm exec vitest run web_src/js/features/common-page.test.ts
wsync go test -run '^TestName$' ./routers/web/misc/
wsync make lint-js
wsync make build
wsync            # sync only
```
`C:\Users\carso\bin\wsync` reads the branch checked out here, warns if tracked files are
uncommitted (only COMMITTED work reaches WSL — commit first, ask Carson before committing), then
runs WSL `~/bin/wsync-wsl <branch> [cmd]`: fetches remote `win` (this folder over /mnt/c;
push disabled), force-switches `~/gitea` to that branch, runs the command with Go 1.26.4/Node PATH.

Gotchas: don't run `git status` on `/mnt/c` from WSL (hangs); WSL can't run `.exe`s; use
`wsl -d Debian --exec bash -c '...' name args` (plain `wsl -- bash -c` drops args).
To try the app: `~/gitea/custom/conf/app.ini` serves Gitea on http://localhost:3001 (SQLite) —
run `wsl -d Debian --exec bash -c 'cd ~/gitea && ./gitea web'` in the background after `wsync make build`.
Baseline rule: some backend tests fail on `main` too — compare branch vs `main`, not vs zero.
wsync is /c/Users/carso/bin/wsync

## Tech Debt

**Introduced:**
- `TestPullReviewApplySuggestion` takes about 5s, over the 2s target. The 11 subtests share one repo and PR to keep it down, but each apply is a real git commit and push.
- Right after an apply, comments are invalidated asynchronously, so a page reloaded within a second or two can still show Apply on the applied suggestion. Clicking it then gets the AC3 "outdated" refusal and commits nothing.
- Comments shown in expanded context ("Expand" on the Files tab, the `ExcerptBlob` handler) don't get the Apply button, because that handler doesn't call `prepareSuggestionApply`. Reloading the page shows them normally.

**Encountered:** `conversation.tmpl` is rendered from two handlers with different `ctx.Data` (its existing `FIXME: DIFF-CONVERSATION-DATA`). The apply data therefore has to be set in each handler that renders comments, which is why `ExcerptBlob` is missed above. I left the FIXME as is. `ChangeRepoFiles`'s `LastCommitID` check only catches changes to the same file (`update.go`), so AC4 has its own head-SHA check before calling it (Decision 1).

```text
# AI Logs

This folder holds every AI session for each sprint, one folder per student. The course rules are on
the [AI Log Instructions](https://csci-435-se.github.io/ai-logs/) page and the current sprint page
at <https://csci-435-se.github.io/>. This README is the team's shared convention for following them.

## What to log

Every AI session tied to this project: code, debugging, tests, reviews, drafting issues and PRs,
design discussion, the sprint report. That includes sessions that went nowhere. Purely academic
questions unrelated to the project don't need logging.

## Structure

```
ai-logs/
  sprint<N>/
    <github-username>/                          ← exact GitHub username, matching case
      .gitkeep                                  ← the folder must exist even if you used no AI
      YYYY-MM-DD_<tool>_<short-slug>.md
      YYYY-MM-DD_<tool>_<short-slug>/           ← attachments (images, etc.), optional
```

Team folders: `ab-wm`, `arjunsb26`, `CarsonRackley`, `controlled-opposition`, `Jack-Donohue`,
`vvchopra`.

## Naming

`YYYY-MM-DD_<tool>_<short-slug>.md`

- **Date:** the day the session started.
- **Sprint folder:** the sprint that date falls in, not the sprint the work is for.
- **Tool:** one of the course identifiers: `claude-code`, `claude-web`, `claude-desktop`, `cursor`,
  `gemini-cli`, `codex-cli`, `copilot`, `chatgpt`, `other-<name>`. Claude Code run inside VS Code is
  `claude-code`.
- **Slug:** lowercase words joined with hyphens that say what the session did. Put the issue number
  first when there is one: `issue-52-impl`, `issue-52-spec`, `pr-61-review`, `sprint1-report`.
  Replace auto-generated slugs such as `local-command-caveat...`.
- **Formats:** `.md` is preferred; `.txt` and `.json` are also accepted. No `.docx`, `.pdf`, `.html`
  or share links.

## Capturing a session

| Tool | How |
| --- | --- |
| Claude Code (terminal or VS Code), other agentic CLIs | Start it with [SpecStory](https://specstory.com/): `specstory run claude`, from the repo root. Forgot? Run `specstory sync` afterwards; it back-fills from Claude Code's local history. Then copy from `.specstory/history/` (git-ignored) into your folder and rename it to the convention. |
| Web chat (claude.ai, ChatGPT, Gemini, ...) | Install a browser chat exporter and export the session as Markdown right after it ends. Include any files you pasted in as context. |
| Claude Desktop | SpecStory doesn't capture it. Copy the conversation into a `.md` file by hand. |

At the end of each sprint, run `specstory sync` once more and re-copy. A log copied mid-session is
incomplete.

## Content

- The **tool and AI model** used (SpecStory writes both).
- The **complete** prompt and response history. For agentic tools, that includes file edits and
  commands (SpecStory includes them). Logs with missing responses or truncated histories are
  **invalid**. Don't hand-write, summarise or trim a log; only rename it.
- These are **not** logs and get no full credit: a summary of a session, paraphrased prompts, a
  share link to a chat, or tool output without the prompts that produced it (Sprint 3 page).
- Attachments (screenshots, snippets) go in a folder with the log's name minus `.md`.
- Log **every** session, including ones that went nowhere. Grading is on how complete the record
  is, not on whether AI helped.

## Where logs are referenced

- **Issue comments only.** Each contributor posts their own `### AI Assistance — @username` comment
  on the issue, with full `https://github.com/...` links to their logs. Format:
  [`.claude-students/AI-ASSISTANCE.md`](../.claude-students/AI-ASSISTANCE.md).
- **Not** in PR descriptions or PR comments. The PR has a short AI-use note with no log link. The
  AI Log Instructions page says "Issue/PR comments" and the Sprint 3 page "the issue or PR", but
  the Sprint 1 page narrows it to issue comments only; the team keeps that rule, which satisfies
  all three.
- Each teammate posts their own comment, including reviewers who used AI to review.
- No AI used? Post an issue comment saying so, and keep your folder with its `.gitkeep`.
- The sprint report lists each member's tools, session count, folder link, and 2–3 sentences on
  lessons learned.

---

For [[csci-435-gitea-project]], AI logs must be **captured by SpecStory**, not hand-written. Spec:
`https://csci-435-se.github.io/ai-logs/` (the repo's `ai-logs/README.md` link is dead).

**Installed 2026-09-03:** SpecStory CLI v2.10.0 at `C:\Users\carso\.local\bin\specstory.exe`
(single binary from the GitHub releases zip; that folder was already on the user PATH because
`claude.exe` lives there, so no PATH edit was needed). No brew on Windows - manual zip install.

**The habit: launch as `specstory run claude`, not `claude`** - and start it from inside the `Gitea`
folder so `.specstory/history/` lands in the repo (required: only Gitea-folder sessions get logged, see [[gitea-ai-log-scope]]).
`.specstory/` is excluded via `Gitea/.git/info/exclude`, deliberately NOT the tracked `.gitignore`,
to keep upstream files out of PR diffs.

**Forgot to wrap a session? `specstory sync` back-fills it** from Claude Code's own local history
(`~/.claude/projects/<slug>/*.jsonl`) - this recovered the 2026-09-02 toolchain session in full.
Sync is also safe mid-session to pick up turns so far.

**Filing rules:** copy from `.specstory/history/` to `ai-logs/sprint<N>/<github-username>/` as
`YYYY-MM-DD_claude-code_<slug>.md`; the site says to fix auto-generated slugs so they describe the
session. `.md`/`.txt`/`.json` only - no `.docx`/`.pdf`/`.html`. Log unproductive sessions too;
grading is on completeness of documentation, not on whether AI helped. Share links do not count.

**Also required per issue:** each contributor posts their own `### AI Assistance - @username`
**issue** comment with a Role line and a `# | Tool | Log | What AI helped with` table (full
https://github.com links, relative paths break) - and must post it saying "No AI used" even when no
AI was used. **Sprint 1 rule: log links go in issue comments ONLY, never PR descriptions/comments**;
the PR gets a short AI-use note with no link. Slugs lead with the issue number (`issue-52-impl`,
`pr-61-review`). Team convention in repo `ai-logs/README.md`.

**Other tools (site, re-read 2026-09-24):** web chats are exported as Markdown with a browser
exporter right after the session (include pasted context files); Claude Desktop isn't captured by
SpecStory and must be copied by hand. Truncated logs or missing responses are invalid. Full team
convention is in the repo's `ai-logs/README.md`.

**How to apply:** re-run `specstory sync` and re-copy before each sprint deadline (Sprint 1: Oct 8 11:59 PM); logs copied
earlier are snapshots of in-progress sessions and will be incomplete.
